usage_note: 常用 play cribbage；传统上在板上移动小钉计分，它仍是纸牌游戏，不是以棋子走格的棋类。

senses.english_definition: Cribbage is a card game in which players score points for particular combinations of cards and usually record their scores with pegs on a board.
senses.collocation_en: play cribbage; a cribbage board

etymology_story.zh: cribbage 在17世纪已有记载，由 crib 与后缀 -age 构成。在这种游戏中，crib 指双方各弃出部分牌后组成、由庄家额外计分的一手牌。
etymology_story.en: Recorded in the seventeenth century, cribbage was formed from crib and the suffix -age. In the game, the crib is an extra hand assembled from cards discarded by the players and scored by the dealer.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：crib（游戏中的额外一手牌）+ -age（构成名词）→ cribbage，拼写中双写 b。cribbage 通常为不可数名词，没有常用的进一步派生词；相关表达有 cribbage board（计分板）和 cribbage player（玩家），其中 cribbage 作名词定语，并非独立的形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: crib, the extra hand in the game, + the noun-forming suffix -age → cribbage, with a doubled b. Cribbage is normally uncountable and has no common further derivatives; related expressions include cribbage board and cribbage player, where cribbage is an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用的严格近义词。card game（纸牌游戏）是上位词；whist（惠斯特牌戏）和 bridge（桥牌）是不同的纸牌游戏，主要围绕赢墩展开，不能替换 cribbage。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no standard exact synonym. Card game is the broader category; whist and bridge are different card games organized mainly around winning tricks and cannot replace cribbage.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 crib“额外一手牌”：多算一手牌，再用插钉记分。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the name to the crib: an extra hand to score, with pegs tracking the points.

usage_note: 英语重音诗中是一重两轻；古典诗律按一长两短计算。本课用英语重音模式理解。

senses.meaning_zh: 扬抑抑格音步；古典格律中由一长两短音节组成的音步
senses.meaning_en: a metrical foot consisting of one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed syllables, or one long followed by two short syllables
senses.english_definition: A dactyl is a group of three syllables in poetry, with the first stressed and the next two unstressed, or, in classical verse, the first long and the next two short.
senses.collocation_en: a metrical dactyl; a line of dactyls
senses.collocation_zh: 一个扬抑抑格音步；一行由扬抑抑格音步组成的诗
senses.sentence_en: The word 'merrily' can illustrate a dactyl because its first syllable is stressed and the next two are unstressed.
senses.sentence_zh: merrily 一词可以用来说明扬抑抑格，因为它的第一个音节重读，后两个音节轻读。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语 dactylus 源自希腊语 daktylos，原义为“手指”。古人把手指一长两短的三节比作古典格律中一长两短的三个音节，英语重音诗律又用它表示一重两轻的音步。
etymology_story.en: The word came through Latin dactylus from Greek daktylos, meaning 'finger.' A finger's three sections, one long and two short, supplied an image for the classical long–short–short foot, later adapted to stressed–unstressed–unstressed rhythm in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 dactyl 作为完整词基，不再拆分。词族：dactyls（复数音步）、dactylic（扬抑抑格的）、dactylically（以扬抑抑格方式）；dactyl-／dactylo- 在其他学术词中表示“手指、足趾”，与本词共享希腊语来源。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dactyl is normally treated as a complete base rather than divided further. Its family includes dactyls, dactylic, and dactylically; the learned combining forms dactyl- and dactylo-, meaning 'finger' or 'toe,' share its Greek origin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的常用单词。metrical foot（音步）是上位词；anapest（抑抑扬格）为两轻一重，与 dactyl 次序相反；trochee（扬抑格）只有一重一轻两个音节。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact single-word synonym. Metrical foot is the broader term; an anapest reverses the pattern to unstressed–unstressed–stressed, while a trochee has only two syllables, stressed–unstressed.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 手指三节：长—短—短；诗歌节奏：重—轻—轻。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture three finger sections: long–short–short, matching the poetic beat strong–weak–weak.

morphology.text: de- + myelin + -ate → demyelinate（使脱髓鞘）；de- 表示去除，myelin 指髓鞘物质。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语用 de-、myelin 和 -ate 组成；myelin 联系希腊语 myelos（髓），把包在神经外的髓鞘受损脱失作为记忆画面。

usage_note: 医学动词，指髓鞘丢失，不等于整条神经已经消失；常见名词形式 demyelination。

senses.meaning_zh: 使神经纤维脱髓鞘；发生脱髓鞘
senses.meaning_en: to remove or lose the myelin sheath surrounding nerve fibres
senses.english_definition: If a process demyelinates nerve fibres, it causes them to lose their protective myelin covering; nerve fibres can also be said to demyelinate when they lose this covering.
senses.collocation_en: demyelinate nerve fibres; demyelinating disease

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学英语中由 de-（去除）、myelin（髓鞘质）与动词后缀 -ate 构成的术语。myelin 的名称可追溯至希腊语 myelos“髓”，整个动词表示神经纤维外层髓鞘的脱失。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical term combines de-, meaning removal, myelin, and the verb-forming suffix -ate. Myelin ultimately takes its name from Greek myelos, 'marrow,' and the verb describes loss of the myelin covering around nerve fibres.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：de-（去除）+ myelin（髓鞘质）+ -ate（使成为、使发生）→ demyelinate。核心词族：demyelinates（第三人称单数）、demyelinated（过去式、过去分词；脱髓鞘的）、demyelinating（现在分词；引起或涉及脱髓鞘的）、demyelination（脱髓鞘）；相关词有 myelinate（形成髓鞘）、myelination（髓鞘形成）、remyelinate（重新形成髓鞘）和 remyelination（髓鞘再生）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: de- 'remove' + myelin + the verb-forming suffix -ate → demyelinate. The core family comprises demyelinates, demyelinated, demyelinating, and demyelination; related forms include myelinate and myelination for sheath formation, and remyelinate and remyelination for its restoration.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: strip of myelin（剥除髓鞘）强调移除过程；lose myelin（失去髓鞘）对应不及物用法；damage myelin（损伤髓鞘）范围更宽，并不一定表示髓鞘已经脱失。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Strip of myelin emphasizes removal; lose myelin corresponds to the intransitive use; damage myelin is broader and does not necessarily mean that the sheath has been lost.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 去掉 + myelin 髓鞘：神经的“绝缘外套”脱落。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- removes myelin: the nerve loses its insulating coat.

etymology_story.zh: durum 来自植物学名称 Triticum durum，其中拉丁语 durum 是 durus“硬的”的中性形式，与表示“小麦”的 Triticum 配合。英语后来用 durum 单独指这种籽粒坚硬的小麦。
etymology_story.en: Durum comes from the botanical name Triticum durum, in which Latin durum is the neuter form of durus, 'hard,' agreeing with Triticum, 'wheat.' English subsequently adopted durum as a noun for this hard-grained wheat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 durum 是整体借入的简单词，通常不可数，没有常用的直接派生词；不宜把它分析成英语词根 dur- 加后缀 -um。durum wheat（硬粒小麦）、durum flour（硬粒小麦粉）和 durum semolina（硬粒小麦粗粒粉）是常用组合；durable（耐用的）与其共享拉丁语 durus 的历史联系，但不是 durum 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, durum is a borrowed simple word, normally uncountable, with no common direct derivatives; it should not be parsed as an English root dur- plus a suffix -um. Common combinations include durum wheat, durum flour, and durum semolina; durable shares a historical connection with Latin durus but is not derived from durum.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: durum wheat（硬粒小麦）是完整的等义名称；pasta wheat（意大利面用小麦）是用途导向的称呼，通常指硬粒小麦；semolina（粗粒粉）指碾磨后的产品，常由硬粒小麦制成，并不是小麦品种名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Durum wheat is the full equivalent name; pasta wheat is a use-based label usually referring to durum; semolina is a milled product, often made from durum, rather than the name of the wheat itself.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语“硬”对应坚硬麦粒，再联想到有嚼劲的意大利面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link Latin 'hard' to hard wheat kernels, then to firm pasta.

senses.collocation_en: a pastoral eclogue; Virgil's Eclogues
senses.collocation_zh: 一首田园短诗；维吉尔的《牧歌集》
senses.sentence_en: In the eclogue, two shepherds discuss love while their sheep graze nearby.
senses.sentence_zh: 在这首田园诗中，两位牧人谈论着爱情，羊群则在附近吃草。

etymology_story.zh: eclogue 经拉丁语 ecloga 源自希腊语 eklogē，原义为“选取、选段”。这一名称因维吉尔的田园诗集而与牧歌传统紧密相连，后来专指一类田园短诗。
etymology_story.en: Eclogue came through Latin ecloga from Greek eklogē, meaning 'selection' or 'extract.' Its association with Virgil's pastoral collection helped establish the later meaning of a short pastoral poem.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 eclogue 通常作为完整词基记忆，不宜按现代英语词缀强行拆分。词族包括 eclogues（复数）、eclogist（田园诗作者，较少用）、eclogic 和 eclogical（田园诗的，均较少用）；相关派生词采用 eclog- 词干。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, eclogue is normally treated as a complete base rather than divided into productive English affixes. Its family includes eclogues, the uncommon noun eclogist, and the uncommon adjectives eclogic and eclogical; these derivatives use the stem eclog-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pastoral（田园诗）范围更广，不限于短诗或对话；idyll（田园诗、田园生活描写）强调宁静理想化的生活场景，也可用于散文；bucolic（牧歌）作名词时与 eclogue 接近，但使用较少。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pastoral is broader and need not be short or dialogic; idyll emphasizes a peaceful, idealized scene and can also refer to prose; bucolic, used as a noun, is close in meaning to eclogue but less common.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“选段”记到一段田园诗：想象两位牧人在诗中交谈。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move from 'selected passage' to a pastoral scene: two shepherds talking in verse.

senses.meaning_en: A surgical incision in the perineum during childbirth.
senses.english_definition: An episiotomy is a surgical cut made in the tissue between the vaginal opening and the anus to enlarge the opening during childbirth.
senses.collocation_en: perform an episiotomy; routine episiotomy
senses.collocation_zh: 实施会阴切开术；常规会阴切开术

senses.sentence_zh: 助产士解释了分娩过程中可能需要进行会阴切开术的原因。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由源自希腊语 epision（阴部、外阴区域）的 episio- 和表示“切开术”的 -tomy 构成。其现代医学意义专指分娩时进行的会阴切开术。
etymology_story.en: The word combines episio-, from Greek epision, referring to the pubic or external genital region, with -tomy, meaning surgical cutting. Its modern medical meaning specifically concerns an incision in the perineum during childbirth.

morphology_enriched.zh: 医学构词公式：episio-（外阴、会阴区域）+ -tomy（切开术）→ episiotomy。复数为 episiotomies；相关形容词为 episiotomic（会阴切开术的），但较少使用。
morphology_enriched.en: Medical word formation: episio- (the external genital or perineal region) + -tomy (surgical cutting) → episiotomy. The plural is episiotomies; the related adjective episiotomic means relating to an episiotomy and is uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: perineal incision（会阴切口、会阴切开）是最接近的描述性表达；incision（切口、切开）是范围更广的上位词；perineotomy（会阴切开术）也是相关术语，但可用于更广泛的会阴切开操作，不能在所有语境中直接替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Perineal incision is the closest descriptive equivalent; incision is a broader term for a surgical cut; perineotomy is a related technical term that can cover other surgical incisions into the perineum and is not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: episio- 定位会阴，-tomy 表示切开：部位加手术动作。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Episio- identifies the region; -tomy identifies the surgical cut: location plus procedure.

forms: 通常不可数；表示生长过程。
family: epitaxial 外延生长的；epitaxially 以外延方式

morphology.text: epi- + -taxy → epitaxy（在表面依序生长）；epi- 表示在上，-taxy 表示排列。

etymology.text: 英语以希腊语来源的 epi（在上）和 taxis（排列）构成术语；想成新晶层照着底层晶格排列。

usage_note: 材料科学术语，指在晶体衬底上按一定晶体取向生长晶层；本课强调生长过程。

sentence: The laboratory used epitaxy to grow a thin crystal layer on the substrate.
translation: 实验室用外延生长在衬底上生长了一层薄晶体。

senses.meaning_zh: 外延生长：晶体按衬底晶体的取向关系生长
senses.meaning_en: Crystal growth in an orientation determined by a crystalline substrate.
senses.english_definition: Epitaxy is a process in which a crystal grows on another crystal with an orientation determined by the crystal underneath.
senses.collocation_en: molecular beam epitaxy; vapor-phase epitaxy
senses.collocation_zh: 分子束外延；气相外延
senses.sentence_en: The researchers used molecular beam epitaxy to grow a thin semiconductor layer.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员利用分子束外延技术生长了一层薄的半导体材料。

etymology_story.zh: 该术语经法语 épitaxie 进入英语，由希腊语来源的 epi-（在……之上）和 taxis（排列、秩序）构成。名称描述了新晶体在已有晶体表面按一定取向关系排列生长的现象。
etymology_story.en: The term entered English through French épitaxie and combines Greek-derived epi- (upon) with taxis (arrangement or order). Its name describes a new crystal growing on an existing crystal in a particular orientation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科技构词公式：epi-（在……之上）+ -taxy（排列）→ epitaxy。主要词族包括 epitaxial（外延的）、epitaxially（以外延方式）、homoepitaxy（同质外延）、heteroepitaxy（异质外延），以及 homoepitaxial（同质外延的）、heteroepitaxial（异质外延的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Scientific word formation: epi- (upon) + -taxy (arrangement) → epitaxy. The principal word family includes epitaxial (relating to epitaxy), epitaxially (by epitaxy), homoepitaxy (epitaxy involving the same material), heteroepitaxy (epitaxy involving different materials), homoepitaxial, and heteroepitaxial.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: epitaxial growth（外延生长）是直接对应表达；oriented crystal growth（定向晶体生长）范围更广，不一定涉及晶体衬底；crystal growth（晶体生长）是上位概念，不要求新晶体与衬底具有特定取向关系。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Epitaxial growth is a direct equivalent; oriented crystal growth is broader and need not involve a crystalline substrate; crystal growth is the general process and does not require a particular orientation relative to a substrate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: epi- 是“在上”，-taxy 是“排列”：上层晶体跟着底层取向长。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Epi- means upon and -taxy means arrangement: the upper crystal takes its orientation from the crystal below.

forms: 形容词；比较级 more factitious，最高级 most factitious。
family: factitiously 人为地；factitiousness 人为性

morphology.text: factitious + -ly → factitiously（人为地）；factitious 是借入的整词，作为独立词素记忆，不拆成 fact + -ious。

etymology.text: 17世纪来自拉丁语 facticius（人为制作的），关联 facere（做、制作）；把人为造出的需求或情绪作为线索。

usage_note: 正式词，强调人为制造、并非自然产生；fictitious 主要强调虚构，两者拼写相近但侧重点不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 人为制造的；刻意营造而非自然产生的
senses.meaning_en: Artificially created rather than naturally arising.
senses.english_definition: Something that is factitious has been deliberately created rather than developing naturally.
senses.collocation_en: factitious enthusiasm; factitious demand
senses.collocation_zh: 刻意营造的热情；人为制造的需求
senses.sentence_en: The campaign generated a factitious enthusiasm that quickly faded.
senses.sentence_zh: 这场宣传活动营造出了一阵很快便消退的人为热情。

senses.meaning_zh: （医学症状或疾病表现）人为诱发或伪造的
senses.meaning_en: Describing symptoms or illness deliberately induced or falsified.
senses.english_definition: Factitious symptoms are symptoms that someone deliberately produces or falsely presents as signs of illness.
senses.collocation_en: factitious disorder; factitious symptoms
senses.collocation_zh: 人为障碍；人为诱发或伪造的症状
senses.sentence_en: The article explains how clinicians assess suspected factitious symptoms.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章解释了临床医生如何评估疑似人为诱发或伪造的症状。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 facticius，意为“人工制作的”，最终关联 facere（做、制作）。英语保留了“人为造成”的核心意义，并将其用于刻意营造的情绪、需求以及人为诱发或伪造的疾病表现。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin facticius, meaning artificially made, ultimately related to facere, to make or do. English retained the idea of deliberate manufacture and extended it to emotions, demand, and induced or falsified signs of illness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 factitious 作为完整借入词识记，不拆成 fact（事实）加后缀。派生公式：factitious + -ly → factitiously（人为地、刻意地）；factitious + -ness → factitiousness（人为性、造作性）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, factitious is best treated as a complete borrowed base, not as fact plus a suffix. Derivatives are factitious + -ly → factitiously (artificially or contrivedly) and factitious + -ness → factitiousness (the quality of being artificially produced).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: artificial（人工的、不自然的）范围最广，也可中性描述人造材料；contrived（刻意设计的、牵强的）突出安排痕迹明显；spurious（虚假的、非真实的）强调真实性不足。factitious 的重点是某事由人为制造，而非自然产生。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Artificial is broad and can neutrally describe manufactured materials; contrived emphasizes conspicuous planning or forced effects; spurious emphasizes a lack of authenticity. Factitious specifically highlights deliberate production rather than natural development.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住拉丁语“制作”的线索：factitious 是“做出来的”，不是“自然来的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the Latin idea of making: factitious describes something manufactured into existence.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

usage_note: 用于植物叶、枝或纤维等聚成的小束；本课不教分册出版物义。

senses.meaning_zh: （植物、肌肉或神经纤维等的）小束
senses.meaning_en: A small bundle of plant structures, muscle fibers, or nerve fibers.
senses.english_definition: A fascicle is a small bundle of structures such as needles, muscle fibers, or nerve fibers.
senses.collocation_en: muscle fascicle; nerve fascicle
senses.collocation_zh: 肌束；神经束
senses.sentence_en: Each muscle fascicle contains a group of muscle fibers.
senses.sentence_zh: 每个肌束都包含一组肌纤维。

senses.meaning_zh: （分批出版著作的）分册
senses.meaning_en: A separately published installment of a larger work.
senses.english_definition: A fascicle is one part of a book or other large work that is published separately as the work is completed.
senses.collocation_en: publish in fascicles; the first fascicle
senses.collocation_zh: 分册出版；第一分册
senses.sentence_en: The dictionary was originally published in fascicles.
senses.sentence_zh: 这部词典最初是分册出版的。

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 fasciculus（小束），是 fascis（一束）的指小形式。“小束”的形象既用于成束的植物结构和纤维，也用于汇成一组、单独出版的书页。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin fasciculus, a small bundle, the diminutive of fascis, a bundle. The image of a small bundle applies both to grouped plant structures or fibers and to a separately issued group of pages.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 fascicle 作为完整词基；复数为 fascicles。主要词族包括 fascicled（成束的，fascicle 加 -ed，词尾 e 不重复）、fascicular（束状的、束的）、fasciculate 或 fasciculated（簇生的、成束的）和 fasciculation（成束；医学中指肌束颤动）。相关拉丁形式 fasciculus 的复数为 fasciculi。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats fascicle as a complete base; its plural is fascicles. The principal family includes fascicled (arranged in bundles, formed with -ed without doubling the final e), fascicular (relating to bundles), fasciculate or fasciculated (clustered or bundled), and fasciculation (bundling, or medically a muscle-fiber bundle twitch). The related Latin-form noun fasciculus has the plural fasciculi.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bundle（束）是最普通、范围最广的对应词；fasciculus（小束、纤维束）是解剖学中常见的相关术语，具体所指依结构而定；installment（分期出版部分）对应出版义，强调陆续推出，不一定是独立装订的分册。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bundle is the broad everyday equivalent; fasciculus is a related anatomical term whose exact reference depends on the structure; installment matches the publishing sense but emphasizes serial release and need not describe a separately bound section.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 一小束纤维，一小束书页：都可叫 fascicle。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A small bundle of fibers or a small bundle of pages: both can be a fascicle.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

etymology.text: 英语从法语 galette 借入，名字用于扁圆形的饼；用摊开、边缘折起的果馅饼形象来记。

senses.meaning_zh: （法国布列塔尼式、通常配咸馅的）荞麦薄饼

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语 galette 借入该词；其名称与 galet（卵石、圆石）有关，通常认为借用了圆而扁的形象。法语中的名称用于多种扁圆饼，英语也用它指法式馅饼和布列塔尼荞麦薄饼。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed galette from French, where the name is related to galet, a pebble, generally understood as referring to a rounded, flattened shape. The French name covers several kinds of flat cakes, and English also uses it for French pastries and Breton buckwheat pancakes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 galette 是完整借入词，不作能产性的英语词根加词缀拆分；复数为 galettes。法语词源上可联系 galet（卵石）及 -ette 形式，但这不是英语中的派生规则；英语没有常用的派生形容词或动词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, galette is a complete loanword rather than a productive English root-and-affix formation; its plural is galettes. Its French history connects it with galet (pebble) and the -ette form, but this is not an English derivational rule; it has no common derived adjective or verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tart（馅饼）通常指有底、有馅且顶部敞开的点心，常用模具成形；crostata（意式馅饼）与某些 galette 相似，但属于意大利烹饪传统；crêpe（法式薄饼）对应薄饼类，布列塔尼 galette 通常用荞麦制作并配咸馅，而 crêpe 常用小麦粉制作。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tart usually describes an open pastry with a base and filling, often shaped in a tin; crostata is a similar pastry from the Italian tradition; crêpe overlaps with the pancake sense, but a Breton galette is typically made with buckwheat and served savory, whereas a crêpe commonly uses wheat flour.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由圆扁卵石联想到圆扁饼：可盛果馅，也可包咸馅。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a flat, rounded pebble becoming a flat cake, carrying fruit or savory fillings.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪从印地语借入 ganja，其源头可追溯到梵语中的大麻名称。这个词后来随南亚移民传播到加勒比地区，并广泛见于牙买加口语和雷鬼音乐文化。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed ganja from Hindi in the nineteenth century, with its ancestry traced to a Sanskrit name for hemp. South Asian migration subsequently helped carry the word to the Caribbean, where it became prominent in Jamaican speech and reggae culture.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 ganja 作为不可再作常规分析的借入词，通常用作不可数名词；没有常用的标准派生词族。ganja smoke（大麻烟雾）等是名词组合；ganjaism 极罕见，不宜作为核心派生词学习。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ganja is an unanalyzed borrowing, normally used as a mass noun, with no common standard family of derivatives. Expressions such as ganja smoke are noun combinations; ganjaism is extremely rare and is not a useful core derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cannabis（大麻）较中性，常用于科学和正式语境；marijuana（大麻）在日常和公共讨论中常见；weed（大麻）是常见俚语。ganja 同样非正式，但南亚和加勒比文化色彩更突出。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cannabis is relatively neutral and common in scientific or formal contexts; marijuana is common in everyday and public discussion; weed is familiar slang. Ganja is also informal but has stronger South Asian and Caribbean cultural associations.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词记忆：ganja 是大麻的南亚借词名，后来也成为加勒比口语中的常用称呼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole borrowing: ganja is a South Asian name for cannabis that also became familiar in Caribbean speech.

senses.meaning_zh: 他律的；受外部规则、意志或权威支配的
senses.meaning_en: Governed by rules, purposes, or authority originating outside oneself.
senses.english_definition: If a person or their actions are heteronomous, they are governed by rules or influences that come from outside rather than by principles they independently accept.
senses.collocation_en: heteronomous morality; heteronomous ethics
senses.collocation_zh: 他律道德；他律伦理学
senses.sentence_en: The philosopher contrasts heteronomous morality with principles that people rationally choose for themselves.
senses.sentence_zh: 这位哲学家将他律道德与人们通过理性为自己选择的原则作了对比。

etymology_story.zh: heteronomous 属于以希腊语 heteros（其他的）和 nomos（法律、规则）为基础的词族，19世纪进入英语使用。它与康德伦理学中的 heteronomy（他律）密切相关，强调意志受到自身理性立法以外的因素支配。
etymology_story.en: Heteronomous belongs to a word family built on Greek heteros, meaning 'other,' and nomos, meaning 'law' or 'rule,' and entered English use in the nineteenth century. It is closely associated with heteronomy in Kantian ethics, where the will is governed by something other than its own rational legislation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词结构为 hetero-（其他、外部）+ nom-（法律、规则）+ -ous（形容词后缀）；与 heteronomy（他律）构成名词—形容词对应关系，不能简单理解为仅去掉 y 再加 -ous。词族包括 heteronomy（他律）、heteronomous（他律的）、heteronomously（以他律方式）；autonomy（自主、自律）和 autonomous（自主的、自律的）是对照词。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is hetero- ('other, external') + nom- ('law, rule') + -ous (an adjective suffix). It forms a noun–adjective pair with heteronomy, rather than being produced simply by removing y and adding -ous. The family includes heteronomy, heteronomous, and heteronomously; autonomy and autonomous provide the contrasting terms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: externally governed（受外部支配的）最直接说明规则来源；dependent（依赖的）强调缺乏独立性，但不一定涉及规则；other-directed（受他人导向的）强调行为迎合他人的期待。heteronomous 尤其关注决定意志或行为的原则来自外部。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Externally governed most directly identifies the source of control; dependent emphasizes a lack of independence without necessarily involving rules; other-directed emphasizes responding to other people's expectations. Heteronomous specifically concerns an external source of the principles governing will or action.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hetero-＝他者，nom-＝规则：规则由他者给定，就是“他律”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hetero- means 'other' and nom- means 'rule': rules supplied by another source make something heteronomous.

morphology.text: hypochondriac + -al → hypochondriacal（疑病的）。

etymology.text: 由 hypochondriac 加 -al 构成；词根经新拉丁语联系希腊语表示上腹部的词，后来发展到疑病含义。可把古老身体部位名与后来对病痛的过度担忧联系起来。

usage_note: 较正式，也可能带贬义；描述担忧时应谨慎，不能仅凭一个行为给现实中的人下诊断。

senses.meaning_zh: 疑病的；过度担心自己患病的
senses.meaning_en: Excessively anxious about having an illness.
senses.english_definition: Someone who is hypochondriacal worries too much that they are ill, often interpreting minor bodily sensations as signs of serious disease.

etymology_story.zh: hypochondriacal 由 hypochondriac 加 -al 构成；其词源最终联系希腊语中表示肋软骨下方身体区域的词。古代医学曾将这一部位与忧郁等病症联系起来，相关词义后来逐渐转向对自身健康的过度忧虑。
etymology_story.en: Hypochondriacal was formed from hypochondriac with the suffix -al; its ultimate Greek ancestry refers to the region beneath the rib cartilages. Ancient medicine associated that region with conditions such as melancholy, and the word family later developed its sense of excessive anxiety about personal health.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代直接构词：hypochondriac（疑病的；疑病者）+ -al（形容词后缀）→ hypochondriacal；hypochondriacal + -ly → hypochondriacally（以疑病方式）。词族还包括 hypochondria（疑病、疑病状态）和 hypochondriasis（疑病症，传统医学术语）；历史词素 hypo- 表示“下方”，chondr- 表示“软骨”，并不表示“低水平的担忧”。
morphology_enriched.en: The immediate modern formation is hypochondriac (an adjective or a noun denoting a person) + -al → hypochondriacal; adding -ly gives hypochondriacally. The family also includes hypochondria and hypochondriasis, a traditional medical term. Historically, hypo- means 'below' and chondr- means 'cartilage'; the components do not mean 'a low level of worry.'

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hypochondriac（疑病的）作形容词时含义基本相同，而且也可作名词指疑病者；health-anxious（对健康焦虑的）更直接描述心理体验；anxious（焦虑的）范围更广，不专指健康问题。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hypochondriac has essentially the same meaning as an adjective and can also name a person; health-anxious describes the experience more directly; anxious is broader and need not concern health.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“肋下部位”的古代医学名称，联想到“总担心身体出了问题”；记住词义经历了历史转移。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the old medical name for the region beneath the ribs with constantly fearing that something is wrong inside the body.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

etymology.text: 17世纪从希腊语 ikhor 借入，古代故事用它称神体内流动的液体；可记成与凡人鲜血相对的神之血。

usage_note: 本课仅教希腊神话义；医学文本中另可指伤口渗液，需要按语境区分。

etymology_story.zh: ichor 最终来自希腊语 ikhōr，古希腊文献用它指神体内的液体，也用于某些体液。英语在17世纪借入该词，保留了神话中的“神血”义，并在旧医学中用来指伤口或溃疡的稀薄分泌物。
etymology_story.en: Ichor ultimately comes from Greek ikhōr, which ancient texts used for the fluid of the gods and also for certain bodily fluids. Borrowed into English in the seventeenth century, it retained the mythological meaning and also appeared in older medicine for thin discharges from wounds or ulcers.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 ichor 是不可再作常规拆分的词根词，通常用作不可数名词。主要派生词为 ichor + -ous → ichorous（脓水样的；分泌稀薄脓液的），另有较少见的 ichoric（神血的；与 ichor 有关的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ichor is an unanalyzed base, normally used as a mass noun. Its principal derivative is ichor + -ous → ichorous, meaning resembling or producing a thin wound discharge; the less common ichoric means relating to ichor.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: divine blood（神血）是神话义的解释性近义表达；exudate（渗出液）是更广泛、较现代的医学术语；pus（脓）通常指较浓稠的化脓性分泌物，与旧医学义中稀薄、水样的 ichor 并不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Divine blood is an explanatory equivalent for the mythological sense; exudate is a broader, more current medical term; pus usually denotes a thicker purulent discharge and is not an exact equivalent of the thin, watery substance called ichor in older medicine.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 以“特殊的体液”为核心：神话里是神血，旧医学里是伤口流出的稀薄液体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to an unusual bodily fluid: divine blood in mythology, thin wound discharge in older medicine.

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；lambent + -ly → lambently（柔和发光地）。不要按 lamb（羊羔）拆解。

etymology.text: 来自拉丁语 lambens，源自动词 lambere（舔）。想象火舌轻舔物体表面，便能记住柔和闪动的光。

usage_note: 文学用语，常修饰 light、glow 或 flame；本卡学习实际光线的柔亮，不考形容文采的引申义。

senses.meaning_zh: 柔和发光的；微微闪烁的（文学用语）
senses.meaning_en: Glowing or flickering with a soft light; literary.
senses.english_definition: A lambent light glows or flickers gently without being harsh or dazzling.

senses.english_definition: Lambent flames move lightly over or around the surface of something.
senses.collocation_en: lambent flames; lambent fire
senses.collocation_zh: 轻舔表面的火焰；轻轻闪动的火

senses.meaning_en: Lightly brilliant or subtly witty, especially in humor or writing; literary.
senses.english_definition: Lambent wit or humor is clever and lively in a light, subtle way.
senses.collocation_en: lambent wit; lambent humor
senses.collocation_zh: 轻巧含蓄的机智；灵动含蓄的幽默

etymology_story.zh: lambent 来自拉丁语 lambent-，是 lambere（舔）的现在分词词干。英语最初用它描写仿佛轻舔表面的火焰，后来扩展到柔和闪动的光，又引申为轻巧灵动的机智或文风。
etymology_story.en: Lambent comes from Latin lambent-, the present-participle stem of lambere, meaning 'to lick.' English first used it for flames seeming to lick a surface, then extended it to softly playing light and, figuratively, to lightly brilliant wit or writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 lambent 通常作为完整的借入形容词学习，不能拆成 lamb（羊羔）加后缀。词族包括 lambent + -ly → lambently（柔和闪动地；轻巧灵动地），以及 lambency（柔和闪光；轻灵的光彩）；其拉丁语来源可分析为 lamb-（舔）+ -ent-（现在分词成分）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lambent is best learned as a complete borrowed adjective, not as lamb plus a suffix. Its family includes lambent + -ly → lambently and the noun lambency, meaning softly playing light or light brilliance. Its Latin source contains lamb- ('lick') and the participial element -ent-.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: luminous（发光的）只强调有光，不一定柔和或闪动；flickering（闪烁的）强调亮度或火焰的不稳定变化；sparkling（才思闪耀的）可形容机智，但通常比 lambent 更鲜明、更外露。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Luminous emphasizes giving off light without necessarily suggesting softness or movement; flickering emphasizes unsteady changes in light or flame; sparkling can describe wit but usually suggests a brighter, more conspicuous brilliance than lambent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“舔”：火舌轻舔表面 → 光柔和闪动 → 才思轻轻闪光。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow 'lick': a flame lightly licks a surface, light plays softly, and wit shines with a gentle touch.

senses.meaning_zh: 阴沉地皱眉；怒目而视，尤用于文学语境
senses.meaning_en: to frown or look threatening, especially in literary usage
senses.english_definition: If someone lours, they look angry or threatening, usually with a frown.

senses.collocation_zh: 阴沉地瞪着某人；阴沉的表情

senses.meaning_zh: 天空或云层变得阴暗逼人；呈现风暴将至的景象，尤用于文学语境
senses.meaning_en: of the sky or clouds, to look dark and threatening, especially in literary usage
senses.english_definition: If the sky or clouds lour, they become dark and seem to threaten bad weather.

senses.sentence_zh: 乌云阴沉沉地笼罩着群山。

etymology_story.zh: 源自中古英语 louren，早期含有“皱眉、显露不悦”的意思，后来也用于形容天空阴沉。更早的词源尚不确定，可能与其他日耳曼语言中表示窥视或阴沉注视的词有关。
etymology_story.en: Lour comes from Middle English louren, associated with frowning or showing displeasure, and was subsequently applied to threatening skies. Its earlier origin is uncertain, though connections with Germanic words for watching or looking sullen have been proposed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为不可再作常规拆分的词基 lour；屈折形式为 lours、loured、louring。词族包括 louring（阴沉的、怒容满面的）和 louringly（阴沉地）；另有同音异拼形式 lower，须与表示“降低”的 lower 区分。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lour is a simple base rather than a productive combination of smaller parts; its inflected forms are lours, loured, and louring. Its family includes adjectival louring and the adverb louringly; lower is an alternative spelling, distinct from the verb lower meaning to reduce height or amount.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: frown（皱眉）主要描述面部动作；scowl（怒目而视）更突出愤怒或敌意；loom（隐约逼近、赫然耸现）强调庞大或威胁性的存在感，而 lour 强调人脸或天空的阴沉神态。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Frown mainly describes a facial movement; scowl suggests stronger anger or hostility; loom emphasizes an imposing or threatening presence, whereas lour emphasizes a dark, sullen appearance in a face or sky.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把阴沉的脸看成一片乌云：脸和天空都能 lour。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a face turning stormy: both a face and a sky can lour.

etymology.text: 现代英语把源自希腊语的 meta- 与 language 组合成这个术语，20世纪逻辑学和语言研究中开始使用。可以记成“用语言来谈语言”。

usage_note: noun、verb 等术语属于谈论语言的工具。metalanguage 描述语言本身，不是指说话声音像金属。

senses.meaning_zh: 元语言；用于描述或分析另一种语言的语言或术语体系
senses.meaning_en: language or terminology used to describe or analyze another language
senses.english_definition: A metalanguage is a language or set of terms that you use to describe and discuss another language.
senses.collocation_en: grammatical metalanguage; the metalanguage of linguistics
senses.collocation_zh: 语法元语言；语言学的元语言
senses.sentence_en: Terms such as 'noun' and 'verb' are part of the metalanguage used to describe English.
senses.sentence_zh: noun（名词）和 verb（动词）等术语属于用于描述英语的元语言。

etymology_story.zh: 这是20世纪逻辑学和语言研究中的构词，由 meta- 与 language 组成，用于区分被讨论的“对象语言”和描述它的语言。meta- 源自希腊语，在此表示超出原有层次、对其进行描述的关系。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century formation combines meta- with language and distinguishes an object language from the language used to describe it. The Greek-derived prefix meta- here signals a level at which the original system is discussed or analyzed.

morphology_enriched.zh: meta-（描述某系统的更高层次）+ language（语言）→ metalanguage；复数为 metalanguages。相关词族包括 metalinguistic（元语言的）、metalinguistically（从元语言角度）和 metalinguistics（元语言研究），后三者使用相关词干 linguist-/linguistic，而非直接在完整的 metalanguage 后加后缀。
morphology_enriched.en: Meta- (at a level describing a system) + language forms metalanguage; the plural is metalanguages. Related family members include metalinguistic, metalinguistically, and metalinguistics, which use the related linguist-/linguistic stem rather than adding suffixes directly to the complete word metalanguage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: terminology（术语体系）泛指某领域的专门词汇；technical language（专业语言）强调专业交流所用的表达；descriptive language（描述性语言）范围更广，只有以语言本身为描述对象时才构成 metalanguage。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Terminology means the specialized vocabulary of any field; technical language emphasizes expressions used in specialist communication; descriptive language is broader and functions as metalanguage only when language itself is what it describes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用语言谈语言，就是元语言。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Language talking about language is metalanguage.

etymology_story.zh: 源自意大利语 mezza tinta，字面义为“半色调”，其中 mezza 表示“半”，tinta 表示“色调”。该名称指向这种版画技法所能表现的丰富中间调，后来也用于指成品版画及相应的制作动作。
etymology_story.en: Mezzotint derives from Italian mezza tinta, literally 'half tint,' combining mezza, meaning 'half,' with tinta, meaning 'tint' or 'tone.' The name refers to the process's rich intermediate tones and came to denote both the resulting print and the act of producing it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 mezzotint 作为整体借词使用；mezzo- 与 tint 的联系可辅助理解，但不宜把它当作普通英语前缀加词根的规则构词。名词复数为 mezzotints；同形转类为动词后有 mezzotints、mezzotinted、mezzotinting；mezzotinter 指美柔汀版画制作者。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats mezzotint as an established loanword; the association with mezzo- and tint helps explain it, but it is not an ordinary productive English prefix-and-root formation. The noun plural is mezzotints; conversion to a verb gives mezzotints, mezzotinted, and mezzotinting; a mezzotinter is an artist who works in the process.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: engraving（雕版或雕版画）是更宽泛的类别，也常特指用刻刀刻线的技法；etching（蚀刻）主要靠酸蚀形成图像；aquatint（飞尘法）也擅长表现色调，但通过颗粒状防蚀层和酸蚀形成明暗，而 mezzotint 通过刮磨粗化版面获得亮部。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Engraving is a broader category and also names a line-cutting technique; etching creates an image chiefly through acid biting; aquatint also produces tonal areas but uses a granular resist and acid, whereas mezzotint creates lighter areas by smoothing a roughened plate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“半色调”：从深黑中磨出亮部，形成细腻的中间层次。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'half tint': smoothing light out of darkness creates delicate middle tones.

etymology_story.zh: 由源自希腊语 mikros（小）的 micro- 与英语 world（世界）组合而成，字面义为“小世界”。在计算机教育中，这一名称又用于指范围受限、可供学习者主动探索的模拟环境。
etymology_story.en: Microworld combines micro-, from Greek mikros meaning 'small,' with English world, literally naming a small world. In computing education, the term also came to describe a bounded simulated environment that learners can actively explore.

morphology_enriched.zh: micro-（微小）+ world（世界）→ microworld；复数为 microworlds。常规词族主要限于单复数形式，没有广泛通用的专属派生形容词或副词；microcosm（微观缩影）是意义相关词，并非其直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Micro- (small) + world forms microworld; its plural is microworlds. Its ordinary word family is largely limited to these number forms, with no widely established dedicated adjective or adverb; microcosm is semantically related rather than a direct derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: microcosm（缩影）强调小系统反映更大整体；microenvironment（微环境）强调局部物理或生物条件；simulation（模拟环境）强调对系统的建模，而教育意义上的 microworld 特别强调学习者在有限世界中的主动探索。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Microcosm emphasizes a small system that reflects a larger whole; microenvironment emphasizes localized physical or biological conditions; simulation emphasizes modeling a system, while an educational microworld particularly emphasizes active exploration within a bounded world.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: micro 表示“小”：把世界缩小，就得到可观察、可探索的 microworld。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Micro means small: shrink a world until you can observe or explore it.

senses.meaning_zh: 江湖骗子；靠夸耀和假冒本领骗人的人，原指招摇卖假药者
senses.meaning_en: a boastful fraud who deceives people by pretending to have knowledge or skills, originally a seller of supposed cures
senses.english_definition: A mountebank is someone who deceives people by making impressive claims about knowledge, skills, or cures that they do not really possess.
senses.collocation_en: a political mountebank; a shameless mountebank
senses.collocation_zh: 政治骗子；无耻的江湖骗子

etymology_story.zh: 源自意大利语 montimbanco，与 monta in banco（登上长凳）这一表达有关，原指登上长凳或台子招徕顾客的卖药人。由于这类人常靠夸张宣传推销所谓灵药，词义后来扩展为假冒行家、招摇撞骗的人。
etymology_story.en: Mountebank comes from Italian montimbanco, associated with monta in banco, 'mount onto a bench,' referring to a medicine seller who stood on a bench or platform to attract customers. Its meaning broadened from a seller of supposed remedies to a boastful impostor or fraud.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 mountebank 为整体词基，不宜按现代英语的 mount + bank 直接推导词义；历史上的 bank 对应“长凳”，不是“银行”。复数为 mountebanks；派生词 mountebankery（江湖骗术、招摇撞骗的行为）较少见。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats mountebank as a complete base rather than a transparent combination of the current words mount and bank; the historical bank element refers to a bench, not a financial institution. The plural is mountebanks; the derivative mountebankery, meaning fraudulent showmanship or imposture, is uncommon.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: charlatan（假行家）突出冒充拥有专业知识；quack（庸医、冒牌医者）主要用于医疗领域；impostor（冒名者、假冒者）强调虚假身份，而 mountebank 常带有公开表演、夸口招徕的意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Charlatan emphasizes pretended expertise; quack chiefly concerns false medical competence; impostor emphasizes an assumed identity, while mountebank often suggests public showmanship and extravagant claims.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象一个登上长凳大声卖“神药”的骗子：高台招摇，假冒行家。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a fraud mounting a bench to advertise a miracle cure: a showy false expert.

etymology_story.zh: pearlescent 由 pearl（珍珠）加表示某种状态或性质的后缀 -escent 构成，英语用例至少可追溯至1926年。它把珍珠的柔润光泽作为参照，用来描写油漆、涂层等表面的视觉效果。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pearlescent)
etymology_story.en: Pearlescent combines pearl with the adjective-forming suffix -escent and is recorded in English from at least 1926. It uses a pearl's soft lustre as the model for describing surfaces such as paints and coatings. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pearlescent)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：pearl（珍珠）+ -escent（呈现某种性质的）→ pearlescent。直接词族：pearlescence（名词，珠光），pearlescently（罕用副词，呈珠光地）；基础词族：pearl（名词，珍珠；动词，采珠或使呈珠状），pearly（形容词，珍珠般的），pearling（名词，采珠业；亦为 pearl 的 -ing 形式）。比较级和最高级通常用 more pearlescent、most pearlescent。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: pearl + -escent, meaning 'having or displaying a quality' → pearlescent. Direct derivatives are pearlescence (noun, pearl-like lustre) and the uncommon adverb pearlescently. The base family includes pearl (noun and verb), pearly (adjective), and pearling (a noun for pearl harvesting and also the -ing form of pearl). Comparison normally uses more pearlescent and most pearlescent.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pearly（珍珠般的）最接近日常表达，也可强调珍珠般的颜色或形状；nacreous（珍珠母般的）较专业，强调贝壳内层的珠光；iridescent（虹彩的）强调随光线或视角变化而出现的多种颜色，色彩变化通常比 pearlescent 更明显。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pearly is the closest everyday alternative and can also describe pearl-like colour or shape; nacreous is more technical and evokes mother-of-pearl; iridescent emphasizes colours that change with the light or viewing angle, often more noticeably than pearlescent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pearl（珍珠）→ 像珍珠表面一样泛着柔光。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pearl → a surface glowing softly like a pearl.

etymology_story.zh: platen 源自中古英语 plateine（薄金属板），后者借自盎格鲁法语，与 plate（板）同源。它从普通的板状物发展为机器中的施压或承压部件名称，也用于打字机的承纸滚筒。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/platen)
etymology_story.en: Platen comes from Middle English plateine, meaning a thin metal plate, borrowed from Anglo-French and related to plate. Its meaning developed from a plate to a machine component that applies or receives pressure, including the paper-supporting roller of a typewriter. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/platen)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 platen 视为完整词干，不拆成 plate + -en；复数为 platens。派生词 platenless（形容词，无压板或无压纸滚筒的）用于特定技术语境；常见复合表达包括 platen press（平压印刷机）、platen roller（压纸滚筒）和 platen glass（稿台玻璃）。plate 是历史相关词，不是现代派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, platen is a whole stem rather than plate + -en; its plural is platens. The derivative platenless means 'without a platen' in specialized contexts. Established compounds include platen press, platen roller, and platen glass. Plate is historically related rather than a modern derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pressure plate（压板）可对应施压或承压平板这一义项，但也用于其他机械部件；roller（滚筒）可描述打字机中的 platen，但范围更广；document glass（稿台玻璃）对应扫描或复印语境。三个表达分别对应不同义项，不能跨语境任意替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pressure plate can correspond to the flat pressure-bearing sense but also names other mechanical components; roller describes a typewriter platen but is broader; document glass corresponds to the scanning or copying sense. These alternatives apply to different senses and are not freely interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 plate（板）：机器里托住材料或承受压力的那块板；打字机里则卷成了承纸滚筒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of plate: the machine surface supporting material or taking pressure; in a typewriter, picture that support as a roller.

etymology_story.zh: pneumothorax 经新拉丁语医学用语进入英语，由源自希腊语的 pneumo-（气、呼吸）和 thorax（胸部）组成。它在英语中至少可追溯至1821年，指胸膜腔内积气，而不是肺内正常存在的空气。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pneumothorax)
etymology_story.en: Pneumothorax entered English through New Latin medical terminology, combining Greek-derived pneumo-, meaning air or breath, with thorax, meaning chest. Recorded in English from at least 1821, it names gas in the pleural cavity rather than the air normally inside the lungs. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/pneumothorax)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代医学构词：pneumo-（此处指气体）+ thorax（胸部）→ pneumothorax。复数为 pneumothoraces 或 pneumothoraxes；相关复合术语有 hydropneumothorax（液气胸）和 hemopneumothorax（血气胸，英式亦写 haemopneumothorax）。thoracic（胸部的）属于 thorax 的词族；pneumonia（肺炎）不是 pneumothorax 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern medical formation: pneumo- ('air' here) + thorax ('chest') → pneumothorax. Plurals are pneumothoraces and pneumothoraxes. Related compounds include hydropneumothorax (fluid and air in the pleural cavity) and hemopneumothorax, also British haemopneumothorax (blood and air there). Thoracic belongs to the thorax family; pneumonia is not a derivative of pneumothorax.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: air in the pleural cavity（胸膜腔积气）是准确的描述性同义表达；pleural air（胸膜腔内气体）是较简短的临床表述；collapsed lung（肺萎陷）是常见通俗说法，但强调可能出现的结果，也可能指其他原因造成的肺萎陷，因此并非严格同义。[美国国家癌症研究所](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/pneumothorax)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Air in the pleural cavity is an accurate descriptive equivalent; pleural air is shorter clinical wording; collapsed lung is a common lay expression but emphasizes a possible consequence and can describe collapse from other causes, so it is not an exact synonym. [National Cancer Institute](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/pneumothorax)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pneumo-（气）+ thorax（胸）：气跑进肺外的胸膜腔。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pneumo- 'air' + thorax 'chest': air collects outside the lung in the pleural space.

etymology.text: 20世纪美国口语中出现的英语词，用来表达对肮脏、邋遢事物的厌恶。它的声音也容易让人联想到 scum（污垢）。

etymology_story.zh: scuzzy 是20世纪出现的俚语，韦氏词典记录的最早用例为1962年，但其确切来源不明。它既形容外观肮脏破败，也表达对人品或行为的厌恶；与 scum 或 disgusting 的联系不宜当作已证实的词源。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/scuzzy)
etymology_story.en: Scuzzy is twentieth-century slang, with a first known use dated to 1962 by Merriam-Webster, but its precise origin is unknown. It describes both physical dirtiness and objectionable character or behaviour; proposed connections with scum or disgusting should not be treated as established etymology. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/scuzzy)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 scuzz（污垢、令人嫌恶的人或物）+ -y（具有某种特征的）→ scuzzy；这是共时构词分析，不代表已确定历史派生顺序。词族包括 scuzz、scuzziness（名词，脏乱或卑劣）、scuzzball（名词，卑劣或令人嫌恶的人）；副词 scuzzily 较少见。比较级 scuzzier，最高级 scuzziest。
morphology_enriched.en: A modern analysis is scuzz ('filth or an unpleasant person or thing') + -y ('characterized by') → scuzzy; this describes the present-day structure without establishing the historical order of formation. The family includes scuzz, scuzziness (noun), and scuzzball (a contemptible or unpleasant person); the adverb scuzzily is uncommon. Comparative: scuzzier; superlative: scuzziest.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: grubby（脏兮兮的）侧重表面污垢或不整洁；seedy（破败低俗的）侧重环境衰败或名声不佳；sleazy（卑劣猥琐的）更强调不正派、欺骗性或性方面的低俗。scuzzy 带强烈嫌恶感，可同时涵盖外表脏乱和品行卑劣。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Grubby emphasizes dirt or untidiness; seedy suggests shabby surroundings or a disreputable atmosphere; sleazy more strongly suggests dishonesty, moral unpleasantness, or sexual sordidness. Scuzzy expresses strong disgust and can cover both physical condition and character.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: scuzz（污垢）+ -y：像沾满污垢一样让人嫌恶，也可转指人品。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Scuzz 'filth' + -y: unpleasant as if covered in grime, physically or morally.

etymology_story.zh: skald 借自古诺尔斯语 skáld（诗人），英语用例至少可追溯至1780年。英语中主要用它称呼古代斯堪的纳维亚诗人，也可较宽泛地指吟游诗人。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/skald)
etymology_story.en: Skald was borrowed from Old Norse skáld, meaning poet, and is recorded in English from at least 1780. English uses it chiefly for an ancient Scandinavian poet and, more broadly, for a bard. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/skald)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 skald 是不可再作常规拆分的借词词干；复数为 skalds。skald + -ic → skaldic（形容词，古代北欧诗人的；北欧宫廷诗歌的），如 skaldic poetry（北欧宫廷诗歌）；异体拼写 scald 及其派生形容词 scaldic 较少见，此处的 scald 与表示“烫伤”的 scald 是不同词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, skald is an unsegmented borrowed stem; its plural is skalds. Skald + -ic → skaldic, an adjective relating to skalds or their verse, as in skaldic poetry. Less usual spelling variants are scald and scaldic; this noun scald is a different word from scald meaning 'burn with hot liquid'.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: poet（诗人）范围最广，不限定时代或文化；bard（吟游诗人、颂诗诗人）强调传统诗歌创作或传唱；court poet（宫廷诗人）强调服务于君主的身份。skald 特指古代北欧传统中的诗人，并非所有 skald 都必须担任宫廷职务。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Poet is the broadest term and has no necessary historical or cultural restriction; bard suggests traditional verse-making or recitation; court poet emphasizes service to a ruler. Skald identifies the ancient Scandinavian tradition, although not every skald necessarily held a court position.

senses.meaning_zh: 声谱记录仪；声谱分析仪
senses.meaning_en: an instrument that produces a visual record of the frequency components of sound
senses.english_definition: A sonograph is an instrument that analyzes sound and produces a visual record showing its different frequencies over time.

senses.collocation_zh: 声谱记录仪；用声谱记录仪分析语音

etymology_story.zh: 该词由源自拉丁语 sonus（声音）的 sono- 与源自希腊语 graphein（书写）的 -graph 构成。其命名体现了把声音转化为可见记录的功能，尤其指记录声音频率结构的仪器。
etymology_story.en: The word combines sono-, from Latin sonus, meaning 'sound,' with -graph, ultimately from Greek graphein, meaning 'to write.' Its name describes the conversion of sound into a visible record, particularly a record of its frequency structure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：sono-（声音）+ -graph（记录仪器）→ sonograph。复数为 sonographs；相关构词族包括 sonogram（声谱图；超声图像）、sonography（声成像；现代通常指超声检查）、sonographic（声成像的；超声检查的）、sonographically（以声成像方式）和 sonographer（超声检查技师）；这些相关词在现代医学中常有专门含义。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: sono- ('sound') + -graph ('recording instrument') → sonograph. The plural is sonographs. Related formations include sonogram, sonography, sonographic, sonographically, and sonographer; several of these now have established medical meanings involving ultrasound.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sound spectrograph（声谱仪）是这一技术义下最接近的对应词；sound recorder（录音设备）侧重保存声音，而非显示频谱；oscilloscope（示波器）主要显示电信号波形，不能直接当作声谱仪的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sound spectrograph is the closest technical equivalent. A sound recorder preserves audio rather than necessarily displaying its spectrum, while an oscilloscope primarily displays electrical waveforms and is not an interchangeable term.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sono- 是声音，-graph 是记录：把听见的声音变成看得见的频谱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sound + recording instrument: turn what you hear into a spectrum you can see.

senses.meaning_zh: 频闪的；利用周期性闪光观察运动的
senses.meaning_en: using or relating to repeated brief flashes of light, especially to observe motion
senses.english_definition: Stroboscopic lighting or equipment uses repeated brief flashes of light, which can make a moving object appear stationary or move more slowly.
senses.collocation_en: stroboscopic effect; stroboscopic lighting
senses.collocation_zh: 频闪效应；频闪照明

senses.sentence_zh: 在频闪照明下，旋转的轮子看起来像是静止的。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 stroboscope（频闪观测仪）派生，后者结合了与希腊语 strobos（旋转、打转）有关的成分和表示观察的 -scope。其含义从相关观测仪器扩展到周期性闪光及其产生的视觉效应。
etymology_story.en: The adjective comes from stroboscope, which combines an element associated with Greek strobos, meaning 'whirling,' and -scope, referring to observation. Its use extends from the instrument to repeated flashing light and the visual effects it produces.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：stroboscope 去掉词尾 e + -ic（……的）→ stroboscopic。常用构词族包括 stroboscope（频闪观测仪）、stroboscopically（以频闪方式）、stroboscopy（频闪观测法）和 strobe（频闪灯；发出频闪光，名词或动词）；strobe 是 stroboscope 的缩略形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: stroboscope minus final e + -ic → stroboscopic. The main family includes stroboscope, stroboscopically, stroboscopy, and strobe, a shortened form of stroboscope used as both a noun and a verb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flashing（闪烁的）泛指反复闪光；intermittent（间歇的）只强调时断时续；pulsating（脉动的）强调有节奏的强弱变化。stroboscopic 更具体地指短促、重复的闪光，常涉及对运动的视觉影响。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flashing broadly describes repeated flashes, intermittent emphasizes interruptions, and pulsating suggests rhythmic changes in intensity. Stroboscopic specifically concerns repeated brief flashes, often with an effect on the perception of motion.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 旋转物体＋一闪一看：连续运动仿佛被切成静止画面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A spinning object seen flash by flash can look like a sequence of frozen pictures.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语 voracité 源自拉丁语 voracitas（贪食），与 vorax（贪吃的）和 vorare（吞食）同源。由大量吞食食物的本义，发展出对知识、信息等事物如饥似渴的比喻义。
etymology_story.en: The word came through French voracité from Latin voracitas, related to vorax, meaning 'greedy for food,' and vorare, meaning 'to devour.' The literal idea of consuming food eagerly developed into a figurative sense of an intense appetite for knowledge, information, or other things.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词分析：拉丁词干 vorac-（贪食的）+ 名词后缀 -ity（性质、状态）→ voracity；vorac- 在现代英语中不是独立词。核心词族包括 voracious（贪食的；求知欲强的）、voraciously（贪婪地；如饥似渴地）和 voraciousness（贪食；强烈渴求）；devour（吞食）以及 omnivore（杂食动物）等也与拉丁语 vorare 同源。
morphology_enriched.en: Analysis: the Latin-derived stem vorac- ('voracious') + -ity ('state or quality') → voracity; vorac- is not an independent English word. The core family includes voracious, voraciously, and voraciousness. Devour and formations such as omnivore also share the Latin root vorare.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ravenousness（极度饥饿）更强调饿得厉害；gluttony（暴食、贪食）通常带有过量进食的贬义；avidity（热切、渴求）适合比喻义，强调追求某物的强烈愿望。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ravenousness emphasizes extreme hunger, while gluttony usually criticizes excessive eating. Avidity is closer to the figurative sense and emphasizes an eager desire for something.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“吞食”：吞食物是贪食，吞知识是如饥似渴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'devour': devour food literally, or devour knowledge figuratively.

etymology_story.zh: 该词是十九世纪的动物学术语，由源自希腊语 zōion（动物）的 zoo- 和表示形似的 -oid 构成。它用于指群体动物中具有动物个体形态、但属于整个群体的组成单位。
etymology_story.en: This nineteenth-century zoological term combines zoo-, from Greek zōion, meaning 'animal,' with -oid, meaning 'resembling.' It names an animal-like individual unit that forms part of a larger colonial organism.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：zoo-（动物）+ -oid（形似者）→ zooid。复数为 zooids，形容词为 zooidal（个员的）；相关专业复合词包括 autozooid（通常承担摄食功能的普通个员）和 heterozooid（与普通个员形态或功能不同的特化个员）。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: zoo- ('animal') + -oid ('resembling entity') → zooid. The plural is zooids, and the adjective is zooidal. Related technical compounds include autozooid, an ordinary zooid typically involved in feeding, and heterozooid, a specialized zooid differing in form or function.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: individual（个体）是更宽泛的词，不一定属于群体动物；polyp（水螅体、珊瑚虫体）只指特定类群中的体型或个体，不能涵盖所有 zooids；module（模块）强调群体中重复的结构单位，是解释性近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Individual is broader and need not refer to a colonial animal. Polyp describes a particular body form or individual in certain animal groups, so it does not cover all zooids. Module emphasizes a repeated structural unit and is an explanatory near-equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: zoo- 动物＋-oid 形似：一个大群体里，一个个“小动物单元”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Animal + resembling: picture the small animal units that build one larger colony.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 apiarium（养蜂场），由 apis（蜜蜂）和表示场所的 -arium 构成。进入英语后，它继续指集中饲养蜂群、放置蜂箱的地方。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin apiarium, meaning 'a place for bees,' formed from apis, meaning 'bee,' and the place-forming suffix -arium. In English, it retained the sense of a location where bee colonies are kept in hives.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：api-（蜜蜂）+ -ary（场所）→ apiary；该词整体借自拉丁语，并非现代英语中新造。复数为 apiaries；相关词族包括 apiarist（养蜂人）、apiarian（蜜蜂的；养蜂的）、apiculture（养蜂业）、apicultural（养蜂业的）和 apiculturist（养蜂人、养蜂专家）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: api- ('bee') + -ary ('place') → apiary, although the word was borrowed as a whole from Latin. The plural is apiaries. Related words include apiarist, apiarian, apiculture, apicultural, and apiculturist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bee yard（蜂场）是较通俗的近义表达；bee farm（养蜂农场）更强调经营活动或整个养蜂企业；beehive（蜂箱、蜂巢）指单个蜂群的住所，而 apiary 指放置一个或多个蜂箱的场所。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bee yard is a less formal equivalent. Bee farm puts more emphasis on the farming operation or business. A beehive is the home of a single bee colony, whereas an apiary is the site where one or more hives are kept.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: api- 蜜蜂＋-ary 场所：蜜蜂住的蜂箱集中起来，就是养蜂场。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bee + place: a site where beehives are gathered is an apiary.

etymology_story.zh: 由源自希腊语的否定前缀 a- 和 plastic（与塑造、形成有关的）构成，用于医学，表示组织形成或再生不足。这里的 plastic 保留了“形成”的早期含义，与塑料无关。
etymology_story.en: This medical adjective combines the Greek-derived negative prefix a- with plastic, meaning concerned with molding or formation. Plastic here retains its older sense of forming tissue and does not refer to synthetic material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：a-（无；缺乏）+ plastic（形成组织的）→ aplastic。核心医学词族包括 aplasia（组织或器官未发育；再生障碍）、aplastic（发育不全的；再生不良的）和较少见的 aplasic（发育不全的）；plastic、plasticity（可塑性）、plastically（以可塑方式）共享“塑造、形成”的词源基础。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: a- (without or lacking) + plastic (concerned with tissue formation) → aplastic. The core medical family includes aplasia, aplastic, and the less common adjective aplasic; plastic, plasticity, and plastically share the underlying historical idea of molding or formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hypoplastic（发育不全的）强调组织发育不足；underdeveloped（未充分发育的）是较宽泛的普通用词；nonfunctional（无功能的）强调功能缺失，不一定涉及组织形成。三者均不能在所有医学语境中替换 aplastic。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hypoplastic emphasizes insufficient tissue development; underdeveloped is a broader everyday description; nonfunctional describes a lack of function without necessarily implying failed tissue formation. None is interchangeable with aplastic in every medical context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a- 表示“缺乏”，plastic 表示“形成”：组织“形成不起来”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A- means lacking; plastic concerns formation: tissue fails to form or regenerate.

etymology_story.zh: 由 cathode（阴极）派生；cathode 是法拉第在19世纪采用的电化学术语，命名得到威廉·惠威尔的协助，取自希腊语 kathodos，意为“向下的道路”。cathodic 随后用来描述与阴极有关的性质和过程。
etymology_story.en: Cathodic derives from cathode, an electrochemical term adopted by Michael Faraday in the nineteenth century with naming assistance from William Whewell, from Greek kathodos, meaning a downward path. The adjective came to describe properties and processes associated with that electrode.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cathode（阴极，去掉词尾 e）+ -ic（……的）→ cathodic。词族包括 cathode（阴极）、cathodic（阴极的）、cathodically（以阴极方式）、cathodal（阴极的）和 cathodally（以阴极方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: cathode, with final e removed, + -ic (relating to) → cathodic. The family includes cathode, cathodic, cathodically, cathodal, and cathodally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cathodal（阴极的）与 cathodic 意义接近，但 cathodic protection 等固定术语通常使用 cathodic；electrochemical（电化学的）范围更广；reductive（还原的）强调还原反应，不一定专指电极。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cathodal is a close alternative, although established terms such as cathodic protection normally use cathodic. Electrochemical is broader, while reductive emphasizes reduction and need not refer specifically to an electrode.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cathode 是阴极，-ic 表示“相关的”：阴极处发生还原。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Cathode + -ic means cathode-related: reduction happens at the cathode.

etymology_story.zh: 借自法语 chapeau（帽子），经古法语 chapel 可追溯至拉丁语 cappa（带兜帽的斗篷）。法律及正式文件中的引申义把位于各分项上方的统领文字比作一顶“帽子”。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French chapeau, meaning hat, which developed through Old French chapel from Latin cappa, a hooded cloak. In legal and formal writing, introductory wording above a set of provisions is figuratively treated as their hat.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再作常规词缀分析的法语借词处理。复数为 chapeaux 或 chapeaus；罕见形容词 chapeaued 表示“戴着帽子的”，不属于日常核心词汇。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chapeau is treated as a French loanword without a productive English root-and-affix breakdown. Its plurals are chapeaux and chapeaus; the rare adjective chapeaued means wearing a hat and is outside the everyday core vocabulary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hat（帽子）是普通中性用词，chapeau 通常带诙谐或法语色彩；headwear（头部穿戴物）是范围更广的集合称呼；在法律义中，introductory clause（引导条款）是较透明的释义，未必具有 chapeau 对后续分项的统领作用。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hat is the neutral everyday term, whereas chapeau often sounds playful or French. Headwear is a broader collective term; in legal usage, introductory clause is a transparent alternative, although it does not always imply the same governing relationship to subsequent provisions.

mnemonic_anchor.en: A hat sits above your head; a legal chapeau sits above and governs the provisions below.

etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from the Hindi and Urdu bird name commonly transliterated as chakor or cakor, generally traced further back to Sanskrit cakora. In English, it became the name of the chukar partridge.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为整体借入的单纯词，不能可靠地拆成英语词根与词缀。常用复数为 chukars；chukar partridge（石鸡）是复合名称；chukar-like（像石鸡的）属于可临时构造的表达，并非固定的常用派生词。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chukar partridge（石鸡）是同一鸟种的完整名称；partridge（鹧鸪类鸟）是上位词，范围更广；rock partridge（欧石鸡）通常指另一鸟种，不能作为精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chukar partridge is the fuller name for the same species. Partridge is a broader category, while rock partridge normally names a different species and is not an exact synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 借自盎格鲁法语 cordage，由 corde（绳）和表示集合的后缀 -age 构成。它保留了“绳索集合”的含义，尤其常见于航海和制绳语境。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Anglo-French cordage, formed from corde, meaning rope, and the collective suffix -age. It retained the meaning of ropes collectively, especially in nautical and rope-making contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可分析为 cord（绳）+ -age（集合）→ cordage（绳索总称）。相关词族包括 cord（绳；用绳捆）、corded（有绳的；带棱纹的）、cording（绳饰；捆扎）和 cordage；cordage 通常不使用复数。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analyzed as cord + -age, a collective suffix, giving cordage, or ropes collectively. Related forms include cord as a noun and verb, corded, cording, and cordage; cordage normally has no plural.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rope（绳；粗绳）可指单根绳索或这种材料；line（绳；索）常按航海等具体用途命名；rigging（索具）指船上的支撑和操纵系统，其范围可包括绳索、钢缆及相关配件。cordage 强调绳索本身的集合。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rope can mean an individual length or the material generally; line often identifies a rope by its practical use, especially at sea. Rigging denotes a vessel's supporting and operating system, which can include ropes, wire cables, and fittings; cordage emphasizes the ropes themselves collectively.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cord 是绳，-age 把它们集合起来：一整批绳索。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 coruscāre，意为“闪光、闪耀”，英语形式以其过去分词词干 coruscāt- 为基础。词义由实际的光芒闪烁，进一步比喻思想、谈吐或文笔的才华闪耀。
etymology_story.en: Coruscate comes from Latin coruscāre, meaning 'to flash or glitter,' through its past-participial stem coruscāt-. Its meaning extended from physical flashes of light to brilliance in thought, conversation, and writing.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 coruscate 作为整体词基，不拆成有独立意义的普通英语词素。词族包括 coruscates、coruscated、coruscating；coruscate 去掉词尾 e 加 -ion 构成 coruscation（闪光；才华的闪现）；相关形容词有 coruscant（闪耀的，罕用）和 coruscating（闪耀的；才华横溢的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, coruscate is normally treated as a whole base rather than divided into independently meaningful everyday elements. Its family includes coruscates, coruscated, and coruscating; removing final e and adding -ion gives coruscation, 'a flash or display of brilliance.' Related adjectives include the rare coruscant and the participial adjective coruscating.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sparkle（闪闪发光）最通用，也可形容谈吐生动；scintillate（闪烁；才思焕发）与本词最接近，同样适用于光与才智；glitter（闪耀）侧重明亮、反复的视觉闪光。coruscate 带明显的文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sparkle is the most general term and also describes lively conversation; scintillate is especially close because it applies to both light and intellectual brilliance; glitter emphasizes bright, repeated visual reflections. Coruscate has a distinctly literary register.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“闪光”：宝石闪的是光，妙语闪的是才智。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to flashes: a jewel flashes with light, and a conversation flashes with wit.

etymology_story.zh: 由法国哲学家 Jacques Derrida（雅克·德里达）的姓氏与表示关联或追随者的后缀 -ean 构成。该词既用于描述与其思想有关的理论和方法，也用作名词指其思想的追随者。
etymology_story.en: Derridean was formed from the surname of the French philosopher Jacques Derrida with the suffix -ean, marking association or adherence. It describes ideas and methods connected with his work and also names a follower of his thought.

morphology_enriched.zh: Derrida 去掉词尾 a，加 -ean，构成 Derridean；同一形式兼作形容词和名词。名词复数为 Derrideans；相关派生词 Derrideanism 指“德里达思想或学说”，使用较少。
morphology_enriched.en: Derrida loses its final a before -ean to form Derridean, which functions as both an adjective and a noun. The plural noun is Derrideans; the less common derivative Derrideanism denotes Derrida's thought or doctrine.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deconstructive（解构的）强调分析方法，未必专指德里达；deconstructionist（解构主义的；解构主义者）强调理论立场或其支持者；poststructuralist（后结构主义的；后结构主义者）涵盖更广的思想领域。三者均不能在所有语境下替代 Derridean。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deconstructive emphasizes an analytical method without necessarily referring specifically to Derrida; deconstructionist identifies a theoretical approach or its advocates; poststructuralist covers a broader intellectual field. None is interchangeable with Derridean in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Derrida 加“关联或追随”后缀：形容词指他的思想，名词指其追随者。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Derrida plus an association suffix: the adjective points to his thought, and the noun points to a follower.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从印地语及乌尔都语的 dhotī 借入该词，用来称呼南亚传统的男式围裹衣物。借入后，它在英语中保留了这一特定服饰名称的含义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed dhoti from Hindi and Urdu dhotī as the name of a traditional South Asian men's wrapped garment. The borrowed word retained this specific clothing sense.

morphology_enriched.zh: dhoti 在现代英语中是不可进一步拆分的借词词基，复数为 dhotis。dhoti-clad（穿着托蒂的）由 dhoti 与 clad（穿着……的）组成，是复合形容词；本词没有常用的独立动词或副词派生形式。

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: waistcloth（围腰布）是较宽泛的描述性词；loincloth（遮腰布）通常指更小、覆盖更少的布；sarong（纱笼）指另一类围裹衣物，通常呈裙状。它们可用于比较或解释，但都不是 dhoti 的精确同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Waistcloth is a broader descriptive term; loincloth usually suggests a smaller garment providing less coverage; sarong names a different wrapped garment, generally worn in a skirt-like form. These are useful comparisons rather than exact synonyms for dhoti.

etymology_story.zh: 由 dopamine（多巴胺）与医学、药理学后缀 -ergic 构成，后者源于希腊语 ergon，意为“工作、作用”。该词随神经科学术语的发展而形成，用于描述多巴胺参与的神经活动及相关作用。
etymology_story.en: Dopaminergic combines dopamine with the medical and pharmacological suffix -ergic, ultimately from Greek ergon, 'work or action.' It developed as a neuroscience term for neural activity and other effects involving dopamine.

morphology_enriched.zh: dopamine 去掉词尾 e，加 -ergic，构成 dopaminergic；此处 -ergic 表示“通过某种物质发挥作用或与其作用有关的”。相关词族包括 dopamine（多巴胺）、dopaminergically（以多巴胺能方式，较少用）、antidopaminergic（抗多巴胺能的）和 nondopaminergic（非多巴胺能的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Removing final e from dopamine and adding -ergic produces dopaminergic; here -ergic means 'acting through or involving the action of a substance.' Related forms include dopamine, the less common adverb dopaminergically, antidopaminergic, and nondopaminergic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dopamine-related（与多巴胺有关的）范围最广；dopamine-mediated（由多巴胺介导的）明确强调多巴胺的中介作用；dopamine-releasing（释放多巴胺的）只强调释放功能。它们与 dopaminergic 的对应程度取决于所修饰的是神经元、信号传递还是药物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dopamine-related is the broadest expression; dopamine-mediated specifically identifies dopamine as the mediator; dopamine-releasing describes only the release function. Their equivalence to dopaminergic depends on whether the context concerns neurons, signaling, or drugs.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dopamine 加表示“作用”的 -ergic：多巴胺参与发挥作用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dopamine plus the 'action' suffix -ergic: dopamine is involved in doing the work.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 ēdūcere，意为“引出、带出”，由 ē-（向外）与 dūcere（引导）组成。英语保留了“把内在之物引出来”的基本意象，并将其用于激发潜能和推导意义或结论。
etymology_story.en: Educe comes from Latin ēdūcere, 'to lead or draw out,' formed from ē-, 'out,' and dūcere, 'to lead.' English retained the image of bringing something out and applied it to revealing latent qualities and deriving meanings or conclusions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 educe 作为整体动词词基；历史上可分析为 ē-（向外）与 duc-（引导）。词形有 educes、educed、educing；派生词包括 eduction（引出；推导）、educible（可引出的；可推导出的）和 eductive（引出的；推导的），这些派生词多用于正式或专业语境。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats educe as a whole verb base; historically it contains ē-, 'out,' and duc-, 'lead.' Its inflected forms are educes, educed, and educing; derivatives include eduction, 'drawing out or derivation,' educible, 'capable of being drawn out or inferred,' and eductive, 'drawing out or deriving.' These derivatives chiefly occur in formal or specialist contexts.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: elicit（引出）通常指获得回应、信息或反应；evoke（唤起）侧重激起感情、记忆或意象；deduce（推断）侧重依据事实或前提进行推理。educe 是较少用的正式词，核心是把隐含或潜在的内容引出来。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Elicit usually means obtaining a response, information, or reaction; evoke emphasizes bringing feelings, memories, or images to mind; deduce emphasizes reasoning from facts or premises. Educe is an uncommon formal word centered on drawing out something latent or implicit.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: e- 向外，duc- 引导：把潜能引出来，把结论推出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: E- means 'out' and duc- means 'lead': lead a hidden ability or an implicit conclusion out into view.

etymology_story.zh: Exempla 保留了拉丁语 exemplum（样本、例子、范例）的中性复数形式；exemplum 与表示“取出”的 eximere 有词源联系，体现“取出一个样本”的思路。在中世纪的布道与文学传统中，这类“例子”尤其发展为传达道德教训的短故事。
etymology_story.en: Exempla preserves the Latin neuter plural of exemplum, meaning a sample, example, or model; exemplum is etymologically connected with eximere, meaning to take out, suggesting a sample taken out for inspection. In medieval preaching and literature, such examples became especially associated with short stories conveying moral lessons.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是借入英语的复数形式：exemplum → exempla；历史上可分析为 exempl-（词干）+ -a（拉丁语中性复数词尾），但 -a 不是英语中普遍适用的复数后缀。相关词族包括 exemplum、exempla、example（例子；举例说明）、exemplar（典范）、exemplary（堪称典范的；警戒性的）、exemplarily（典范地）、exemplarity（典范性）、exemplify（举例说明）、exemplification（例证；例示）、exemplificatory（用于例示的）；这些词并非都直接由 exempla 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed plural: exemplum → exempla. Historically, it consists of exempl- (the stem) + -a (the Latin neuter plural ending), but -a is not a generally productive English plural suffix. The related family includes exemplum, exempla, example, exemplar, exemplary, exemplarily, exemplarity, exemplify, exemplification, and exemplificatory; these are not all direct derivatives of exempla.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Examples（例子）最宽泛，不一定包含叙事或教训；illustrations（说明性例证）强调帮助理解；parables（寓言式说理故事）通常通过类比传达道理。Exempla 特别适用于修辞、历史与布道语境，可指被当作道德或论证依据的故事和事例。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Examples is the broadest term and need not involve a story or lesson; illustrations emphasize making something clear; parables usually communicate lessons through analogy. Exempla is especially associated with rhetoric, history, and preaching, where stories or cases provide moral instruction or argumentative support.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 取出多个“例子”来讲道理：一个 exemplum，多个 exempla。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Take out examples to make a point: one exemplum, several exempla.

etymology_story.zh: Exemplum 借自拉丁语 exemplum，原有“样本、例子、范例”等含义，与表示“取出”的 eximere 有词源联系。英语保留了它的学术色彩，并用它指修辞中的例证，尤其是中世纪布道中用于劝诫的短故事。
etymology_story.en: Exemplum was borrowed from Latin exemplum, meaning a sample, example, or model, and is etymologically connected with eximere, meaning to take out. English retained its learned character and used it for rhetorical examples, especially the instructive short stories associated with medieval sermons.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 exemplum 视为整体借词；历史结构为 exempl-（词干）+ -um（拉丁语中性单数词尾），复数为 exempla。相关词族包括 example（例子；举例说明）、exemplar（典范）、exemplary（堪称典范的；警戒性的）、exemplarily（典范地）、exemplarity（典范性）、exemplify（举例说明）、exemplification（例证；例示）、exemplificatory（用于例示的）；这些词与 exemplum 同源，并非都由它在现代英语中直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, exemplum is treated as a whole borrowed word. Its historical structure is exempl- (the stem) + -um (the Latin neuter singular ending), with the plural exempla. Related words include example, exemplar, exemplary, exemplarily, exemplarity, exemplify, exemplification, and exemplificatory; they share its etymological family but are not all direct modern English derivatives of it.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Example（例子）可指任何说明性事例；anecdote（轶事）强调简短、有趣或有启发性的叙事；parable（寓言式说理故事）通常借助类比传达教训。Exemplum 强调故事或事例被用作说理、劝诫或论证的依据。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An example is any illustrative case; an anecdote is a brief narrative that is interesting or revealing; a parable usually teaches through analogy. An exemplum emphasizes the use of a story or case as a vehicle for instruction or argument.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从一般道理中“取出一个例子”：exemplum 是用来说明道理的故事或事例。

etymology_story.zh: Fluorosis 是由表示氟的 fluor- 与源自希腊语的病理状态后缀 -osis 构成的医学术语。Fluor- 所属的词源链可追溯到拉丁语 fluere（流动）：萤石曾被用作助熔剂，使冶炼材料更易流动。
etymology_story.en: Fluorosis is a medical formation combining fluor-, referring to fluorine, with -osis, a Greek-derived suffix for a condition or disease. The fluor- family ultimately traces to Latin fluere, meaning to flow, because fluorspar was used as a flux to help materials flow during smelting.

morphology_enriched.zh: fluor-（氟）+ -osis（病理状态）→ fluorosis；对应形容词为 fluorotic（氟中毒的；氟沉着症的）。相关词族包括 fluorine（氟）、fluoride（氟化物）、fluoridate（向……加氟）、fluoridation（加氟）、fluorinated（经氟化的）和 fluorination（氟化）；这些词共享氟相关词基，不能把它们都理解为 fluorosis 的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: fluor- (fluorine) + -osis (a pathological condition) → fluorosis; the corresponding adjective is fluorotic. Related words include fluorine, fluoride, fluoridate, fluoridation, fluorinated, and fluorination. These share a fluorine-related base rather than all being derivatives of fluorosis.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Chronic fluoride poisoning（慢性氟中毒）是强调长期过量暴露的近义表达；dental fluorosis（氟斑牙）和 skeletal fluorosis（氟骨症）分别指牙齿与骨骼受累的类型。Fluoride toxicity（氟化物毒性或毒性作用）范围更广，也可涉及急性毒性，不能在所有语境中替换 fluorosis。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chronic fluoride poisoning is a near-equivalent that emphasizes prolonged excessive exposure; dental fluorosis and skeletal fluorosis identify tooth-related and bone-related forms. Fluoride toxicity is broader and can include acute toxic effects, so it is not interchangeable with fluorosis in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fluor- 指氟，-osis 指病变：氟暴露过量形成的病理状态。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fluor- means fluorine and -osis signals a disorder: a condition caused by too much fluoride.

etymology_story.zh: Fumigant 属于 fumigate（熏蒸）的词族，其词干可追溯到拉丁语 fumigare（用烟熏），与 fumus（烟）有关。随着防治技术的发展，词义从烟熏延伸到使用气体或蒸气杀灭有害生物，不要求实际产生可见的烟。
etymology_story.en: Fumigant belongs to the family of fumigate, whose stem traces to Latin fumigare, meaning to expose to smoke, and ultimately to fumus, meaning smoke. As pest-control methods developed, the meaning extended to treatment with gases or vapors, without requiring visible smoke.

morphology_enriched.zh: fumig-（熏蒸词干，与 fumigate 对应）+ -ant（表示作用物或性质的后缀）→ fumigant，可作名词和形容词。词族包括 fumigate（熏蒸）、fumigates／fumigated／fumigating（动词变化形式）、fumigation（熏蒸处理）、fumigator（熏蒸人员或设备）及 fumigatory（熏蒸用的，较少见）；fume（烟气；冒烟）是相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: fumig- (the stem associated with fumigate) + -ant (a suffix forming agent nouns or adjectives) → fumigant, used as both a noun and an adjective. The family includes fumigate, its inflections fumigates, fumigated, and fumigating, plus fumigation, fumigator, and the less common adjective fumigatory; fume is a related word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Pesticide（农药；有害生物防治剂）按防治用途分类，不限作用形式；insecticide（杀虫剂）专指针对昆虫的药剂；disinfectant（消毒剂）主要针对微生物。Fumigant 强调通过气体或蒸气发挥作用，因此与这些类别可能交叉，但并非完全同义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pesticide classifies a substance by its pest-control purpose, regardless of how it acts; insecticide specifically targets insects; disinfectant primarily targets microorganisms. Fumigant emphasizes action through gas or vapor, so it can overlap with these categories without being an exact synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由 fume“烟气”联想到熏蒸：fumigant 是靠气体或蒸气起作用的药剂，也可表示“有熏蒸作用的”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link it to fume: a fumigant works through gas or vapor, and fumigant can also describe that action.

etymology_story.zh: Geocentric 由源自希腊语 gē（地球、大地）的 geo- 与表示“以……为中心”的 -centric 构成，后者最终源自希腊语 kentron（尖点；中心）。它既用于描述把地球置于宇宙中心的历史模型，也用于现代科学中以地球中心为参照点的测量。
etymology_story.en: Geocentric combines geo-, from Greek gē meaning Earth or land, with -centric, ultimately from Greek kentron meaning a point or center. It describes both historical models that place Earth at the center of the universe and modern measurements referenced to Earth's center.

morphology_enriched.zh: geo-（地球）+ -centric（以……为中心的）→ geocentric。直接相关形式包括 geocentrically（以地球为中心地）、geocentrism（地心说；地心观）、geocentricity（以地球为中心的性质）和 geocentrist（地心说支持者）；geocentre／geocenter（地心）是相关名词，分别采用英式和美式拼写。
morphology_enriched.en: geo- (Earth) + -centric (having a specified center) → geocentric. Related forms include geocentrically, geocentrism, geocentricity, and geocentrist. Geocentre and geocenter are the British and American spellings of the related noun meaning Earth's center.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Earth-centered（以地球为中心的）是最直接的释义性近义表达；Ptolemaic（托勒密体系的）特指某一历史地心体系，范围更窄；heliocentric（日心的）则是常用对照词，表示以太阳为中心。现代地心坐标只是选择地球中心作为参照点，并不意味着接受地心说。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Earth-centered is the closest plain-language equivalent; Ptolemaic refers more narrowly to a particular historical geocentric system; heliocentric is a contrasting term meaning Sun-centered. Using geocentric coordinates in modern science simply selects Earth's center as a reference point and does not imply belief in a geocentric universe.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo-＝地球，centric＝居中：把地球或地球中心设为参照。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Geo- means Earth and centric means centered: put Earth, or its center, at the reference point.

etymology_story.zh: 该词在中古英语时期借自中古法语，与 gorge（喉咙）同源，最初指保护喉部的甲片。后来也用于颈部饰物和鸟类喉部的彩色羽斑，几个义项都围绕喉颈位置展开。参见 [《韦氏词典》](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/gorget)。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English from Middle French and is related to gorge, meaning 'throat'; its earliest English use referred to throat armour. Later uses include neck ornaments and coloured throat patches on birds, all linked by their location. See [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/gorget).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中把 gorget 作为完整词基处理，不按英语词缀强行拆分。屈折形式：gorgets（复数）；派生形式：gorget + -ed → gorgeted（戴有护喉甲的；具有明显喉斑的）。gorge 是历史相关词，并非现代构词时可以直接替换的词基。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gorget is treated as a whole base rather than divided into productive English affixes. Inflection: gorgets, the plural; derivative: gorget + -ed → gorgeted, meaning wearing a gorget or having a distinctive throat patch. Gorge is historically related, rather than an interchangeable modern base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bevor（下脸及喉部护甲）通常还保护下巴或下半张脸；neck guard（护颈装具）范围更广，也可指现代防护用品；throat patch（喉斑）是描述鸟类该部位色斑的普通表达。它们分别对应 gorget 的不同义项，不能跨义项替换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bevor usually protects the chin or lower face as well as the throat; neck guard is broader and can describe modern protective equipment; throat patch is a plain descriptive equivalent for the bird marking. These alternatives match different senses of gorget and are not interchangeable across them.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“喉部”这个位置：保护它的是护喉甲，装饰它的是颈饰，染亮它的是喉斑。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to the throat: armour protects it, an ornament decorates it, and a bird's coloured patch highlights it.

Hoof originally names an animal's foot, providing the physical image behind the dancing expression. See [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/hoofer).

morphology_enriched.zh: hoof（跳舞）+ -er（从事某活动的人）→ hoofer；复数为 hoofers。相关词族：hoof（蹄；步行；跳舞），hooves 或 hoofs（名词复数），hoofed（有蹄的；动词过去式及过去分词），hoofing（步行或跳舞；动词现在分词）。hoof it 是“步行前往”的固定表达。
morphology_enriched.en: Hoof ('dance') + -er ('a person who performs an activity') → hoofer; plural: hoofers. Related family: hoof, a noun meaning an animal's foot and an informal verb meaning to walk or dance; hooves or hoofs, noun plurals; hoofed, an adjective or past-tense and past-participle form; and hoofing, the -ing form, also used for walking or dancing. Hoof it is a fixed expression meaning to travel on foot.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dancer（舞者）是范围最广的中性词；tap dancer（踢踏舞演员）明确限定舞种；hoofer 带非正式的舞台行话色彩，常让人联想到职业舞者扎实、利落的脚步功夫。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dancer is the broad, neutral term; tap dancer specifies the dance style; hoofer is informal theatrical language that often suggests a working professional with strong, lively footwork.
