etymology_story.zh: 该词由 swing（在不同状态或位置之间转换）与 man（人）构成，把“来回转换”的形象用于体育角色。它在篮球中指可转换后卫与前锋位置的球员，在棒球中常指可转换先发与后援角色的投手。
etymology_story.en: Swingman combines swing, in the sense of moving between alternatives, with man, applying that image to sporting roles. In basketball it denotes a player who moves between guard and forward positions; in baseball it commonly denotes a pitcher who alternates between starting and relief work.

morphology_enriched.zh: swing（转换）＋man（人）→ swingman，是复合名词；复数为 swingmen，man 变为 men，通常读作 /ˈswɪŋmən/。也可写作 swing man；没有常用的直接派生动词、形容词或副词，名词用于修饰另一名词时不必另列为形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Swing + man forms the compound noun swingman. Its plural is swingmen, with man changing to men; the plural is commonly pronounced /ˈswɪŋmən/ as well. The spaced spelling swing man also occurs. There are no established common directly derived verbs, adjectives, or adverbs; attributive noun use does not by itself establish a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: guard-forward（锋卫球员）是篮球义最接近的对应说法；wing（侧翼球员）强调场上位置，不保证能兼任两个位置；utility player（多位置球员、工具人）范围更广，在棒球中通常指能守多个野手位置的球员，不等于先发后援两用投手。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Guard-forward is the closest basketball equivalent. Wing emphasizes an area or positional grouping and does not necessarily imply competence at both positions. Utility player is broader; in baseball it usually means a player who fields several positions, rather than a pitcher who both starts and relieves.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: swing＝“两边切换”：篮球切换锋卫，棒球切换先发与后援。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture someone swinging between two roles: guard and forward in basketball, starter and reliever in baseball.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由源于希腊语的 theo-（神）和 -crat（统治者）构成，属于与 theocracy（神权政治）相关的政治词族。词义既可指凭宗教权威掌权的人，也可指主张这种统治方式的人。
etymology_story.en: The word combines Greek-derived theo-, meaning 'god', with -crat, meaning 'ruler', and belongs to the political vocabulary associated with theocracy. It can describe either someone exercising religious government or someone advocating it.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：theo-（神）+ -crat（统治者或某种统治制度的支持者）。复数：theocrats（神权统治者；神权政治支持者）。主要同根词：theocracy（神权政治；神权国家）、theocracies（复数）、theocratic（神权政治的）、theocratical（同义形容词，较少用）、theocratically（以神权政治方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: theo- ('god') + -crat ('ruler or supporter of a form of rule'). Plural: theocrats. The principal related forms are theocracy, theocracies, theocratic, the less common adjective theocratical, and the adverb theocratically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: religious ruler（宗教统治者）是宽泛的近义表达；cleric（神职人员）强调宗教身份，不一定拥有政治权力；clericalist（教权主义者）主张扩大教会或神职人员的公共影响，但未必支持完整的神权政治。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Religious ruler is a broad near-equivalent; cleric identifies a religious office without necessarily implying political power; clericalist describes someone favoring church or clerical influence, which need not amount to full theocracy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: theo- 是“神”，-crat 是“统治者”：把宗教权威变成统治权力的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Theo- means 'god' and -crat means 'ruler': connect religious authority with governing power.

morphology.text: toco-（与生育酚同族） + trien-（三个双键） + -ol（醇类名称词尾） → tocotrienol（生育三烯酚）。

etymology.text: 现代生物化学命名沿用生育酚类名称，并用 trien- 标出侧链上的三个双键；英语以 tocotrienol 称呼这一相关化合物。

usage_note: 生物化学名称。与 tocopherol 相近，但侧链结构不同；不能省略 trien- 后仍当作同一化合物。

senses.meaning_zh: 生育三烯酚；侧链含三个碳碳双键的一类维生素E化合物
senses.meaning_en: a vitamin E compound with three carbon–carbon double bonds in its side chain
senses.english_definition: A tocotrienol is one of a group of vitamin E compounds whose side chains contain three carbon–carbon double bonds.

senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测定了几种植物油中的生育三烯酚含量。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是在 tocopherol（生育酚）的命名基础上形成的现代生物化学名称，其中 trien- 标示侧链上的三个双键。其更早的命名背景与生育酚最初因生殖功能研究而得名有关，但这段命名史本身并不表示生育三烯酚具有已获证实的生育功效。
etymology_story.en: This modern biochemical name was formed on the naming pattern of tocopherol, with trien- identifying three double bonds in the side chain. The older naming background concerns the reproductive research that gave tocopherol its name; that history does not itself establish a fertility benefit for tocotrienols.

morphology_enriched.zh: 名称结构：toco-（沿用生育酚类名称的构词成分）+ tri-（三）+ -en-（指示碳碳双键）+ -ol（含羟基化合物的命名词尾）；这里的羟基属于酚羟基。复数：tocotrienols（生育三烯酚类）。常见形式：α-/β-/γ-/δ-tocotrienol（α、β、γ、δ型生育三烯酚）、tocotrienol-rich（富含生育三烯酚的）、tocotrienol-containing（含生育三烯酚的）。tocopherol（生育酚）是相关化合物名称，并非本词的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Name structure: toco- (retained from tocopherol naming) + tri- ('three') + -en- (indicating carbon–carbon double bonds) + -ol (a hydroxyl-bearing compound ending); the hydroxyl group here is phenolic. The plural is tocotrienols. Common forms include α-, β-, γ-, and δ-tocotrienol, tocotrienol-rich, and tocotrienol-containing. Tocopherol names a related compound rather than a derivative of this word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 本词没有完全等义的常用单词。vitamin E compound（维生素E化合物）是较宽泛的描述；tocopherol（生育酚）属于相关类别，但侧链饱和；tocochromanol（生育色原烷醇类化合物）是涵盖生育酚和生育三烯酚等的上位名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact single-word synonym. Vitamin E compound is a broader description; tocopherol names a related class with a saturated side chain; tocochromanol is an umbrella term covering tocopherols, tocotrienols, and related compounds.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 tri-＝三：生育“三烯”酚的侧链有三个双键。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor on tri- meaning 'three': a tocotrienol has three double bonds in its side chain.

etymology_story.zh: 英语 Jurassic 借自法语 jurassique，名称来自欧洲的汝拉山脉。那里受到研究的岩层使这一地名成为地质名称，后来也用于指形成这些岩层的地质时期。
etymology_story.en: English Jurassic was borrowed from French jurassique, a name derived from the Jura Mountains in Europe. Studied rock formations there gave the geographical name a geological use, which also came to identify the corresponding period of time.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代可辨结构：Jura（汝拉山）+ 形容词命名形式 -ssic；实际词形经法语 jurassique 借入，不能把 -assic 当作可自由使用的英语后缀。Jurassic 可直接作形容词，也可名词化为 the Jurassic（侏罗纪；侏罗系）。常见组合：Early/Middle/Late Jurassic（早／中／晚侏罗世）、Lower/Middle/Upper Jurassic（下／中／上侏罗统）、Jurassic-age（侏罗纪时代的）；没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable modern structure: Jura (the mountain name) + the adjectival naming form -ssic; the actual spelling entered through French jurassique, and -assic is not a freely productive English suffix. Jurassic functions as an adjective and as the noun the Jurassic. Common combinations include Early/Middle/Late Jurassic, Lower/Middle/Upper Jurassic, and Jurassic-age; there are no common verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Jurassic-age（侏罗纪时代的）强调年代归属；of the Jurassic（属于侏罗纪的）是直接释义性表达；Mesozoic（中生代的）范围更广，还包括三叠纪和白垩纪，不能与 Jurassic 完全互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Jurassic-age emphasizes geological age; of the Jurassic is a direct explanatory equivalent; Mesozoic is broader, also including the Triassic and Cretaceous, so it is not interchangeable with Jurassic.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 汝拉山的岩层给侏罗纪命名：地名 Jura → 地质名 Jurassic。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The Jura Mountains supplied the name: Jura as a place becomes Jurassic as a geological label.

etymology_story.zh: Brae 经中古英语和苏格兰语的相关形式传下，通常追溯至古诺尔斯语 brá（睫毛）。其语义与“眉缘、边缘”的形象相联系，发展为陡岸或山坡等地形意义。

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：brae 是不可再作实用拆分的单纯词，没有可识别的常用前后缀。复数：braes（山坡）。复合词：brae + side → braeside（山坡侧面；也见于地名）。没有常用的动词、形容词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: brae is a simple base without useful productive prefix or suffix divisions. Its plural is braes. The compound brae + side gives braeside, meaning a hillside or the side of a slope and also appearing in place names. There are no common verb, adjective, or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: slope（斜坡）最通用，可指任何倾斜地面；hillside（山坡）明确指山丘的侧面；bank（斜岸；土坡）常指河岸、路旁等较陡的坡面。Brae 带有鲜明的苏格兰或英格兰北部地域色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Slope is the general term for inclined ground; hillside specifically means the side of a hill; bank often denotes a steeper slope beside water or a road. Brae adds a distinctly Scottish or northern English regional flavor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把山坡想成大地隆起的眉缘：一道 brae，向上爬。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the brow-like edge of the land: a brae is a slope you can climb.

etymology_story.en: English borrowed fusilier from French, where fusil named a flintlock firearm and -ier identified someone using it. The title survived in certain infantry regiments after their original weapons had been replaced.

morphology_enriched.zh: 借词内部结构：法语 fusil（燧发枪）+ -ier（使用者；从事者）；英语通常把 fusilier 作为完整词使用。复数：fusiliers（燧发枪兵；燧发枪团成员）；拼写变体：fusileer。相关词：fusil（燧发枪，历史词）、fusillade（连续齐射；猛烈连发），后二者属于相关词族，不是从现代英语 fusilier 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: Internal borrowed structure: French fusil ('flintlock firearm') + -ier ('user or practitioner'); English normally treats fusilier as a complete borrowed word. Its plural is fusiliers, and fusileer is a spelling variant. Related vocabulary includes the historical noun fusil and fusillade, meaning a sustained burst or volley of gunfire; these are related words rather than direct modern English derivatives of fusilier.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Infantryman is the broader term and does not specify a regimental title; rifleman may identify a weapon type or a particular military title; musketeer chiefly describes a historical soldier armed with a musket and is not interchangeable with fusilier in every context.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再作常规词缀分析的单纯词 strath；复数为 straths。地名 Strathspey 由 strath + Spey（斯佩河）构成；由该地名产生的普通名词 strathspey 指一种苏格兰舞蹈及其舞曲。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, strath is a simplex noun without a productive prefix–suffix breakdown; its plural is straths. The place name Strathspey combines strath with Spey, the river name; the common noun strathspey, derived from that place name, denotes a Scottish dance and its music.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: valley（谷地）是最宽泛的词；glen（苏格兰的山谷）通常较狭窄；dale（谷地）多见于英国地域用语和地名。strath 特别突出宽阔、谷底较平坦的河谷地貌。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Valley is the broadest term; glen usually suggests a narrower Scottish valley; dale is especially associated with British regional usage and place names. Strath specifically emphasizes a broad river valley with a relatively flat floor.

etymology_story.en: Footsie originated as an affectionate diminutive of foot. In play footsie, it came to describe discreet flirtation through touching feet and later extended figuratively to covert political or commercial dealings.

morphology_enriched.zh: foot（脚）+ 亲昵小称结尾 -sie → footsie；这里的结尾属于带玩笑色彩的构词形式，不是可随意套用的常规后缀。相关形式有拼写变体 footsy、复数 footsies，以及固定表达 play footsie；基础词 foot 的复数为 feet。
morphology_enriched.en: Foot + the affectionate diminutive ending -sie forms footsie; this is a playful formation rather than a freely productive suffix pattern. Related forms include the spelling variant footsy, the plural footsies, and the fixed expression play footsie; the base noun foot has the plural feet.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: flirtation（调情）泛指表达爱慕的互动，不限于碰脚；collusion（串通）更明确地指秘密且不正当的合作；cozying up（刻意套近乎）强调拉近关系，未必已经达成合作。play footsie 用轻佻的形象暗示隐秘往来。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Flirtation covers expressions of attraction beyond touching feet; collusion more explicitly denotes secret, improper cooperation; cozying up emphasizes cultivating closeness without necessarily reaching an agreement. Play footsie uses a playful image to suggest discreet dealings.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 dibble 是单纯词，名词转作动词时词形不变。常用词形为 dibbles、dibbled、dibbling；派生词 dibbler 指打穴器或使用这种工具的人，构成为 dibble 去末尾 e 后加 -er；dibber 是相关工具名。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, dibble is a simplex word, with unchanged conversion from noun to verb. Its regular forms are dibbles, dibbled, and dibbling; dibbler, formed by dropping final e before adding -er, denotes the tool or its user. Dibber is a related name for the tool.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: dibber（打穴器）与名词 dibble 基本同义；plant（种植）泛指把植物或种植材料放入土中；sow（播种）专指播下种子。动词 dibble 强调利用尖头工具打出的单个种植孔。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Dibber is essentially synonymous with the tool noun dibble; plant broadly means to put plants or planting material into the ground; sow specifically concerns seeds. The verb dibble emphasizes individual planting holes made with a pointed tool.

etymology_story.zh: 现代 bodge 通常被认为是 botch“粗劣地修补；做砸”的变体；botch 可追溯至中古英语表示修补的词。bodge 在英式口语中既可强调做工差，也可强调利用现有材料临时应付。
etymology_story.en: Modern bodge is generally regarded as a variant of botch, whose history goes back to a Middle English word for patching or repairing. In informal British English, bodge can emphasize either poor workmanship or an improvised way of getting something to work temporarily.

morphology_enriched.zh: bodge 是单纯词，动词与名词同形。词形包括 bodges、bodged、bodging；bodge 去末尾 e 加 -er 得 bodger，可指粗劣施工或修补的人，但 bodger 另有传统制椅工的专门含义；相关复合形式有 bodge job（粗劣或凑合的活儿）。
morphology_enriched.en: Bodge is a simplex word used as both verb and noun. Its forms include bodges, bodged, and bodging; dropping final e and adding -er gives bodger, which can mean someone who works or repairs badly, although bodger also has a specialized traditional chairmaking sense. A related compound is bodge job.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: botch（做砸）更直接强调结果糟糕；patch up（临时修补）强调修复到暂时可用；jury-rig（利用现有材料临时组装）强调应急创造性。bodge 可涵盖粗劣施工和勉强奏效的权宜修补。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Botch more directly emphasizes a bad result; patch up stresses temporary repair; jury-rig highlights improvised construction using available materials. Bodge can cover both poor workmanship and a makeshift repair that succeeds for the moment.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先拼起来，能用再说：这次临时凑合可能奏效，也可能把活儿做糟。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Piece it together and get it working: a bodge may work temporarily, but the workmanship can be poor.

etymology_story.zh: mesic 由源自希腊语 mesos“中间”的构词成分与形容词后缀 -ic 构成。在生态学中，“居中”专指水分条件介于干旱和过湿之间。
etymology_story.en: Mesic was formed from a combining element based on Greek mesos, meaning middle, and the adjective suffix -ic. In ecology, this middle position specifically concerns moisture conditions between dry and very wet.

morphology_enriched.zh: mes-（中间，meso- 在此词中的形式）+ -ic（形容词后缀）→ mesic。相关同根词有 mesophyte（中生植物）和 mesophytic（中生植物的；适应中等水分条件的）；它们是共享构词成分的词，不是直接在 mesic 后加后缀形成的。
morphology_enriched.en: Mes- meaning middle, the form of meso- used here, combines with -ic to form mesic. Related words sharing this combining element include mesophyte, a plant adapted to moderate moisture, and mesophytic, describing such plants or their adaptations; these are not formed by adding suffixes directly to mesic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: moderately moist（中度湿润的）是最直接的通俗释义；moist（湿润的）只说明存在一定水分，不明确限定生态范围；mesophytic（中生的）主要描述植物或植被的适应性。mesic 可直接描述生境的水分条件。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moderately moist is the closest plain-language equivalent; moist indicates moisture without specifying an ecological range; mesophytic primarily describes the adaptation of plants or vegetation. Mesic can directly characterize the moisture conditions of a habitat.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mes- 表示“中间”：把水分刻度停在干与湿之间。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mes- means middle: place the moisture gauge midway between dry and wet.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经中古英语来自法国城市 Arras（阿拉斯）的名称；这座城市曾以精美挂毯闻名。法语中表示“阿拉斯织物”的说法使产地名逐渐成为挂毯的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English from the name of Arras, a French city famous for fine tapestries. French expressions referring to cloth from Arras helped turn the place name into a name for the product.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 arras 是不可再作常用词根、词缀切分的整体名词，词尾 -s 并非复数标记；规则复数为 arrases。罕见历史形容词 arrased = arras + -ed，意为“装饰着挂毯的”；没有常用的动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, arras is a whole noun without a useful productive root-and-affix division; its final -s is not a plural ending. The regular plural is arrases. The rare historical adjective arrased consists of arras + -ed and means decorated with tapestry; there are no common derived verbs or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tapestry is the closest and more widely used equivalent; wall hanging includes decorations made from other materials; curtain emphasizes screening or covering. Arras has a distinctly historical or literary tone.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Arras was famous for tapestry: the place name became the product name.

etymology_story.zh: Escherichia 是以德国儿科医生兼细菌学家 Theodor Escherich（特奥多尔·埃舍里希）的姓氏命名的新拉丁语属名。他对肠道细菌的早期研究促成了后来称为大肠埃希菌的细菌的发现。
etymology_story.en: Escherichia is a New Latin genus name honoring the German pediatrician and bacteriologist Theodor Escherich. His early research on intestinal bacteria led to the identification of the organism later named Escherichia coli.

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名结构为 Escherich（人名）+ -ia（新拉丁语属名结尾）→ Escherichia。属名首字母大写，规范科学排版使用斜体；Escherichia coli 可缩写为 E. coli。Escherichia coli 等是分类学名称组合，并非该词的派生词；普通英语中没有常用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: The naming structure is Escherich, a surname, + -ia, a New Latin genus-name ending. The genus name begins with a capital letter and is italicized in scientific typography; Escherichia coli can be abbreviated to E. coli. Such species names are taxonomic combinations, not derivatives, and the word has no common ordinary-English derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有可完全替换的日常近义词。Escherichia spp. 指该属中未具体指明的多个物种；E. coli（大肠埃希菌）只指其中一个物种；coliforms（大肠菌群）是更广的检测分类，不能与属名等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday synonym. Escherichia spp. refers to unspecified species within the genus; E. coli names just one species; coliforms is a broader testing category and is not interchangeable with the genus name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Escherich 的名字加上 -ia：把埃希菌属与研究它的科学家联系起来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Escherich + -ia: connect the bacterial genus with the scientist it honors.

senses.collocation_zh: 《申命记》；《申命记》中的一段经文
senses.sentence_en: The lecturer discussed a passage from Deuteronomy.
senses.sentence_zh: 讲师讨论了《申命记》中的一段经文。

etymology_story.zh: 书名经拉丁语 Deuteronomium 来自希腊语 Deuteronomion，传统上理解为“第二律法”。这一名称与《申命记》17:18 中希伯来语“这律法的抄本”的希腊语译法有关，后来也契合本书重申律法的内容。
etymology_story.en: The title comes through Latin Deuteronomium from Greek Deuteronomion, traditionally understood as second law. It reflects the Greek rendering of a Hebrew expression meaning a copy of this law in Deuteronomy 17:18 and also suits the book's restatement of the law.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常将 Deuteronomy 作为完整书名学习；历史构词成分为 deutero-（第二）与希腊语 nomos（律法），不宜把它解释为普通英语中临时拼合的词。主要相关形式：Deuteronomic、Deuteronomical（《申命记》的），Deuteronomist（《申命记》相关文本的作者或编者），Deuteronomistic（与相关编纂传统有关的），Deuteronomism（相关神学或思想传统）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats Deuteronomy as a complete book title. Its historical components are deutero-, meaning second, and Greek nomos, meaning law, rather than a freely assembled ordinary-English formation. Principal related forms are Deuteronomic and Deuteronomical, relating to the book; Deuteronomist, an author or editor associated with its textual tradition; Deuteronomistic, relating to that editorial tradition; and Deuteronomism, its associated theological outlook.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: the Book of Deuteronomy（《申命记》）是完整称呼；the Fifth Book of Moses（《摩西第五经》）是传统别称，强调其在摩西五经中的位置。这些是同一部书的不同名称，而非一般意义上的近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The Book of Deuteronomy is the fuller designation; the Fifth Book of Moses is a traditional alternative emphasizing its position within the five books of Moses. These are alternative titles for the same work rather than ordinary synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: deutero-＝第二，nomos＝律法：再次申说律法 →《申命记》。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Deutero- means second and nomos means law: think of the law being stated again.

etymology_story.zh: 这一形状义借自法语 lune（月亮），其源头是拉丁语 luna（月亮）。月牙的外形使该词被用于命名平面及球面上的相似几何区域。
etymology_story.en: The shape term comes from French lune, meaning moon, ultimately from Latin luna. The outline of a crescent moon supplied the name for similar regions in plane and spherical geometry.

morphology_enriched.zh: lune 在现代英语中是整体词，复数为 lunes；semi-（半）+ lune → semilune（半月形物）。同源相关词包括 lunar（月亮的）、lunate（月牙形的）、lunule（小月牙形物）、lunular（小月牙形的）、lunation（朔望月周期）和 semilunar（半月形的）；这些词并非都由英语 lune 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Lune is a whole word in modern English, with the plural lunes; semi-, meaning half, + lune gives semilune, a half-moon-shaped object. Etymologically related forms include lunar, relating to the moon; lunate, crescent-shaped; lunule, a small crescent-shaped structure; lunular, shaped like a small crescent; lunation, a lunar cycle; and semilunar, half-moon-shaped. These are not all direct derivatives of English lune.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crescent（月牙形）是最通用的形状词；meniscus（月牙形物、弯月面）有特定物理或解剖用法；lens（透镜形区域）在几何中通常指两个圆盘相交的中间区域。lune 强调月牙形区域，不能随意与 lens 互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crescent is the most general shape word; meniscus has specialized physical or anatomical uses; lens usually names the central overlap of two disks in geometry. Lune emphasizes a crescent-shaped region and is not freely interchangeable with lens.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 lunar（月亮的）与 lune 相连：月牙轮廓就是 lune 的形状线索。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link lune with lunar: the moon's crescent supplies the shape.

senses.meaning_en: A sleeveless protective garment with front and back panels and open or fastened sides.

etymology_story.zh: tabard 经中古英语借自古法语 tabart，原指一种外罩衣，其更早来源尚不确定。这个名称既保留在纹章礼仪服饰中，也用于现代具有类似覆盖结构的工作罩衣。
etymology_story.en: Tabard entered Middle English from Old French tabart, a name for an outer garment; its earlier origin is uncertain. The name survives both in heraldic ceremonial dress and in modern protective garments with a similar covering structure.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tabard 是整体服装名词，复数为 tabards。tabard + -ed → tabarded，是较少见的形容词，意为“穿着罩衣的”；常见搭配 protective tabard 和 herald's tabard 属于短语，并非派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tabard is a whole garment noun, with the plural tabards. Tabard + -ed produces the uncommon adjective tabarded, meaning wearing a tabard. Expressions such as protective tabard and herald's tabard are phrases rather than derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: surcoat（外罩衣）最接近历史服饰义，常与盔甲相关；apron（围裙）主要覆盖身体前部；smock（宽松罩衫）通常覆盖更完整，也可能有袖子。tabard 的现代义突出前后覆盖、两侧较开放的结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Surcoat is closest to the historical sense and is often associated with armor; apron mainly protects the front of the body; smock usually provides fuller coverage and may have sleeves. A modern tabard characteristically covers the front and back while remaining relatively open at the sides.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象肩上连着前后两片布：礼仪时展示纹章，工作时保护衣服。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture front and back panels joined at the shoulders: they display heraldic arms or protect working clothes.

morphology.text: divis-（divide 的词干变体，分、除） + -or（施事或工具名词结尾） → divisor（除数），记作“用来除的数”。

etymology.text: 晚期中古英语从法语 diviseur 或拉丁语 divisor 借入，与拉丁语 dividere“分开”相连；从“分开者”联想到把一个数分成份的数。

usage_note: 在 12 ÷ 3 = 4 中，3 是 divisor，12 是 dividend，4 是 quotient。本卡学除法算式中的除数。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 divisor，意为“分割者”，经法语或直接进入中古英语；它与 dividere“分开、分配”同源。数学意义把“分割者”具体化为用来除另一个数的数。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin divisor, meaning a divider, entering Middle English through French or directly from Latin; it is related to dividere, meaning to separate or distribute. In mathematics, the divider became the number by which another number is divided.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按 divis-（与 divide“分、除”对应的拉丁词干变体）+ -or（表示施事者或工具的名词后缀）理解；这是继承的拉丁构词结构，并非现代英语直接用 divide 加后缀造出的词。复数为 divisors；相关词族包括 divide（分、除）、division（分割；除法）、divider（分隔物）、divisible（可整除的）、indivisible（不可分的）和 divisibility（可整除性）。
morphology_enriched.en: The structure is divis-, a Latin stem related to divide, + -or, a suffix naming an agent or instrument; this is an inherited Latin formation rather than a new English formation from divide. The plural is divisors; related family members include divide, division, divider, divisible, indivisible, and divisibility.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: factor（因数）与 divisor 在整数整除意义上通常同义；denominator（分母）是在分数写法中表示除数的数，但名称取决于表达形式；divider（分隔物、分割者）通常指人或工具，不是数学术语 divisor 的常规替代词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Factor is usually synonymous with divisor when exact integer division is intended. Denominator names the divisor as represented in a fraction. Divider normally means a person or device that separates things and is not the usual mathematical substitute for divisor.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 divisor 看成“执行 divide 的数”：普通除法中是除数，恰好除尽时也是因数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of a divisor as the number doing the dividing: it is the divisor in a calculation and a factor when integer division is exact.

etymology_story.zh: 来自拉丁语 artemisia，可追溯到古希腊语的植物名称 artemisia，传统上与女神 Artemis（阿耳忒弥斯）的名字相联系。后来 Artemisia 成为植物属名，英语小写 artemisia 可指该属的一株植物。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin artemisia, ultimately from a Greek plant name traditionally associated with the goddess Artemis. Artemisia later became a botanical genus name, while lowercase artemisia can name an individual plant belonging to that genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜作整体借词处理，不宜强拆为具有现成意义的英语词根和词缀；作普通可数名词时，复数为 artemisias。相关名称包括 Artemisia（蒿属，学名）和 artemisinin（青蒿素，以蒿属植物名称为基础形成的化学名称）；wormwood（苦艾）、mugwort（艾类植物）和 sagebrush（蒿灌木）是该属部分植物的俗名，并非形态派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, artemisia is best treated as a whole borrowed base rather than divided into productive English roots and affixes; its count-noun plural is artemisias. Related names include the scientific genus name Artemisia and artemisinin, a chemical name based on the plant name; wormwood, mugwort, and sagebrush are common names for particular members of the genus, not morphological derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wormwood（苦艾）、mugwort（艾类植物）和 sagebrush（蒿灌木）都是相关植物名称，但各自只涵盖蒿属的部分成员；artemisia 的范围更广，不能在所有语境中与这些名称互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wormwood, mugwort, and sagebrush name particular plants or groups within Artemisia. Artemisia is the broader term, so these names are not interchangeable synonyms in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Artemis 的名字作线索，连接 Artemisia“蒿属”；女神联想帮助记词，不代表植物具有神奇功效。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Use the name Artemis as a cue for Artemisia, the plant genus; the goddess association is a memory aid, not a claim about the plant's effects.

senses.meaning_zh: 麻鸭；翘鼻麻鸭等体型较大、羽色对比鲜明的鸭类
senses.meaning_en: a large duck, typically with strongly contrasting plumage
senses.english_definition: A shelduck is a fairly large duck, often with clearly contrasting patches of colour, that belongs to a group closely related to geese.
senses.collocation_en: a common shelduck; a pair of shelducks
senses.collocation_zh: 一只翘鼻麻鸭；一对麻鸭
senses.sentence_en: A pair of shelducks was feeding on the mudflats.
senses.sentence_zh: 一对麻鸭正在潮滩上觅食。

etymology_story.zh: 由旧时或方言中的 sheld“杂色的、有斑块的”和 duck“鸭”合成。这个名称突出了麻鸭羽毛上鲜明的色块对比。
etymology_story.en: Shelduck combines the old or dialectal word sheld, meaning pied or marked with patches of colour, with duck. The name highlights the contrasting patches in the bird's plumage.

morphology_enriched.zh: sheld（旧词：杂色的）+ duck（鸭）→ shelduck（麻鸭），属于复合名词；复数通常为 shelducks，也可用集合式 shelduck。相关词有 sheldrake（雄麻鸭，也可泛指麻鸭）和 shelduckling（麻鸭幼鸟，较少见）；common shelduck（翘鼻麻鸭）和 ruddy shelduck（赤麻鸭）是物种名称。
morphology_enriched.en: Sheld, an old word meaning pied, + duck forms the compound noun shelduck. The usual plural is shelducks, though collective shelduck also occurs; related forms include sheldrake, meaning a male shelduck or sometimes a shelduck generally, and the less common shelduckling, meaning a young shelduck. Common shelduck and ruddy shelduck are species names.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sheldrake（雄麻鸭；也可泛指麻鸭）与 shelduck 有意义重叠，但可能特别指雄鸟；duck（鸭）是范围更广的上位词；common shelduck（翘鼻麻鸭）特指一个物种，不能涵盖所有麻鸭。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sheldrake overlaps with shelduck but can specifically identify a male. Duck is the broader category, while common shelduck identifies one particular species rather than every shelduck.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sheld＝杂色，duck＝鸭：看见醒目的羽色块，就联想到麻鸭。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sheld means pied and duck means duck: picture a duck with bold patches of contrasting colour.

forms: 可数名词；复数 wallahs。常接在表示工作或物品的词后。
family: boxwallah 流动小贩；tea wallah 卖茶或端茶的人

morphology.text: wallah 整词作为独立词素记忆；box + wallah → boxwallah（提箱售货的小贩），前面的词提示此人做什么。

etymology.text: 来自印地语 vālā，表示负责某事或与某事相关的人；进入英语后常跟在职业、物品名称后称呼从业者。

usage_note: 多见于南亚英语或带印度背景的文字，常与工作词连用，如 tea wallah。称呼有地域和时代色彩，注意语境。

senses.meaning_zh: 从事某项工作或与某事有关的人，常用于南亚语境或非正式表达
senses.meaning_en: a person who does a particular job or is associated with a particular activity
senses.english_definition: A wallah is someone who does a particular kind of work or is connected with a particular thing, especially in South Asian contexts.
senses.collocation_en: a chai wallah; a rickshaw wallah
senses.collocation_zh: 卖茶人；人力车夫
senses.sentence_en: The chai wallah poured hot tea into small glasses.
senses.sentence_zh: 卖茶人把热茶倒进小玻璃杯里。

senses.meaning_zh: 我向真主发誓；我保证，确实如此，常用于非正式口语
senses.meaning_en: an expression meaning 'I swear by God', used to emphasize that something is true
senses.english_definition: Some speakers say wallah to swear by God that what they are saying is true, or informally to emphasize their sincerity.
senses.collocation_en: wallah, I swear; wallah, it's true
senses.collocation_zh: 我向真主发誓；我发誓，这是真的
senses.sentence_en: Wallah, I left your keys on the table.
senses.sentence_zh: 我发誓，我把你的钥匙放在桌上了。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“某类人”的 wallah 来自印地语及乌尔都语的 -vālā／-wālā，表示与某种事物或活动有关的人，经南亚英语进入英语。表示“我发誓”的 wallah 则另来自阿拉伯语 wa-llāh“以真主之名起誓”，两个用法来源不同。
etymology_story.en: The occupational noun comes from Hindi and Urdu -vālā or -wālā, identifying someone associated with a thing or activity, and entered English through South Asian usage. The oath wallah has a separate origin in Arabic wa-llāh, meaning by God.

morphology_enriched.zh: 名词 wallah 可独立使用，也常作复合词后项：chai（茶）+ wallah → chai wallah（卖茶人），rickshaw（人力车）+ wallah → rickshaw wallah（人力车夫）；复数为 wallahs，另有拼写变体 wala、walla。感叹词 wallah 在英语中通常作为整体借词使用，没有常规屈折变化；其阿拉伯语来源可分析为 wa-（誓言用介词）+ Allāh（真主）。
morphology_enriched.en: The noun wallah can stand alone or serve as the second element of a compound: chai + wallah gives chai wallah, and rickshaw + wallah gives rickshaw wallah. Its plural is wallahs, with spelling variants including wala and walla. The interjection is normally an uninflected borrowing in English; its Arabic source consists of the oath particle wa- plus Allāh, meaning God.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词义可比较 worker（工作者）、vendor（小贩）和 specialist（专门人员）：wallah 根据前面的词确定具体身份，本身不表示一定是售货者或专家。感叹词义接近 I swear（我发誓）或 honestly（说真的），但 wallah 保留了宗教誓言的来源，实际语气随语境变化。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the noun, compare worker, vendor, and specialist: the preceding word identifies the role, and wallah itself does not necessarily mean a seller or an expert. As an interjection, it resembles I swear or honestly, while retaining its origin as a religious oath; its force depends on context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 职业用法记成“X wallah＝做 X 的人”；誓言用法另记“以真主之名保证”，两条来源分开记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For occupations, remember X wallah as the person who does X; separately, remember the oath as a promise made by God.

morphology.text: butterfly（蝴蝶）+ fish（鱼）→ butterflyfish（蝴蝶鱼）：把艳丽的鱼联想成水中的蝴蝶。

etymology.text: 英语用 butterfly 和 fish 合成鱼名；像蝴蝶般醒目的色彩，是记住这个名字的线索。

usage_note: 指蝴蝶鱼科的热带海鱼；写作一个词。不是会飞的蝴蝶。

senses.meaning_zh: 蝴蝶鱼：通常色彩鲜艳、身体侧扁的热带海鱼
senses.meaning_en: a tropical marine fish with a flattened body and usually bright colours
senses.english_definition: A butterflyfish is a tropical sea fish with a thin, flattened body and usually bright colours or striking patterns.
senses.collocation_en: a copperband butterflyfish; a pair of butterflyfish
senses.collocation_zh: 一条铜带蝴蝶鱼；一对蝴蝶鱼
senses.sentence_en: A pair of butterflyfish swam above the coral.
senses.sentence_zh: 一对蝴蝶鱼在珊瑚上方游动。

etymology_story.zh: 由英语 butterfly“蝴蝶”和 fish“鱼”合成，名称把这类鱼的鲜艳颜色和醒目花纹比作蝴蝶。它是根据外观形成的描述性鱼名。
etymology_story.en: The name combines butterfly and fish, comparing the fishes' bright colours and striking patterns to those of butterflies. It is a descriptive name based on appearance.

morphology_enriched.zh: butterfly（蝴蝶）+ fish（鱼）→ butterflyfish（蝴蝶鱼），属于复合名词；复数通常仍为 butterflyfish，强调不同种类时也可用 butterflyfishes。常见物种名称包括 copperband butterflyfish（铜带蝴蝶鱼）、raccoon butterflyfish（浣熊蝴蝶鱼）和 threadfin butterflyfish（丝鳍蝴蝶鱼）；没有常用的动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Butterfly + fish forms the compound noun butterflyfish. The plural is usually butterflyfish, while butterflyfishes can emphasize different species. Species names include copperband butterflyfish, raccoon butterflyfish, and threadfin butterflyfish; there are no commonly used derived verbs or adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chaetodontid（蝴蝶鱼科鱼类）是较专业的对应名称；reef fish（珊瑚礁鱼类）范围更广；angelfish（神仙鱼）是常见的比较对象，海水神仙鱼虽外形相近，却属于不同的鱼类科，不能作为同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chaetodontid is a more technical equivalent for a fish of the butterflyfish family. Reef fish is much broader. Angelfish is a useful comparison, but marine angelfishes belong to a different family and are not synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: butterfly + fish：把色彩鲜艳、身体扁薄的鱼想成“海里的蝴蝶”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Butterfly + fish: picture a brightly coloured, flattened fish as a butterfly of the sea.

morphology.text: corrie（冰斗）+ -s（复数）→ corries（多个冰斗）；corrie 以 ie 结尾，直接加 s。

etymology.text: 单数 corrie 借自苏格兰盖尔语 coire，原意是“锅”；想象群山中像大锅一样的凹地。

usage_note: 苏格兰地貌用语；corries 是复数，要说 corries are。指冰川侵蚀形成的盆状山谷。

senses.meaning_zh: 冰斗；山坡上由冰川侵蚀形成的碗状洼地
senses.meaning_en: Bowl-shaped mountain hollows formed by glacial erosion
senses.english_definition: Corries are large, bowl-shaped hollows in mountainsides that were formed by glaciers.
senses.collocation_en: glacial corries; steep-sided corries
senses.collocation_zh: 冰川冰斗；四壁陡峭的冰斗

etymology_story.zh: 单数 corrie 借自苏格兰盖尔语 coire，意为“锅；大锅”，后来用于形容山间形似锅的洼地。地貌学中，它指冰川侵蚀形成的冰斗。
etymology_story.en: The singular corrie comes from Scottish Gaelic coire, meaning a kettle or cauldron, and was applied to mountain hollows resembling such vessels. In geomorphology, it denotes a hollow formed by glacial erosion.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：corrie + 复数词尾 -s → corries；corrie 以 -ie 结尾，直接加 -s，不改为 -ies。常用词形为单数 corrie 和复数 corries，没有常用的直接派生动词或形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: corrie + plural -s → corries. Because corrie ends in -ie, simply add -s; do not replace its ending with -ies. The usual forms are singular corrie and plural corries, with no common directly derived verb or adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cirques（冰斗）是国际地貌学中常用的对应术语；cwms（山间凹谷；冰斗）源自威尔士语，在冰川地貌语境中可指同类地形；bowls（碗状洼地）只描述形状，不必由冰川形成。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Cirques is the usual international geomorphological equivalent; cwms is a Welsh-derived term that can denote the same landform in glacial contexts; bowls describes the shape more generally and does not necessarily imply glacial formation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 山坡被冰川挖成“大锅”：一口是 corrie，多口是 corries。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture glaciers scooping giant cauldrons into a mountainside: one corrie, several corries.

senses.meaning_en: To certify something for the Kitemark or, more broadly, against a standard
senses.english_definition: To kitemark something means to certify that it meets a particular standard, especially through the BSI Kitemark scheme.

etymology_story.zh: Kitemark 由 kite（风筝）和 mark（标志）组成，名称来自该认证标志近似风筝的外形。它最初作为英国标准认证标志的名称使用，后来也产生了表示“授予认证”的动词用法。
etymology_story.en: Kitemark combines kite and mark, referring to the certification symbol's kite-like outline. Originally the name of a British standards certification mark, it subsequently developed a verbal use meaning to certify.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：kite + mark → Kitemark，属于复合名词；复数为 Kitemarks。名词转用为动词时常写作小写 kitemark，词形包括 kitemarks、kitemarked、kitemarking；kitemarked 也可作分词形容词，表示“已获认证的”。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: kite + mark → Kitemark, a compound noun; its plural is Kitemarks. Conversion produces the verb, often written lowercase as kitemark, with forms kitemarks, kitemarked, and kitemarking. Kitemarked also functions as a participial adjective meaning certified.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: certification mark（认证标志）是上位通称，不限于英国标准协会；quality mark（质量标志）强调质量认可，具体认证要求因制度而异；certify（认证）对应动词用法，但不专指风筝标志认证。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Certification mark is the broader category and is not restricted to BSI; quality mark emphasizes recognition of quality, with requirements varying by scheme; certify corresponds to the verbal use but does not specifically imply Kitemark certification.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: kite 是风筝，mark 是标志：看到“风筝”，想到标准认证。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Kite + mark: a kite-shaped symbol anchors the idea of standards certification.

senses.meaning_zh: 毛茛属植物；尤指栽培观赏毛茛
senses.meaning_en: A plant of the buttercup genus, especially an ornamental cultivated variety
senses.english_definition: A ranunculus is a plant belonging to the buttercup genus, often grown in gardens for its brightly coloured flowers.

etymology_story.zh: ranunculus 来自拉丁语 rānunculus，字面意为“小青蛙”，是 rāna（青蛙）的指小形式，后来成为植物名称。这个名称通常被解释为与许多毛茛类植物生长在青蛙出没的潮湿环境有关。
etymology_story.en: Ranunculus comes from Latin rānunculus, literally a little frog, a diminutive of rāna, meaning frog, which became a plant name. The name is traditionally explained by the damp habitats shared by many buttercups and frogs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 ranunculus 作为完整借词处理，不按现代英语词缀拆分；常见复数为 ranunculi 或 ranunculuses。历史结构可联系 rāna（青蛙）及拉丁语指小形式；相关植物学词有 Ranunculaceae（毛茛科）和 ranunculaceous（毛茛科的），它们共享拉丁语词干，并非普通英语中的简单加缀派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ranunculus is normally treated as a complete loanword rather than a combination of productive English affixes; its plurals include ranunculi and ranunculuses. Historically, it belongs to a Latin diminutive formation related to rāna, frog. Related botanical terms include Ranunculaceae, the buttercup family, and ranunculaceous, belonging to that family; these share a Latin stem rather than representing simple everyday English suffixation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: buttercup（毛茛）是常用通俗名称，尤其让人想到黄花野生种；crowfoot（水毛茛；毛茛类植物）是该属部分植物的传统名称。园艺中的 ranunculus 常指花瓣繁多的观赏品种，三者不能在所有语境中互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Buttercup is the familiar common name, especially associated with yellow-flowered wild species; crowfoot is a traditional name for certain members of the genus. In gardening, ranunculus often refers to ornamental varieties with many petals, so these names are not interchangeable in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “小青蛙”住湿地，旁边长毛茛：这是词源联想，不是现代英语拆词。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a little frog beside buttercups in damp ground: an etymological link, not a modern English word split.

senses.meaning_en: A Normandy brandy distilled from fermented apples or a mixture of apples and pears
senses.english_definition: Calvados is a brandy made in Normandy in France by distilling fermented apple juice, sometimes with fermented pear juice.
senses.collocation_en: a glass of calvados; aged calvados

senses.sentence_zh: 晚餐后，他们端上了一小杯卡尔瓦多斯白兰地。

etymology_story.zh: calvados 借自法语，以法国诺曼底的 Calvados（卡尔瓦多斯）地区命名。这个地名后来转指当地著名的苹果白兰地。
etymology_story.en: Calvados was borrowed from French and takes its name from Calvados in Normandy. The place name came to denote the region's celebrated apple brandy.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：calvados 是由地名转成酒名的完整借词，没有可分析的现代英语词根与词缀，词尾 -s 不是复数标记。它通常作不可数名词；a calvados 可指一份或一杯这种酒，没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: calvados is a complete loanword transferred from a place name, with no productive English root-and-affix division; its final -s is not a plural ending. It is normally uncountable, although a calvados can mean one serving or glass. It has no common directly derived word family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: apple brandy（苹果白兰地）是更宽泛的类别，不限定诺曼底产地；cider brandy（苹果酒蒸馏白兰地）强调由发酵苹果酒蒸馏而成；brandy（白兰地）范围最大，也包括葡萄等其他水果制成的蒸馏酒。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Apple brandy is a broader category without the Normandy restriction; cider brandy emphasizes distillation from fermented cider; brandy is the broadest term and includes spirits distilled from grapes and other fruits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把地图上的 Calvados 连到酒杯：诺曼底地名变成苹果白兰地名。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect Calvados on the map to a glass: a Normandy place name becomes the name of its apple brandy.

etymology_story.zh: combi 是与 combination（组合）相关的截短形式，用来表示多种功能合为一体。它用于组合式设备和客货两用交通工具，并在某些地区发展出“小型公共汽车”的含义。
etymology_story.en: Combi is a shortened form associated with combination, expressing the joining of functions in one unit. It has been applied to combined-function appliances and passenger-and-goods vehicles, and in some regions has developed the meaning minibus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：combination 截短为 combi，不宜再拆成 com- 与 -bi；名词复数为 combis。它可作名词，也可在名词前表示“组合式的”，如 combi boiler、combi oven、combi aircraft；这类定语用法也有词典按组合形式处理。相关基础词族包括 combine（组合）、combines、combined、combining、combination（组合）、combinations 和 combinational（组合的），它们不是由 combi 再派生而来。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: combination is shortened to combi; do not reanalyse it as com- plus -bi. The noun plural is combis. It also appears before nouns with the meaning combined-function, as in combi boiler, combi oven, and combi aircraft; some dictionaries classify this attributive use as a combining form. The related base family includes combine, combines, combined, combining, combination, combinations, and combinational; these are not derivatives formed from combi itself.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: combination unit（组合式装置）是描述多功能设备的通称；dual-purpose（两用的）强调两种用途，而 combi 不一定仅限两种；minibus（小型公共汽车）只对应 combi 在部分地区的交通工具含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Combination unit is a general expression for equipment joining functions; dual-purpose emphasizes two uses, whereas combi need not be restricted to two; minibus matches only the regional passenger-vehicle sense of combi.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: combi 联想 combination：一个设备或交通工具，把几种用途合在一起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link combi to combination: one appliance or vehicle brings several uses together.

etymology_story.zh: 来自荧光颜料商标 Day-Glo，由 day（白天）和 glow（发亮）的变体 Glo 组成，突出其在日光下仍然极其鲜亮的特点。这个商标名后来也被用来形容类似的醒目荧光色。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the fluorescent-pigment trademark Day-Glo, combining day with Glo, a respelling of glow, to emphasize brightness in daylight. The trademark also developed a descriptive use for similarly vivid fluorescent colours.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：day（白天）＋ Glo〔glow（发亮）的商标化拼写〕→ DayGlo。常见拼写有 Day-Glo、DayGlo 和描述性用法中的 dayglo；名词可直接转作形容词，无常用的后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: day + Glo, a trademark respelling of glow → DayGlo. Spellings include Day-Glo, DayGlo, and descriptive lowercase dayglo; the noun also functions adjectivally, with no established common family of suffixed derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fluorescent（荧光的）强调吸收光后发出可见光的性质；neon（霓虹般鲜艳的）常作日常色彩描述，不保证具有荧光性；luminous（发光的、明亮的）范围更广，也可描述暗处可见的光亮。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fluorescent emphasizes the property of absorbing light and emitting visible light; neon commonly describes intensely bright colours without guaranteeing fluorescence; luminous is broader and can describe brightness visible in darkness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: day＋glow：白天也亮得跳出来 → 醒目的荧光色。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Day + glow: colour that seems to glow even in daylight → conspicuous fluorescence.

meaning: 处于绝境（用于 in extremis）
aliases: 处于绝境（用于 in extremis）

morphology.text: in + extremis → in extremis（在极端困境中）；这是完整借用的拉丁语短语，两个部分一起记。

etymology.text: 整个短语从拉丁语借入英语；字面描画“处在最极端的境地”，于是用来表达危急关头。

usage_note: 正式或文学用语，通常必须连同 in 使用；可指极端困境，也可指临终，本卡教“处于绝境”。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用了拉丁语完整短语 in extremis，字面意为“在最末端的境况中”，传统上尤其指临终。其意义后来扩展到极端危难和决定成败的最后关头。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the complete Latin phrase in extremis, literally meaning 'in the furthest or final circumstances' and traditionally referring especially to the approach of death. Its meaning broadened to extreme danger and the last possible moment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中应整体记忆 in extremis，不把 extremis 当作可独立自由使用的普通英语词。历史上，in 是拉丁语介词，extremis 是 extremus（最外面的、最后的）的夺格复数形式；它与 extreme、extremity 有历史联系，但没有独立的常用英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, learn in extremis as a fixed phrase rather than treating extremis as an ordinary independent word. Historically, in is a Latin preposition and extremis is an ablative plural form of extremus, meaning outermost or last; it is historically related to extreme and extremity but has no common independent English derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: in dire straits（陷入严重困境）强调处境艰难，不一定危及生命；at death's door（濒临死亡）只对应临终义；at the last minute（在最后一刻）强调时间迟，不一定伴随危机。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: In dire straits emphasizes serious difficulty without necessarily implying danger to life; at death's door corresponds specifically to the dying sense; at the last minute emphasizes late timing without necessarily implying a crisis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想 extreme（极端）：in extremis＝已经到了处境或时间的极限。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect it with extreme: in extremis means reaching the limit of danger, life, or available time.

usage_note: 通常大写 A，也见全大写 ANZAC；本卡指澳大利亚或新西兰军人。Anzac Day 是相关纪念日名称。

etymology_story.zh: ANZAC 源自 Australian and New Zealand Army Corps（澳大利亚和新西兰军团）的首字母缩略形式，于第一次世界大战期间形成，并因加里波利战役而广为人知。名称随后用于相关军人、纪念传统及 Anzac biscuit（澳新军团饼干）等名称。
etymology_story.en: ANZAC originated during the First World War as an acronym for Australian and New Zealand Army Corps and became widely associated with the Gallipoli campaign. The name subsequently extended to the servicemen, commemorative traditions, and names such as Anzac biscuit.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Australian＋New Zealand＋Army＋Corps → A＋NZ＋A＋C → ANZAC，作为单词读出；Anzac 是常见词形。可数名词复数为 Anzacs；常见相关表达包括 Anzac Day、Anzac biscuit 和 Anzac spirit，无常用的后缀派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Australian + New Zealand + Army + Corps → A + NZ + A + C → ANZAC, pronounced as a word; Anzac is a common spelling. The count-noun plural is Anzacs; related expressions include Anzac Day, Anzac biscuit, and Anzac spirit, with no common family of suffixed derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: serviceman（军人）是较宽泛的称呼，不限定国籍或战争；Australian or New Zealand soldier（澳大利亚或新西兰士兵）直接说明国籍，但不一定带有 Anzac 的历史与纪念内涵；digger（澳新士兵）是亲切、非正式的称呼。以上词语均不对应饼干义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Serviceman is broader and does not specify nationality or conflict; Australian or New Zealand soldier states nationality without necessarily carrying Anzac's historical and commemorative associations; digger is a familiar, informal term for an Australian or New Zealand soldier. None of these equivalents applies to the biscuit sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: A＋NZ＋Army Corps：澳大利亚与新西兰并肩组成军团；人、纪念日和饼干都围绕这个名称展开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A + NZ + Army Corps: Australia and New Zealand serving together; the soldiers, remembrance day, and biscuits share that name.

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语和盎格鲁法语 palefrei 传入，源头是晚期拉丁语 paraveredus，指额外配备的驿马。词义后来发展为供舒适、日常骑乘的马，尤其与中世纪贵族出行有关。
etymology_story.en: The word entered through Middle English and Anglo-French palefrei, ultimately from Late Latin paraveredus, an extra post horse. Its meaning developed into a horse for comfortable, ordinary riding, particularly associated with medieval aristocratic travel.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 palfrey 是不可再作有效词缀拆分的单纯词，复数为 palfreys，无常用的派生词族。历史来源 paraveredus 可追溯至希腊语 para-（在旁、额外）与拉丁语 veredus（驿马），但这些成分不是现代 palfrey 中仍可自由组合的词素。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, palfrey is a simple word without a productive root-and-affix breakdown; its plural is palfreys, and it has no common derivative family. Its historical source paraveredus combines Greek para-, meaning beside or additional, with Latin veredus, a post horse, but these are not freely combinable elements within modern palfrey.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: riding horse（骑乘马）是最宽泛的上位表达；mount（坐骑）强调供某人骑乘的动物，可用于多种场景；steed（骏马、坐骑）带文学或英雄叙事色彩。palfrey 特别突出历史背景和温驯、舒适的骑乘用途。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Riding horse is the broadest equivalent; mount emphasizes an animal ridden by someone and suits many contexts; steed is literary and often suggests heroic riding. Palfrey specifically evokes a historical setting and a gentle horse suited to comfortable travel.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 用场景记：中世纪贵妇骑着温驯的马出行 → palfrey。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a medieval lady travelling on a gentle riding horse → palfrey.

meaning: 具有警戒作用的（鲜艳体色等）

usage_note: 生物学用语，常修饰 coloration 或 markings；既强调醒目，也强调警告捕食者的作用。

senses.sentence_en: The frog's bright colours are aposematic, warning predators that its skin contains toxins.
senses.sentence_zh: 这只蛙鲜艳的体色具有警戒作用，向捕食者表明它的皮肤含有毒素。

etymology_story.zh: 英国动物学家爱德华·巴格纳尔·波尔顿于1890年提出这一术语，采用希腊语 apo-（离开）和 sēma（标记、信号）等成分。其核心意思是“发出使敌害远离的信号”，尤其用于解释动物醒目的警戒色。
etymology_story.en: The British zoologist Edward Bagnall Poulton introduced the term in 1890 using Greek elements including apo-, meaning away, and sēma, meaning sign or signal. Its central idea is signalling to keep enemies away, especially through conspicuous warning coloration.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词：apo-（远离）＋ semat-〔希腊语 sēma“信号”的词干〕＋ -ic（形容词后缀）→ aposematic。主要词族：aposematism（警戒现象、警戒作用），aposematically（以警戒信号的方式）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern learned formation: apo- (away) + semat- (the stem of Greek sēma, sign or signal) + -ic (adjective suffix) → aposematic. The principal word family includes aposematism, the phenomenon of warning signalling, and aposematically, meaning in a warning-signalling manner.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: warning（警告性的）是宽泛的日常表达；warning-coloured（具有警戒色的）专指颜色，范围比 aposematic 窄；conspicuous（醒目的）只表示容易被发现，不必具有警告功能，也不一定与防御能力相关。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Warning is a broad everyday equivalent; warning-coloured refers specifically to colour and is narrower than aposematic; conspicuous means easy to notice without necessarily implying a warning function or a connection with defensive traits.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: apo-＝远离，semat-＝信号：鲜艳体色举起“别吃我”的警告牌。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Apo- means away and semat- means signal: bright colours display a 'do not eat me' warning.

pronunciation.note: 按所列词典的读音标注；重音以 ˈ 标出。

forms: 可数名词；复数 poppadoms；异拼 poppadum，复数 poppadums。
family: poppadum 同义异拼；poppadoms 复数

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；poppadom + -like → poppadom-like（像薄脆饼的），用 -like 表示相似。

etymology.text: 借自泰米尔语 pappadam；记住南亚餐桌上那片薄而酥脆的圆饼，就能把声音和食物连起来。

usage_note: 通常是很薄的圆形南亚脆饼，炸制或烤制，常配酸辣酱；与柔软厚实的 naan 不同。

senses.meaning_zh: 南亚薄脆饼，通常用豆粉制成
senses.meaning_en: a thin, crisp South Asian wafer, usually made from pulse flour
senses.english_definition: A poppadom is a thin, crisp food made usually from lentil or other pulse flour and served with South Asian meals.
senses.collocation_en: crispy poppadoms; poppadoms and chutney
senses.collocation_zh: 酥脆的南亚薄饼；南亚薄脆饼配酸甜酱
senses.sentence_en: We shared some poppadoms and chutney while waiting for our curry.
senses.sentence_zh: 等咖喱上桌时，我们分着吃了一些薄脆饼和酸甜酱。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用了南印度语言中 pappaṭam 一类的食物名称，泰米尔语和马拉雅拉姆语中都有相关形式。这个名称随南亚饮食进入英语，指通常用豆粉制成、经油炸或烘烤后食用的薄脆饼。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the food name from South Indian forms such as pappaṭam, found in Tamil and Malayalam. The name entered English with South Asian cuisine and denotes a thin wafer, usually made from pulse flour and fried or roasted.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中视为不可再作有用拆分的借词：poppadom；复数为 poppadoms。常见异体拼写包括 poppadum、pappadum 和 papadum；没有常用的派生词族，poppadom-like 只是可临时组成的“像薄脆饼的”。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, poppadom is a borrowed base with no useful internal morphological division; its plural is poppadoms. Common spelling variants include poppadum, pappadum, and papadum; there is no established everyday derivational family, and poppadom-like is merely a possible descriptive formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: papad：相关的南亚食品名称，通常可指同类薄脆饼，但地区用法和品种可能不同；cracker：泛指咸味薄脆食品，不能准确表达南亚饮食特色；wafer：强调薄片形状和酥脆质地，也可指甜食。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Papad is a related South Asian food name that often denotes the same kind of wafer, although regional usage and varieties differ; cracker is a broader term for a crisp savoury food; wafer emphasizes thinness and crispness and can also describe sweet foods.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 借词整体记：咖喱旁边那片薄、脆、通常用豆粉做成的圆饼。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the borrowed word as a whole: the thin, crisp, usually pulse-flour wafer beside a curry.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标按词典读音转写为 IPA。

forms: trows；过去式、过去分词 trowed；现在分词 trowing。
family: betrow 信任（罕见）；trowing 现在分词；trowed 过去式

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；be-（动词前缀）+ trow（相信）→ betrow（信任，罕见用语）。

etymology.text: 经中古英语延续自古英语 trēowan（相信），与表示忠实、真实的古英语词有亲缘关系；可从“信以为真”帮助记忆。

usage_note: 古旧、文学用语，常见 I trow；现代日常英语通常用 think 或 believe。本卡教“认为”。

senses.meaning_en: to believe, think, or suppose
senses.english_definition: If you trow that something is true, you believe or suppose that it is true; this use is archaic or dialectal.
senses.collocation_en: I trow; trow not
senses.collocation_zh: 我想；我相信；不相信；认为并非如此（均为古语表达）

senses.sentence_zh: “我想他会在天黑前回来，”老人说道。

senses.pos: n. 名词（苏格兰北部岛屿民俗用语）
senses.meaning_zh: 特罗精怪，奥克尼和设得兰民间传说中的超自然生物
senses.meaning_en: a supernatural creature in the folklore of Orkney and Shetland
senses.english_definition: A trow is a supernatural creature in traditional stories from Orkney and Shetland, often described as small and mischievous.
senses.collocation_en: a mischievous trow; tales of trows
senses.collocation_zh: 顽皮的特罗精怪；关于特罗精怪的传说
senses.sentence_en: The islanders told stories of trows that came out after dark.
senses.sentence_zh: 岛民们讲述那些天黑后出来活动的特罗精怪的故事。

etymology_story.zh: 动词 trow 经中古英语传自古英语 trēowian，意为“相信、信任”，与 true 和 truth 所属的日耳曼语词族有亲缘关系。民俗名词 trow 来源不同，属于与古诺尔斯语 troll 相关的苏格兰岛屿用语。
etymology_story.en: The verb trow descends through Middle English from Old English trēowian, meaning 'believe' or 'trust', and belongs to the Germanic family associated with true and truth. The folklore noun has a separate origin in Scottish island usage related to Old Norse troll.

morphology_enriched.zh: 动词和名词在现代英语中都是独立词基，不能按同一词根解释：动词 trow → trows、trowed、trowing；名词 trow → 复数 trows。true、truth、trust 是动词的历史同源词，并非由现代 trow 加词缀直接派生；没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: The verb and noun are separate modern bases, not two meanings of one morphological root: the verb inflects as trows, trowed, and trowing, while the noun has the plural trows. True, truth, and trust are historical relatives of the verb, not direct modern derivatives formed by adding affixes to trow; there is no common modern derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: believe：现代常用词，侧重相信某事为真；suppose：侧重推测或暂时认为，语气通常较弱；troll：与名词 trow 相关的北欧民俗生物名称，但具体形象和地方传统不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Believe is the ordinary modern verb for accepting something as true; suppose suggests an assumption or tentative judgment; troll names a related creature from Scandinavian folklore, but its appearance and local traditions can differ from those of a trow.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 动词连到 true：“当作真的”就是相信；精怪名词另连到 troll，分开记忆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link the verb to true: taking something as true means believing it. Link the separate folklore noun to troll.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标按词典读音转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数名词；复数 corncrakes。
family: corn 谷物；crake 秧鸡；corncrakes 复数

morphology.text: corn（谷物）+ crake（秧鸡）→ corncrake（常出没于谷地和草丛的长脚秧鸡）。

etymology.text: 来自早期苏格兰语 cornecrake，由“谷物”和“秧鸡”两部分组成；名字把鸟与它活动的田野联系起来。

usage_note: 指一种常在高草或农田中活动、叫声响亮的秧鸡；corn 在这个名称里泛指谷物。

senses.meaning_zh: 长脚秧鸡，一种栖于高草地、叫声粗厉的秧鸡科鸟
senses.meaning_en: a secretive rail with a harsh call that lives in tall grass

senses.collocation_en: the corncrake's call; corncrake habitat

senses.sentence_zh: 我们听见高草丛中有一只长脚秧鸡在鸣叫，却看不见它。

etymology_story.zh: corncrake 由 corn“谷物”和 crake“秧鸡”组成，早期苏格兰语中已有相应形式。名称把这种鸟与谷田联系起来，而 crake 本身与模仿鸟类粗厉叫声的词有关。
etymology_story.en: Corncrake combines corn, meaning grain, with crake, a name for a rail, and corresponding forms occur in early Scots. The name associates the bird with grain fields, while crake is connected with words imitating harsh bird calls.

morphology_enriched.zh: 透明复合词：corn（谷物）+ crake（秧鸡）→ corncrake；复数 corncrakes。没有常用的派生词族；corncrake call、corncrake habitat 中的 corncrake 是作定语的名词，不构成独立的形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: A transparent compound: corn 'grain' + crake 'a rail' → corncrake; plural corncrakes. There is no common derivational family; in corncrake call and corncrake habitat, corncrake is an attributive noun rather than a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: landrail：长脚秧鸡的传统别称，指同一种鸟；crake：用于若干种秧鸡的名称，范围更广；rail：秧鸡科鸟类的统称，包含长脚秧鸡及许多其他种类。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Landrail is a traditional alternative name for the same bird; crake is used for several kinds of rails and is broader; rail is the general family-level term covering the corncrake and many other species.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: corn 谷田 + crake 秧鸡：谷草深处传来粗厉叫声的鸟。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Corn 'grain field' + crake 'rail': picture a bird rasping from deep grass beside the crops.

aliases: 轻快的多乐章室内乐曲

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标按词典读音转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数名词；复数 divertimenti 或 divertimentos。
family: divertimenti / divertimentos 复数；divertimento-like 具有嬉游曲风格的

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；divertimento + -like → divertimento-like（具有嬉游曲风格的）。

etymology.text: 借自意大利语 divertimento，原意“娱乐、消遣”，来自 divertire；更早可追到拉丁语 divertere，轻快的音乐正好供人消遣。

usage_note: 音乐术语，常指风格轻松、含数个乐章的器乐室内乐作品；不是所有娱乐音乐都叫 divertimento。

senses.meaning_zh: 嬉游曲，通常由数个乐章组成的轻快器乐作品
senses.meaning_en: a light instrumental composition, usually in several movements
senses.english_definition: A divertimento is a piece of instrumental music, usually with several movements, written in a light and entertaining style.
senses.collocation_en: a divertimento by Mozart; a divertimento for strings
senses.collocation_zh: 莫扎特的一首嬉游曲；一首弦乐嬉游曲
senses.sentence_en: The ensemble opened the concert with a divertimento by Mozart.
senses.sentence_zh: 乐团以莫扎特的一首嬉游曲拉开了音乐会的序幕。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自意大利语 divertimento，原意为“娱乐、消遣”，与 divertire“使娱乐”有关，最终可追溯到拉丁语 divertere“转向别处”。音乐名称保留了“让人从日常事务中转移注意、获得消遣”的含义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian divertimento, meaning entertainment or diversion, from the family of divertire 'to entertain', ultimately tracing back to Latin divertere 'to turn aside'. The musical term preserves the idea of turning attention away from ordinary concerns for enjoyment.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中整体视为音乐借词，不按英语词缀强行拆分；意大利语内部可分析为 diverti-（来自 divertire）+ -mento（构成名词的后缀）。英语复数为 divertimenti 或 divertimentos；divert、diversion、divertissement 是历史相关词，不是由英语 divertimento 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed musical term rather than a formation from productive English affixes; internally in Italian, it consists of diverti- from divertire plus the noun-forming suffix -mento. English plurals are divertimenti and divertimentos; divert, diversion, and divertissement are historical relatives, not direct derivatives of English divertimento.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: serenade：小夜曲，历史上常与晚间演奏有关，和嬉游曲的体裁有重叠；suite：组曲，强调若干乐章或乐曲的组合，不必轻快；cassation：古典时期的一类轻松合奏曲，与嬉游曲相近，但名称的历史使用范围更窄。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Serenade overlaps with divertimento but historically often suggests evening performance; suite emphasizes a sequence of movements or pieces without necessarily implying a light character; cassation denotes a related Classical-period ensemble work, with a narrower historical use.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“转移注意”到“消遣”：让心情轻松转个弯的音乐，就是嬉游曲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: From 'turn aside' to 'be entertained': a divertimento turns your attention toward light musical enjoyment.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标按词典读音转写为 IPA。

forms: 可数名词；复数 euphorbias；学名属名写作 Euphorbia，普通植物名可小写。
family: Euphorbiaceae 大戟科；euphorbias 复数

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；euphorbia + -like → euphorbia-like（像大戟属植物的）。

etymology.text: 来自新拉丁语，改自拉丁语 euphorbea，名称关联古代希腊医生 Euphorbus；可以把它记成一个带着医生名字的植物名。

usage_note: 可指大戟属的草本、灌木或树木；某些种类外形像仙人掌，但不能把整个属等同于仙人掌。

senses.meaning_zh: 大戟属植物，通常具有乳状汁液
senses.meaning_en: a plant of the genus Euphorbia, typically with milky sap
senses.english_definition: A euphorbia is a plant belonging to a large genus whose members typically produce milky sap and include many garden and succulent plants.
senses.collocation_en: grow euphorbias; euphorbia sap
senses.collocation_zh: 种植大戟属植物；大戟属植物的汁液

etymology_story.zh: 现代植物属名 Euphorbia 沿袭了古代以医生 Euphorbus 命名植物的传统；他是毛里塔尼亚国王尤巴二世的医生。这个人名由古代植物名称进入新拉丁语分类命名，再成为英语中大戟属植物的通称。
etymology_story.en: The botanical genus name Euphorbia continues an ancient tradition of naming a plant after Euphorbus, a physician to King Juba II of Mauretania. The personal name passed through ancient plant terminology into New Latin classification and then into English as a common name for plants of the genus.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是以人名为基础的整体借词，不宜拆成具有现代英语意义的 eu- + phorbia；复数 euphorbias。相关植物学词包括 Euphorbiaceae（大戟科）和 euphorbiaceous（大戟科的）；属名 Euphorbia 首字母大写并通常用斜体，普通植物名称 euphorbia 用小写。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a whole borrowed base ultimately founded on a personal name, not a productive English combination of eu- and phorbia; its plural is euphorbias. Related botanical formations include Euphorbiaceae, the spurge family, and euphorbiaceous, meaning belonging to that family; the genus name Euphorbia is capitalized and normally italicized, while the common noun euphorbia is lowercase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spurge：大戟属植物的常用名称，通常最接近 euphorbia；succulent：多肉植物，按储水特征划分，只有部分大戟属植物属于此类；cactus：仙人掌，某些大戟属植物外形与之相似，但二者属于不同的科，不能互作同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spurge is the usual common-name equivalent and the closest synonym; succulent describes a water-storing growth form found in only some euphorbias; cactus may resemble certain euphorbias, but cacti belong to a different family and the words are not synonyms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 医生 Euphorbus 留名植物：记住“带着医生名字的大戟属”，不硬拆词根。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A physician's name preserved in a plant: connect Euphorbus with Euphorbia rather than forcing an English root breakdown.

meaning: 旧时往返印度贸易的大商船

morphology.text: India（印度）+ man（旧时船只名称中的成分）→ Indiaman（从事印度贸易的大商船）。

etymology.text: 英语把 India 与船只名称中使用的 man 合在一起，为历史上往返印度的远洋商船命名；可联想到装载货物的长途航船。

usage_note: 历史用语，通常大写 I；常见 East Indiaman。本卡指商船，不指印度人。

senses.meaning_zh: 旧时从事印度或东印度群岛贸易的大型商船
senses.meaning_en: a large historical merchant ship trading with India or the East Indies
senses.english_definition: An Indiaman was a large merchant ship that carried goods between Europe and India or the East Indies.
senses.collocation_en: an East Indiaman; a heavily laden Indiaman
senses.collocation_zh: 一艘东印度贸易商船；一艘满载货物的印度贸易商船

senses.sentence_zh: 这艘印度贸易商船载着茶叶和香料返回伦敦。

etymology_story.zh: 由 India（印度）和 man 复合而成；man 在一些传统航海名称中可指船只。这个名称与欧洲对印度及东印度地区的远洋贸易有关，尤其常见于 East Indiaman（东印度贸易商船）这一历史称谓。
etymology_story.en: The word combines India with man, which can denote a vessel in traditional nautical names. It developed in the context of European oceanic trade with India and the East Indies, particularly in the historical term East Indiaman.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：India（印度）+ man（船只名称成分）→ Indiaman。复数为 Indiamen，词尾 man 不规则变为 men；常见组合为 East Indiaman / East Indiamen。Indian（印度的；印度人）与其共享 India 这一基础词，但不是由 Indiaman 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: India + man, used as a vessel-name element → Indiaman. The plural is Indiamen, with the irregular change man → men; common combinations include East Indiaman and East Indiamen. Indian shares the base India but is not derived from Indiaman.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: merchantman（商船）泛指用于商业运输的船只；trading vessel（贸易船）强调贸易用途；East Indiaman（东印度贸易商船）是更具体的历史名称，突出其东印度贸易背景。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Merchantman is a general term for a commercial ship; trading vessel emphasizes its commercial function; East Indiaman is a more specific historical term identifying a ship associated with East Indies trade.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: India 指贸易目的地，man 在这里指船：驶向印度贸易航线的大商船。
mnemonic_anchor.en: India names the trading destination; man names the vessel: a large merchant ship on the India trade route.

etymology.text: 通过新拉丁语医学名称进入英语，来自拉丁语 naevus（痣、胎记）；复数保留了拉丁语式的 -i 结尾。

usage_note: 医学词汇，指皮肤上的痣；naevi 是复数，搭配 are。这里只学习词义，不据此判断皮肤病变。

senses.meaning_zh: 痣；胎记样局限性皮肤病变（naevus 的复数，主要用于英式医学英语）
senses.meaning_en: moles or localized birthmark-like skin lesions; the plural of naevus
senses.english_definition: Naevi are localized marks or growths on the skin, such as moles, that result from an abnormal arrangement or accumulation of tissue cells.
senses.collocation_en: melanocytic naevi; congenital naevi
senses.collocation_zh: 黑素细胞痣；先天性痣
senses.sentence_en: The dermatologist examined the naevi on her back.
senses.sentence_zh: 皮肤科医生检查了她背上的痣。

etymology_story.zh: 单数 naevus 来自拉丁语 naevus，意为“痣、胎记”，经医学拉丁语进入英语。Naevi 保留了拉丁语第二变格名词的复数形式，后来成为英语医学术语中的常用复数。
etymology_story.en: The singular naevus comes from Latin naevus, meaning a mole or birthmark, through medical Latin. Naevi preserves the Latin second-declension plural and is used as a plural medical term in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 屈折变化：naevus → 去掉 -us，接拉丁式复数词尾 -i → naevi；这不是新词派生。相关形式：naeval（痣的，形容词）；美式拼写 nevus（单数）、nevi（复数）、neval（形容词）。
morphology_enriched.en: Inflection: naevus → replace -us with the Latin plural ending -i → naevi; this is an inflected form, not a new derivative. Related forms include naeval, an adjective meaning relating to a naevus, and the American spellings nevus, nevi, and neval.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: moles（痣）通常指色素性、尤其是黑素细胞性的痣，范围比 naevi 窄；birthmarks（胎记）强调出生时或出生后不久出现的皮肤标记，而 naevi 也可后天出现；nevi 是美式拼写，含义相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Moles usually refers to pigmented, especially melanocytic, naevi and is narrower in scope; birthmarks emphasizes marks present at birth or appearing soon afterward, whereas naevi can also develop later; nevi is the American spelling with the same meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记 naevus 是“痣”，再记 -us → -i：一个 naevus，多个 naevi。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with naevus, a mole, then switch -us to -i: one naevus, several naevi.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式读音；音标按词典读音转写为 IPA。

forms: 拉丁化生物属名；作为属名不加普通复数 -s；学名中首字母大写，通常排斜体。
family: anserine 雁的；鹅似的

morphology.text: Anser 整词作为独立词素记忆；同源联记：拉丁语 anser（鹅）+ -inus（形容词后缀）→ anserinus（鹅的），英语借入后成为 anserine（鹅的；鹅似的）。Anser 这个属名也来自拉丁语 anser。

etymology.text: 新拉丁语属名，直接来自拉丁语 anser（鹅、雁）；古老的鸟名成为现代分类学名称。

usage_note: 属名必须大写 A；本卡教动物分类名称 Anser，不把它当作单只雁的普通英文名。

senses.meaning_zh: 雁属，包括灰雁等雁类的鸟属

senses.english_definition: Anser is a genus of geese that includes the greylag goose and several related species.
senses.collocation_en: the genus Anser; Anser anser
senses.collocation_zh: 雁属；灰雁（学名）
senses.sentence_en: The greylag goose belongs to the genus Anser.

etymology_story.zh: Anser 是取自拉丁语 anser（鹅、雁）的新拉丁语动物属名。这个古老的鸟名被用于现代生物分类，以指称一组亲缘关系密切的雁类。
etymology_story.en: Anser is a New Latin zoological genus name taken from Latin anser, meaning goose. The ancient bird name was adopted into modern biological classification for a group of closely related geese.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为完整借入的属名使用，没有可用于日常英语构词的前后缀；首字母大写，科学排版通常用斜体。相关词源词族：anserine（雁的；似雁的，也可指愚笨的）、anseriform（雁形目的）、Anseriformes（雁形目）；这些词共享拉丁语 anser 词源，并非都直接由属名 Anser 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is a borrowed genus name without productive everyday English affixes; it is capitalized and normally italicized in scientific writing. Its etymological family includes anserine, meaning relating to or resembling a goose and sometimes foolish; anseriform, relating to the order Anseriformes; and Anseriformes, the order name. These share Latin anser rather than all deriving directly from the genus name.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该属名没有可完全互换的常用近义词。geese（雁；鹅）涵盖多个属，范围更广；grey geese（灰雁类）是与该属相关的常见群体称呼；waterfowl（水禽）还包括鸭、天鹅等，范围更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym for this genus name. Geese covers birds from several genera; grey geese is a common group label associated with Anser; waterfowl is broader still and also includes ducks and swans.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 拉丁语 anser 就是“鹅、雁”：古老鸟名直接变成雁属名称。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Latin anser means goose: the old bird name becomes the modern genus name.

senses.meaning_zh: 领班；负责带领一小组工人的工人
senses.meaning_en: a worker who supervises a small group of other workers
senses.english_definition: A chargehand is a worker who is responsible for supervising a small group of workers, especially in a factory or on a building site.

etymology_story.zh: 由 charge（管理、负责）和 hand（工人）在英语内部复合而成。Hand 用身体部位代指劳动者，整个词因此表示负责带领其他工人的人，主要见于英式英语。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in English from charge, meaning responsibility or supervision, and hand, meaning a worker. Hand uses a body part to stand for a working person, so the compound denotes a worker responsible for others, chiefly in British English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词：charge（管理职责）+ hand（工人）→ chargehand（领班），为复合名词。复数：chargehands；没有常用的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: charge, meaning supervisory responsibility, + hand, meaning worker, → chargehand, a compound noun. The plural is chargehands; there are no common direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: foreman（工头、领班）常指管理一组工人的负责人，职权可能更大；supervisor（主管）适用于更多行业和管理层级；team leader（组长）强调团队领导职责，不一定从事体力劳动。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Foreman often denotes the person directing a group of workers and may imply greater authority; supervisor applies across more industries and management levels; team leader emphasizes leadership of a team and need not involve manual work.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把 in charge 的 hand 连起来：负责管人的那位工人，就是领班。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A hand is a worker; the hand in charge is the chargehand.

usage_note: 地质学用语；至少两侧以断层为界的下陷地块。普通河谷不一定是 graben。

senses.meaning_zh: 地堑；两侧断层之间相对下陷的地壳块体
senses.meaning_en: a block of the earth's crust displaced downward between faults
senses.english_definition: A graben is a block of the earth's crust that lies lower than the blocks on either side because of movement along the faults that bound it.
senses.collocation_en: a fault-bounded graben; a horst-and-graben structure
senses.collocation_zh: 断层限定的地堑；地垒与地堑相间的构造
senses.sentence_en: The valley occupies a graben bounded by two major normal faults.
senses.sentence_zh: 这条山谷位于一个由两条主要正断层限定的地堑中。

etymology_story.zh: 借自德语 Graben，原义为“沟、壕沟”，与德语 graben（挖掘）相关。地质学借用这个形象，指断层之间相对下陷、外形如沟槽的地壳块体。
etymology_story.en: The term was borrowed from German Graben, meaning a ditch or trench, and is related to the German verb graben, to dig. Geology adopted the image for a relatively down-dropped block of crust between faults.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为不可再分析的德语借词使用，没有英语前后缀。复数可用 grabens 或不变的 graben；常见相关复合词为 half-graben（半地堑），指主要由一侧断层控制的不对称下陷构造；graben-like（似地堑的）是可按需构成的形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, this is an unanalyzed German loanword without English prefixes or suffixes. Its plural can be grabens or unchanged graben. A common related compound is half-graben, an asymmetric down-dropped structure controlled mainly by a fault on one side; graben-like is a transparently formed adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: fault trough（断层槽地）是接近的描述性术语；rift valley（裂谷）指地壳伸展形成的谷地，可包含一个或多个地堑；depression（洼地）只说明地势较低，不限定断层成因。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Fault trough is a close descriptive term; rift valley denotes a valley formed by crustal extension and may contain one or more grabens; depression merely identifies a low area without specifying a fault origin.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 德语原义是“沟”：两侧断层之间的地块相对下落，形成地壳上的沟槽。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The German meaning is ditch: a crustal block drops relative to its fault-bounded sides, producing a trough.

senses.english_definition: A hautboy is a wooden musical instrument that you play by blowing through a double reed; the word is an old name for an oboe.

senses.meaning_en: The musk strawberry plant or its fruit, in older horticultural usage.
senses.english_definition: A hautboy is a kind of strawberry plant with strongly scented fruit, or a strawberry from this plant.
senses.collocation_en: hautboy strawberries; hautboy plants
senses.collocation_zh: 麝香草莓果实；麝香草莓植株
senses.sentence_en: The old gardening manual recommends hautboy strawberries for their fragrance.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本旧园艺手册因麝香草莓香气浓郁而推荐种植它。

etymology_story.zh: 乐器名称来自法语 hautbois，由 haut（高的；响亮的）和 bois（木头）组成，指声音响亮的木管乐器；英语 oboe 也经意大利语追溯到同一法语名称。草莓义通常另溯法语 hautbois（高处的树林），与乐器义分属不同的命名来源。
etymology_story.en: The instrument name comes from French hautbois, combining haut, meaning high or loud, with bois, meaning wood; English oboe ultimately comes from the same French name through Italian. The strawberry name is generally traced separately to French hautbois meaning high woods, rather than to the musical instrument.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为不可再分析的借词处理，不宜拆成 haut + boy；历史结构为法语 haut + bois。复数为 hautboys，hautbois 是乐器义的另一拼写；oboe（双簧管）和 oboist（双簧管演奏者）属于相关词汇，但不是由 hautboy 加后缀形成的派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hautboy is normally treated as an unanalyzed loanword, not as haut + boy; its historical French structure is haut + bois. The plural is hautboys, and hautbois is an alternative spelling for the instrument; oboe and oboist are related vocabulary, not suffix derivatives of hautboy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: oboe（双簧管）是乐器义的现代标准名称；shawm（肖姆管）指相关但不同的早期双簧木管乐器，不能直接等同；musk strawberry（麝香草莓）对应 hautboy 的旧时园艺义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Oboe is the standard modern name for the instrument; shawm denotes a related but distinct early double-reed instrument and is not an exact synonym; musk strawberry corresponds to the older horticultural sense of hautboy.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 乐器义记作“响亮的木管”：haut＝高、响亮，bois＝木头；词尾 boy 不表示“男孩”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: For the instrument, remember loud wood: haut means high or loud, and bois means wood; the ending boy does not mean a male child.

senses.meaning_zh: 以音乐演奏为主要内容的社交聚会；小型音乐会
senses.meaning_en: A social gathering or small concert featuring musical performances.
senses.english_definition: A musicale is a social event at which people perform music, often in someone's home.
senses.collocation_en: a private musicale; an evening musicale
senses.collocation_zh: 私人音乐聚会；晚间音乐聚会
senses.sentence_en: She invited a few friends to a private musicale at her home.
senses.sentence_zh: 她邀请了几位朋友到家中参加一场私人音乐聚会。

etymology_story.zh: 此词来自法语 soirée musicale（音乐晚会）中的 musicale，原为 musical（音乐的）的阴性形式。英语在十九世纪将其用作独立名词，指以音乐演奏为中心的社交活动。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from musicale in the French phrase soirée musicale, meaning a musical evening; musicale was originally the feminine form of musical. In nineteenth-century English, it became an independent noun for a social gathering centered on musical performance.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为整体借入的名词，不能把末尾 -e 当作能自由构词的英语后缀；复数为 musicales。相关词族包括 music（音乐）、musical（音乐的；音乐剧）、musically（在音乐方面）、musician（音乐家）和 musicianship（音乐修养），它们并非全部由 musicale 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, musicale is a borrowed noun; its final -e is not a productive English suffix. Its plural is musicales. Related family members include music, musical, musically, musician, and musicianship, but these are not all direct derivatives of musicale.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: concert（音乐会）涵盖各种规模的演出；recital（独奏会；独唱会）通常突出一名演奏者、演唱者或较小的表演组合；musical soirée（音乐晚会）最接近 musicale，强调社交氛围且通常在晚间举行。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Concert is a broad term for a musical performance of any scale; recital usually highlights an individual performer or a small performing group; musical soirée is closest to musicale, emphasizing a social occasion usually held in the evening.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 soirée musicale 想到“一场以音乐为主角的聚会”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a soirée musicale: a gathering where music is the main attraction.

etymology.text: 借自德语 Siderit，上溯希腊语 sidēros（铁）；词根直接提示这是一种含铁矿物。

usage_note: 本卡教矿物义，即碳酸亚铁 FeCO3；同拼词也可指铁陨石，需按语境区分。

senses.meaning_zh: 菱铁矿，主要成分为碳酸亚铁的矿物
senses.meaning_en: A mineral consisting of iron(II) carbonate, FeCO3.
senses.english_definition: Siderite is a mineral made of iron carbonate that can be used as an iron ore.

senses.meaning_en: An iron meteorite, in older classification terminology.
senses.english_definition: In older scientific writing, a siderite is a meteorite made mainly of metallic iron and nickel.

senses.collocation_zh: 富镍铁陨石；铁陨石标本

etymology_story.zh: 此词属于十九世纪以希腊语 sidēros（铁）为基础形成的科学名称，与德语 Siderit 等形式相对应。词名突出了含铁这一特点，因此既用于碳酸亚铁矿物，也曾用于主要由铁组成的陨石。
etymology_story.en: The word belongs to nineteenth-century scientific terminology based on Greek sidēros, meaning iron, alongside forms such as German Siderit. Its reference to iron explains its use both for the iron carbonate mineral and, historically, for meteorites composed mainly of iron.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词结构为 sider-（铁）+ -ite（矿物或物质名称后缀）。常见相关形式有复数 siderites、形容词 sideritic（含菱铁矿的；与菱铁矿有关的），以及地质学术语 sideritization（菱铁矿化）；siderophile（亲铁的）共享铁的词根，但不是 siderite 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation is sider- meaning iron + -ite, a suffix used in mineral and substance names. Related forms include the plural siderites, the adjective sideritic, and the geological term sideritization; siderophile shares the iron root but is not a direct derivative of siderite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spathic iron ore（菱铁矿石）是菱铁矿的传统名称；iron carbonate（碳酸铁，此处特指碳酸亚铁）强调化学组成，并不必然指天然矿物；iron meteorite（铁陨石）只对应 siderite 的旧陨石义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spathic iron ore is a traditional name for the mineral; iron carbonate describes its chemical composition without necessarily identifying a natural mineral; iron meteorite corresponds only to the older meteoritic sense of siderite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sider-＝铁，-ite＝矿物：先记“含铁矿物”，再落实为碳酸亚铁组成的菱铁矿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Sider- means iron and -ite suggests a mineral: anchor the word to iron, then remember the specific mineral is iron carbonate.

etymology_story.zh: 此词来自德语 Xanthin，词根上溯希腊语 xanthos（黄色）。名称与早期化学检验中产生的黄色反应产物有关，并不表示纯黄嘌呤本身必然呈黄色。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from German Xanthin and ultimately from Greek xanthos, meaning yellow. The name refers to a yellow product observed in early chemical testing, rather than implying that pure xanthine itself must be yellow.

morphology_enriched.zh: 科学构词结构为 xanth-（黄）+ -ine（化学物质名称后缀），另有拼写 xanthin。相关词族包括 xanthines（黄嘌呤类化合物）、methylxanthine（甲基黄嘌呤）、hypoxanthine（次黄嘌呤）、paraxanthine（副黄嘌呤）和 xanthinuria（黄嘌呤尿症）；常见复合术语有 xanthine oxidase（黄嘌呤氧化酶）。
morphology_enriched.en: The scientific formation is xanth- meaning yellow + -ine, a suffix used in chemical names; xanthin is an alternative spelling. Related family members include xanthines, methylxanthine, hypoxanthine, paraxanthine, and xanthinuria; a common compound term is xanthine oxidase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: xanthin（黄嘌呤）是同一物质的另一拼写；2,6-dioxypurine（2,6-二氧嘌呤）是强调结构的化学名称；methylxanthine（甲基黄嘌呤）指甲基化衍生物这一类别，不能与黄嘌呤本体直接等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Xanthin is an alternative spelling for the same substance; 2,6-dioxypurine is a chemical name emphasizing its structure; methylxanthine denotes the class of methylated derivatives and is not an exact synonym for the parent compound.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: xanth- 提示“黄色反应”，-ine 提示“化学物质”：由命名线索记住黄嘌呤。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Let xanth- recall the yellow test reaction and -ine signal a chemical substance: together they anchor the name xanthine.

etymology_story.zh: 此词借自拉丁语 armiger，由 arma（武器；军备）和表示“携带”的 -ger 组成，原义为“携带武器的人”。随着 arms 也用于表示纹章，armiger 在纹章语境中发展为“有权使用纹章的人”。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin armiger, formed from arma, meaning weapons or military equipment, and -ger, meaning carrying; it originally meant an arms-bearer. As arms also came to denote heraldic devices, armiger developed the heraldic meaning of a person entitled to bear a coat of arms.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为整体借词处理；历史结构为 armi-（武器）+ -ger（携带者），后半部分不是现代英语常见的施事后缀 -er。复数为 armigers；相关派生词有 armigerous（有权使用纹章的；带有纹章的）和较少见的 armigeral（纹章持有者的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English normally treats armiger as a borrowed whole; its historical structure is armi- meaning arms + -ger meaning bearer, rather than the ordinary English agent suffix -er. The plural is armigers; derivatives include armigerous and the less common armigeral.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: arms-bearer（持械者；纹章持有者）可对应原义或纹章义，须依语境判断；coat-of-arms bearer（纹章持有者）明确指纹章义；squire（骑士侍从）与历史义相近，但也可指特定身份或社会阶层，并非总能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Arms-bearer may refer either to carrying weapons or to bearing heraldic arms, depending on context; coat-of-arms bearer explicitly identifies the heraldic sense; squire overlaps with the historical attendant sense but may also denote a particular rank or social status.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 arms 的双义：“携带武器的人”进一步对应“使用纹章的人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the two meanings of arms: a bearer of weapons becomes, in heraldry, a bearer of a coat of arms.
