etymology_story.zh: Bespatter 于17世纪由英语前缀 be- 与 spatter“溅洒”组合而成，be- 在这里加强“遍及、到处沾上”的意思。从“把泥点溅到身上”的具体画面，进一步发展出“以恶言玷污名誉”的比喻用法。
etymology_story.en: Bespatter was formed in the seventeenth century from be- and spatter, with the prefix reinforcing the idea of covering something all over. The physical image of splashing someone with dirt also supports the figurative meaning of staining a reputation with abuse or slander. [Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/bespatter), [Dictionary.com](https://www.dictionary.com/browse/bespatter).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词公式为 be-（遍及、彻底）+ spatter（溅洒）→ bespatter。屈折形式为 bespatters、bespattered、bespattering；bespattered 还可作分词形容词，表示“溅满污点的”。基础词族包括 spatter（动词：溅洒；名词：飞溅物、溅点）、spattered（溅满的）和 spattering（飞溅、溅洒）。缺乏可核实的考试收录及确切 CEFR 定级，exam_tags 留空。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation is be- “all over or thoroughly” + spatter “splash in scattered drops” → bespatter. Its inflected forms are bespatters, bespattered, and bespattering; bespattered can also serve as a participial adjective meaning “covered with splashes.” The base family includes spatter as a verb and noun, spattered as a participial adjective, and spattering for the action or scattered splashes. No examination inclusion or exact CEFR rating has been verified, so exam_tags is empty.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spatter（溅洒）最接近，强调散落的小液滴；splash（泼溅）更常用，可涉及较大水花；besmirch（玷污、诋毁）与比喻义最接近，重点在名誉受损。Bespatter 语体较文学化，并突出被溅得满是斑点。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spatter is the closest physical synonym and emphasizes scattered droplets; splash is more everyday and can involve larger amounts of liquid. Besmirch is closest to the figurative sense and emphasizes damage to reputation. Bespatter is literary and highlights being covered with scattered spots.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Be- adds “all over” to spatter: mud spots cover the clothes, and verbal mud stains the reputation.

etymology_story.en: The word comes from Greek khrisma, meaning “an anointing substance or ointment,” related to khriein, “to anoint,” and reached Old English through ecclesiastical Latin. It came to refer specifically to consecrated oil used in Christian ceremonies.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中以 chrism 为完整词基，不宜继续拆分。词族包括 chrism + -al → chrismal（圣油的），chrism + -ation → chrismation（傅圣油礼），以及 chrismatory（盛放圣油的容器）；这些派生词主要用于宗教语境。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, chrism is an intact base rather than a word with productive internal divisions. Its family includes chrism + -al → chrismal, “relating to chrism”; chrism + -ation → chrismation, “the rite of anointing with chrism”; and chrismatory, “a container for chrism”; these derivatives are chiefly religious terms.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Council is a general term for a deliberative body; synod usually denotes an assembly of clergy or church representatives; conclave specifically denotes the cardinals' meeting to elect a pope. The function of a consistory depends on the church concerned, and it is distinct from a conclave.

etymology_story.zh: 源于新拉丁语分类名称 Cryptogamia，由希腊语 kryptos“隐藏的”和 gamos“婚配”构成。“隐藏的婚配”指这些生物没有显眼的花和种子；这是传统分类概念，并不对应现代单一自然类群。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from the New Latin classification name Cryptogamia, formed from Greek kryptos, “hidden,” and gamos, “marriage.” The idea of “hidden marriage” referred to the absence of conspicuous flowers and seeds; the traditional grouping does not represent a single modern natural group.

morphology_enriched.zh: 学术构词成分 crypto-（隐藏的）+ -gam（婚配、生殖）→ cryptogam。词族包括 cryptogams（复数），cryptogamic、cryptogamous（隐花植物的），cryptogamy（隐花生殖；隐花植物学），以及较少见的 cryptogamist（隐花植物研究者）。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned combining forms are crypto-, “hidden,” and -gam, “marriage or reproduction.” The family includes the plural cryptogams; cryptogamic and cryptogamous, “relating to cryptogams”; cryptogamy, “cryptogamous reproduction or the study of cryptogams”; and the less common cryptogamist, “a student of cryptogams.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: spore-producing organism（产孢生物）强调繁殖方式，范围不完全相同；flowerless plant（无花植物）只强调没有花，也可能包括裸子植物。cryptogam 是传统术语，还曾涵盖真菌等现代分类中不属于植物的生物，因此没有完全对应的现代同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Spore-producing organism emphasizes reproduction and has a different scope; flowerless plant emphasizes the absence of flowers and can include gymnosperms. Cryptogam is a traditional term that also covered organisms, such as fungi, no longer classified as plants, so it has no exact modern synonym.

etymology_story.zh: 中古英语 cumbren、combren 与 encumbren 密切相关，后者来自古法语 encombrer“阻塞、妨碍”。“挡住去路”的空间意义也发展为“使人背负重担、受到拖累”的意义。
etymology_story.en: Middle English cumbren and combren were closely related to encumbren, from Old French encombrer, “to obstruct or hinder.” The physical idea of blocking movement also developed into the sense of burdening or hampering someone.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cumber 是完整词基。屈折形式为 cumbers、cumbered、cumbering；主要词族有 cumbersome（笨重难用的）→ cumbersomely、cumbersomeness，以及 cumbrous（笨重累赘的）→ cumbrously、cumbrousness；较少见的 cumberer 指造成妨碍的人或物。相关词还有 encumber（拖累；使负担义务）、encumbrance（负担；障碍）和 unencumbered（无负担的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cumber is an intact base. Its inflections are cumbers, cumbered, and cumbering; its main family includes cumbersome, “awkward or difficult to handle,” with cumbersomely and cumbersomeness, and cumbrous, “burdensome or unwieldy,” with cumbrously and cumbrousness; the uncommon cumberer denotes someone or something that obstructs. Related words include encumber, “to burden or impose obligations on,” encumbrance, “a burden or obstruction,” and unencumbered, “free of burdens.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: obstruct（阻挡）强调挡住通路或进程；encumber（拖累）强调附加负担限制行动；burden（使负担）强调承受的重量或责任。cumber 兼有阻塞与拖累义，现代使用通常带文学或古雅色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Obstruct emphasizes blocking a route or process; encumber emphasizes an added load that restricts action; burden emphasizes weight or responsibility borne. Cumber covers both obstruction and burdening and usually sounds literary or old-fashioned today.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从 cumbersome“笨重累赘的”反记 cumber：东西一多，就堵路、拖累。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Work backward from cumbersome: too much stuff blocks your way and weighs you down.

etymology_story.zh: 该词经欧洲语言中的多种形式传入英语，可追溯至阿拉伯语 tarjuman“口译员”，传播过程中涉及中世纪希腊语和意大利语等语言。它在英语中主要用于历史上奥斯曼帝国及周边地区为旅行者、商人或外交使团服务的译员。
etymology_story.en: The word reached English through European forms ultimately traceable to Arabic tarjuman, “interpreter,” with medieval Greek and Italian among the languages involved in its transmission. In English, it became associated especially with historical interpreters serving travelers, merchants, and diplomatic missions in the Ottoman world and surrounding regions.

morphology_enriched.zh: dragoman 是整体借词，不能按现代英语拆成 drag“拖”和 man“人”。复数可用 dragomans 或 dragomen；派生词较少，主要有罕见的 dragomanic（译员的）和 dragomanship（译员的职务、技艺或工作）。
morphology_enriched.en: Dragoman is a borrowed whole word and should not be analyzed as English drag plus man. Its plurals are dragomans and dragomen; derivatives are uncommon and include dragomanic, “relating to a dragoman,” and dragomanship, “the office, skill, or work of a dragoman.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: interpreter（口译员）是最接近的现代通称；translator（译者）通常侧重书面翻译；guide（向导）强调带路和提供当地信息。dragoman 带有特定历史地域背景，职责往往兼具口译、向导和交涉中介功能。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Interpreter is the closest general modern term; translator usually emphasizes written translation; guide emphasizes navigation and local information. Dragoman has a specific historical and regional setting, often combining interpreting, guiding, and mediation.

etymology_story.zh: galvanometer 由 galvano- 和表示测量仪器的 -meter 构成，前者源自意大利科学家路易吉·伽尔瓦尼的姓氏，后者最终源自希腊语 metron（尺度、测量）。这个名称把早期电学研究中的伽尔瓦尼之名与电流测量联系起来。
etymology_story.en: Galvanometer combines galvano-, derived from the surname of the Italian scientist Luigi Galvani, with -meter, ultimately from Greek metron, meaning measure. The name connects Galvani's association with early electrical research to the measurement of electric current.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：galvano-（与电流有关的组合形式）＋ -meter（测量仪器）。主要词族：galvanometers（复数）、galvanometry（检流测量法）、galvanometric／galvanometrical（检流测量的）、galvanometrically（以检流测量方式）；galvanic（原电的）和 galvanism（原电现象）属于共享 galvano- 来源的相关词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: galvano- (a combining form relating to electric current) + -meter (a measuring instrument). The principal family includes galvanometers, galvanometry (measurement using galvanometers), galvanometric/galvanometrical (relating to such measurement), and galvanometrically. Galvanic and galvanism are related formations sharing the same historical base.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ammeter（电流表）是功能相近的较宽泛名称，通常直接显示电流大小；microammeter（微安表）专门测量微安量级电流；galvanometer（检流计）尤其强调微弱电流的检测及其引起的偏转。这些名称的适用范围有重叠，但不完全相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ammeter is a broader functional alternative for an instrument that measures current, usually with a direct numerical scale; microammeter specifies measurement in microamperes; galvanometer particularly emphasizes detecting small currents and the resulting deflection. Their applications overlap, but the terms are not identical.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: galvano- 联想电流，-meter 表示测量仪：让微弱电流通过指针偏转显现出来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect galvano- with electric current and -meter with measurement: a tiny current becomes visible as a needle's movement.

etymology_story.zh: gelignite 是19世纪的造词，结合了 gelatine（明胶）的片段、拉丁语 ignis（火）及后缀 -ite。名称同时提示这种炸药的胶状质地和爆炸性质。
etymology_story.en: Gelignite is a nineteenth-century coinage combining a fragment of gelatine, Latin ignis meaning fire, and the suffix -ite. Its name evokes both the explosive's gelatinous texture and its explosive character.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词来源可表示为 gel(atine)（明胶）＋ ign(is)（火）＋ -ite（物质名称后缀），属于截取片段组成的造词，不能视为三个自由词素的普通拼接。现代英语通常将 gelignite 作为不可数的完整词使用，没有常用的独立派生词族；gelatine（明胶）和 ignite（点燃）分别与其造词材料有关，并非由 gelignite 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Its formation can be represented as gel(atine) + ign(is), meaning fire, + -ite, a substance-name suffix; this is a coinage using shortened elements rather than an ordinary combination of three independent morphemes. In modern English, gelignite normally functions as an uncountable whole word and has no common independent derivative family. Gelatine and ignite relate to its naming elements but are not derivatives of gelignite.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有完全等义的常用替换词。dynamite（达纳炸药、通常也译作黄色炸药）是相关的硝化甘油类炸药名称，部分分类将胶质炸药归入其中；blasting gelatin（爆胶）是相关但组成不同的胶状炸药；explosive（炸药）则是上位词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact substitute. Dynamite names a related class of nitroglycerin-based explosives, within which gelignite is sometimes classified; blasting gelatin is a related gelatinous explosive with a different composition; explosive is the broader category.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: gel 联想胶状，ign 联想火：记住“胶状的爆破炸药”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link gel with a jelly-like texture and ign with fire: remember a gelatinous blasting explosive.

etymology_story.zh: ilmenite 以俄罗斯南乌拉尔地区的伊尔门山脉命名，英语形式来自德语 Ilmenit。地名加矿物名称后缀的结构保留了这种矿物与其早期研究产地的联系。
etymology_story.en: Ilmenite is named after the Ilmen Mountains in the southern Urals of Russia, and the English form comes from German Ilmenit. The place name and mineral suffix preserve its association with an early locality where the mineral was studied.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可辨认结构：Ilmen（伊尔门地名）＋ -ite（矿物名称后缀）；它不是 iron（铁）与其他成分的拼合。主要相关形式：ilmenites（不同样品、种类等语境中的复数）、ilmenitic（含钛铁矿的、与钛铁矿有关的）；ilmenite-bearing（含钛铁矿的）是透明复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Recognizable structure: Ilmen (the place name) + -ite (a mineral-name suffix); the word is not formed from iron. Principal related forms include ilmenites, used for distinct specimens or varieties, and ilmenitic, meaning containing or relating to ilmenite. Ilmenite-bearing is a transparent compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: titanic iron ore（钛铁矿）是较旧的近义名称；titanium ore（钛矿石）范围更广，还包括其他含钛矿物；rutile（金红石）是另一种重要钛矿物，主要成分为 TiO₂，并不是 ilmenite 的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Titanic iron ore is an older near-synonymous name; titanium ore is broader and includes other titanium-bearing minerals; rutile is another important titanium mineral, chiefly TiO₂, and is not a synonym for ilmenite.

etymology_story.en: The singular nauplius entered scientific terminology for crustacean larvae in the nineteenth century and goes back to Latin nauplius and Greek nauplios, a name for a marine shellfish. Nauplii preserves the Latin-style plural ending -i of this Latinized name.

morphology_enriched.zh: 屈折变化：nauplius（单数，无节幼体）→ naupli-（词干）＋ -i（拉丁式复数词尾）→ nauplii；这是复数变化，并非新词派生。主要词族及相关形式：naupliar／nauplial（无节幼体的）、naupliiform（无节幼体形的）、metanauplius／metanauplii（后无节幼体，单数／复数）。
morphology_enriched.en: Inflection: nauplius (singular) → naupli- (stem) + -i (Latin-style plural ending) → nauplii; this is plural formation rather than derivation of a new word. Principal family and related forms include naupliar/nauplial (relating to nauplii), naupliiform (shaped like a nauplius), and metanauplius/metanauplii (a subsequent larval stage, singular/plural).

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nauplius larvae（无节幼体）是释义性近义表达；crustacean larvae（甲壳动物幼体）范围更广；metanauplii（后无节幼体）指随后出现的发育阶段，不能与 nauplii 任意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nauplius larvae is an explanatory equivalent; crustacean larvae is broader and includes other larval stages; metanauplii refers to a subsequent developmental stage and is not freely interchangeable with nauplii.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记单数 nauplius，再把 -us 换成 -i：一只无节幼体变成多只。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with singular nauplius, then replace -us with -i: one early crustacean larva becomes several.

etymology_story.en: Nystatin was named using a contraction of New York State followed by -in, an ending common in substance and drug names. The name commemorates the New York State public-health research institution where its discoverers worked.

morphology_enriched.zh: 命名结构：NY（New York，纽约）＋ stat(e)（State，州）＋ -in（物质名称后缀）。现代英语将 nystatin 作为完整药名使用，没有常用的独立派生词族；nystatin-resistant（耐制霉菌素的）和 nystatin-containing（含制霉菌素的）是按需组成的复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Naming structure: NY (New York) + stat(e) (State) + -in (a substance-name suffix). Modern English treats nystatin as a whole drug name, with no common independent derivative family; nystatin-resistant and nystatin-containing are productive compound adjectives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有通用且完全等义的普通词替换。antifungal（抗真菌药）是上位词；amphotericin B（两性霉素B）和 natamycin（那他霉素）是同属多烯类的其他抗真菌药，各自的用途和制剂不同，不能作为制霉菌素的同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no ordinary generic word that is an exact substitute. Antifungal is the broader category; amphotericin B and natamycin are other polyene antifungal medicines with different uses and formulations, so neither is a synonym for nystatin.

etymology_story.zh: pollard 由表示“头部”的 poll 加后缀 -ard 构成，历史上曾指无角或去角的动物，也指截去上部枝条的树。它后来用作动词，表示这种树木修剪方式，pollarded 则表示过去发生的修剪动作或修剪后的状态。
etymology_story.en: Pollard combines poll, meaning “head,” with the suffix -ard and historically referred to a hornless or dehorned animal as well as a tree with its upper branches cut off. It later became a verb for this pruning method, with pollarded expressing either the past action or the resulting condition.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：pollard（截顶修剪）+ -ed → pollarded；-ed 构成规则动词的过去式和过去分词，过去分词也可作形容词。主要词族：pollard（名词：截顶树；动词：截顶修剪）、pollards（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、pollarding（现在分词；也指这种修剪作业）、pollarded。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: pollard + -ed → pollarded; -ed forms the regular past tense and past participle, and the participle can function as an adjective. The principal word family comprises pollard (a tree managed by this method, or the verb), pollards (plural noun or third-person singular verb), pollarding (present participle or the pruning practice), and pollarded.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pruned（修剪过的）是泛称；lopped（砍去枝条的）强调砍除枝条，不一定形成固定树形；coppiced（萌芽更新修剪过的）通常指近地面截干，与在较高位置修剪的 pollarded 不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pruned is the general term; lopped emphasizes cutting off branches without necessarily establishing a particular tree form; coppiced usually means cut back near ground level, whereas pollarded involves cutting at a higher level.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Poll means “head”: trim the tree’s “head” and let new shoots grow from the raised framework.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在16世纪借用拉丁语 septuaginta（七十）形成这一名称，呼应有关七十或七十二位译者的传统叙事。这个名称最初与《摩西五经》的希腊语翻译传统相关，后来扩展用于更广泛的犹太教经典希腊语译本。
etymology_story.en: English adopted the name in the sixteenth century from Latin septuaginta, meaning “seventy,” in reference to the tradition of seventy or seventy-two translators. Originally associated with the Greek translation of the Pentateuch, the name came to cover a wider collection of Jewish scriptures in Greek.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 Septuagint 视为完整借词，不宜强拆为英语词根和词缀。主要派生词：Septuagint + -al → Septuagintal（七十士译本的）；Septuagint + -alist → Septuagintalist（七十士译本研究者）；Septuagint + -ism → Septuagintism（七十士译本特有的词语或表达）；LXX 是其传统缩写。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, Septuagint is a complete borrowing rather than a transparent combination of English roots and affixes. Principal derivatives include Septuagintal (relating to the Septuagint), Septuagintalist (a scholar of the Septuagint), and Septuagintism (a word or expression characteristic of it); LXX is its conventional abbreviation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: LXX 是最直接的传统简称，其中罗马数字表示“七十”；Greek Old Testament（希腊语《旧约》）是常见描述性名称，但具体文本范围可能随语境而变；Greek Bible（希腊语《圣经》）范围更广，也可能包括《新约》。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: LXX is the direct conventional abbreviation, using the Roman numeral for seventy; Greek Old Testament is a common descriptive name, although its precise textual scope can vary; Greek Bible is broader and may include the New Testament.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 名称里的“七十”连接传统中的译者人数：七十士 → 古希腊语译本。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect “seventy” in the name with the traditional number of translators: seventy translators → the ancient Greek version.

etymology_story.zh: strongroom 由英语 strong（坚固的）和 room（房间）直接复合而成，字面意思是“坚固的房间”。它逐渐固定指经过加固、专门用于保管金钱、贵重物品或重要文件的房间。
etymology_story.en: Strongroom is an English compound of strong and room, literally meaning a strongly built room. It developed the specialized meaning of a reinforced room used to protect money, valuables, or important documents.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：strong（坚固的）+ room（房间）→ strongroom，为名词与形容词组合形成的复合名词。复数为 strongrooms；也可写作 strong room 或 strong-room，没有常用的进一步派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: strong + room → strongroom, a compound noun formed from an adjective and a noun. Its plural is strongrooms; strong room and strong-room are alternative spellings, and there are no common further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vault（保险库、金库）最接近，尤其常见于银行语境；safe（保险箱）通常指独立的箱柜，而不是可进入的房间；secure room（安全储藏室）范围更广，不一定具有保险库级别的加固结构。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vault is the closest equivalent, especially in banking; safe usually means a separate secure container rather than a room; secure room is broader and does not necessarily imply the reinforced construction of a strongroom.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: strong + room：把整个房间做成保险箱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Strong + room: imagine an entire room built like a safe.

etymology_story.zh: supergrass 由 super- 与英国俚语 grass（告密者）组合而成。它把普通“告密者”的含义加强为能够提供大量证据、牵涉多名罪犯或重大案件的告密者。
etymology_story.en: Supergrass combines super- with grass, British slang for an informer. The prefix intensifies the meaning to describe an informer whose extensive evidence implicates numerous criminals or concerns serious crimes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：super-（超常的、程度特别高的）+ grass（告密者）→ supergrass；这里的 grass 不是“草”的字面义。复数为 supergrasses；相关词族包括 grass（告密者；告密）、grasses、grassed、grassing，以及短语 grass on someone（告发某人）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: super- (exceptional or unusually extensive) + grass (an informer) → supergrass; grass does not have its literal plant meaning here. The plural is supergrasses; the related family includes grass (informer or inform), grasses, grassed, grassing, and the phrase grass on someone.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: informer（告密者）常指向警方告发他人的人，往往带贬义；informant（线人、消息提供者）较中性，使用范围也更广；stool pigeon（告密者、警方线人）带明显贬义。supergrass 特别强调所提供证据的数量或案件的重要程度。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Informer often refers disapprovingly to someone who reports others to the police; informant is more neutral and has a broader range of uses; stool pigeon is strongly disapproving slang for a police informer. Supergrass specifically emphasizes the extent or importance of the evidence supplied.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先记俚语 grass＝告密者，再加 super-：掌握重大案情的“大线人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with slang grass, “informer,” then add super-: an informer with exceptionally extensive evidence.

etymology_story.zh: 英语在18世纪从法语借入 tarsier；法语名称来自 tarse（跗部），最终可追溯至希腊语 tarsos。这个名称强调眼镜猴特别长的跗部骨骼，这种结构有助于它跳跃。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed tarsier from French in the eighteenth century; the French name derives from tarse, referring to the tarsus, ultimately from Greek tarsos. The name highlights the animal’s unusually elongated tarsal bones, which help it leap.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tarsier 是整词借入的名词，复数为 tarsiers，没有常用的直接派生词。历史上的法语构词是 tarse（跗部）去末尾 e，再加 -ier；英语 tarsus（跗部）、tarsal（跗部的）属于同源相关词，不是由 tarsier 派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tarsier is a borrowed noun with the plural tarsiers and no common direct derivatives. Its historical French formation is tarse with the final e removed, plus -ier; English tarsus and tarsal are related through the same root, rather than derived from tarsier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用且完全等义的日常近义词。primate（灵长类动物）和 haplorhine（简鼻类灵长动物）都是范围更广的分类名称；bushbaby（婴猴）虽也常为小型夜行灵长动物，却是另一类动物，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common everyday synonym with exactly the same meaning. Primate and haplorhine are broader classification terms; bushbaby refers to a different group of small, often nocturnal primates and is not interchangeable with tarsier.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tars- 联系“跗部”：长后足善跳跃，大眼睛识眼镜猴。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link tars- with the tarsus: long hind feet for leaping, huge eyes for recognizing a tarsier.

etymology_story.zh: teasel 源自古英语 tǣsel，与表示拉开、梳理纤维的 tease 有历史联系。这种植物的带刺干花头曾用于织物起绒，因此植物名称也用于指这种工具，并进一步用作动词。
etymology_story.en: Teasel comes from Old English tǣsel and is historically related to tease in its fibre-pulling or combing sense. The plant's spiny dried heads were used to raise the nap of cloth, giving rise to the tool sense and the verb.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 teasel 是不可再作常用词缀拆分的词基；动词由名词直接转用。词形和派生词包括 teasels、teaselled/teaseled、teaselling/teaseling，以及 teaseller/teaseler（起绒工或起绒设备）；双写 l 的形式常见于英式英语。tease 是历史相关词，不是现代英语中由 teasel 派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, teasel is a lexical base without a productive prefix–root–suffix breakdown; the verb is formed by conversion from the noun. Forms and derivatives include teasels, teaselled/teaseled, teaselling/teaseling, and teaseller/teaseler, a worker or device that raises nap; doubled-l forms are usual in British English. Tease is historically related, rather than a modern derivative of teasel.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 植物义没有完全对应的常用近义词：thistle（蓟）外形相似，但属于不同植物类群。动词义可比较 nap（给织物起绒，强调加工效果）和 card（梳理纤维，通常用于纺纱前）；teasel 强调以起绒草花头或类似设备处理布面。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The plant has no exact everyday synonym: thistle names a different group of plants with a similar prickly appearance. For the verb, nap emphasizes producing a raised fabric surface, while card usually means preparing loose fibres before spinning; teasel specifically refers to working the cloth's surface with teasel heads or similar equipment.

senses.meaning_en: A musical interval spanning three whole tones.
senses.english_definition: A tritone is the distance between two musical notes that are three whole tones apart, such as C and F sharp.
senses.collocation_en: tritone substitution; a dissonant tritone
senses.collocation_zh: 三全音替代；不协和的三全音音程

etymology_story.zh: tritone 的名称可追溯至希腊语 tritonon，经拉丁语音乐术语传统传承，其构词含义为“三个全音”。它指跨三个全音的音程，在十二平均律中相当于六个半音。
etymology_story.en: The name tritone ultimately goes back to Greek tritonon through the Latin tradition of musical terminology, with the literal meaning 'three tones.' It denotes an interval spanning three whole tones, equivalent to six semitones in twelve-tone equal temperament.

morphology_enriched.zh: tri-（三）+ tone（全音）→ tritone；复数为 tritones。现代英语没有广泛使用的直接派生词族；tritone substitution（三全音替代）和 tritone relationship（三全音关系）是术语组合，不能把 tonal、tonality 等 tone 的词族成员算作 tritone 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Tri- 'three' + tone 'whole tone' forms tritone; the plural is tritones. There is no widely used set of direct derivatives in modern English. Tritone substitution and tritone relationship are technical combinations; members of the broader tone family, such as tonal and tonality, are not direct derivatives of tritone.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: augmented fourth（增四度）和 diminished fifth（减五度）在十二平均律中都跨六个半音，但音符拼写与和声功能不同；tritone 强调三个全音的跨度，常统称这两种等音音程。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An augmented fourth and a diminished fifth both span six semitones in twelve-tone equal temperament, but their note spelling and harmonic functions differ. Tritone emphasizes the span of three whole tones and commonly covers both enharmonic intervals.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri- 是“三”，tone 是“全音”：三个全音就是三全音。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means three: count three whole tones to reach a tritone.

etymology_story.zh: verruca 在16世纪由拉丁语 verrūca（疣、赘生物）借入英语。它在医学中可以泛指疣，而在现代英式日常英语中尤其常指脚底的跖疣。
etymology_story.en: Verruca entered English in the sixteenth century from Latin verrūca, meaning a wart or excrescence. It can refer to a wart generally in medical usage, while everyday British English particularly uses it for a wart on the sole.

morphology_enriched.zh: verruca 是借入的词基，不宜强行拆成英语词根与词缀；复数为 verrucas 或拉丁式 verrucae。相关学术构词使用 verruc-：verruc- + -ous → verrucous（疣状的、多疣的），另有 verrucose（具疣状突起的）、verruciform（疣形的）和 verrucosity（疣状性质或突起）；这些属于专业词汇。
morphology_enriched.en: Verruca is a borrowed lexical base rather than an English root-and-affix construction; its plurals are verrucas and Latin-style verrucae. Related learned formations use verruc-: verruc- + -ous gives verrucous, meaning warty; other technical relatives include verrucose, covered with wartlike projections, verruciform, wart-shaped, and verrucosity, a warty condition or projection.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wart（疣）是范围更广的日常词；plantar wart（跖疣）明确限定在脚底，与英式常用义的 verruca 最接近。callus（胼胝、老茧）是摩擦或受压造成的皮肤增厚，并不是疣，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wart is the broader everyday term, while plantar wart explicitly identifies a wart on the sole and is the closest equivalent of the usual British sense of verruca. A callus is thickened skin caused by pressure or friction, so it is a related comparison rather than a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor the whole word to a small wart under the foot; the verruc- family consistently points to warts or wartlike bumps.

etymology_story.zh: wassail 源于中古英语中的祝酒问候语，其历史背景包括古诺尔斯语 ves heill 和相应的古英语 wæs hāl，意思都是“愿你安康”。这一祝语后来用于指祝酒饮料、节庆欢宴，以及唱歌祝酒的活动。
etymology_story.en: Wassail developed from a Middle English drinking salutation associated with Old Norse ves heill and the corresponding Old English wæs hāl, both meaning 'be well.' The greeting subsequently came to name the drink, the festivities, and the activity of singing and toasting.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 wassail 是完整词基，不再按原来的祝语成分拆分；名词与动词同形。词形及直接派生词包括 wassails、wassailed、wassailing，以及 wassail + -er → wassailer（参加唱歌祝酒活动的人）；wassailing 也可作活动名称，表示这种节庆或果园祈丰收习俗。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, wassail is a whole lexical base rather than a transparently divisible greeting; the noun and verb share the same form. Inflections and direct derivatives include wassails, wassailed, wassailing, and wassail + -er → wassailer, a participant. Wassailing also functions as an activity noun for the festive or orchard custom.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: revel（纵情欢庆）强调热闹作乐；carol（唱圣诞颂歌）强调歌唱，不一定涉及饮酒；toast（祝酒）强调举杯表达祝愿。wassail 将传统祝愿、歌唱与饮酒联系起来，也可专指向果树祈丰收。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Revel emphasizes lively enjoyment; carol emphasizes Christmas singing without necessarily involving drink; toast focuses on expressing a wish over a drink. Wassail connects traditional good wishes with singing and drinking and can specifically describe the orchard ceremony.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“愿你安康”出发：举杯祝福 → 热酒欢庆 → 唱歌祝酒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Start with 'be well': a good-health greeting becomes a toast, a festive drink, and a singing celebration.

etymology_story.zh: acta 直接借自拉丁语，是 actum 的中性复数形式，字面意思是“已经做过的事情”，最终源于 agere（做、行动）。由于正式行为需要记录，这个词也用于指议事记录，并出现在学术刊物和文献汇编的名称中。
etymology_story.en: Acta was borrowed directly from Latin as the neuter plural of actum, literally 'things done,' ultimately from agere, 'to do or act.' The association between official actions and their documentation led to its use for records of proceedings and in titles of scholarly publications and collections.

morphology_enriched.zh: 这是保留拉丁语形态的借词：act-（已做、已实施）+ -a（中性复数词尾）→ acta；它不是 act 加英语复数词尾构成的。通常按复数使用，不再加 -s；相关拉丁语单数为 actum，但在英语中不常用。act、action、active、activity、actor 与其共享拉丁语词源，并不是现代英语中由 acta 直接派生的词。
morphology_enriched.en: This borrowing preserves Latin morphology: act- 'done or performed' + -a, the neuter plural ending, gives acta; it is not act with an English plural ending. It is normally plural and does not take an additional -s; the corresponding Latin singular is actum, which is uncommon in English. Act, action, active, activity, and actor share its Latin ancestry but are not direct modern English derivatives of acta.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: minutes（会议纪要）通常记录讨论要点和决定；proceedings（会议记录、会议论文集）可包括更完整的过程或提交的论文；records（记录、档案）范围最广。acta 是较正式的学术或历史用语，强调正式行为及议事活动的记录。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Minutes usually summarize a meeting's business and decisions; proceedings can include a fuller account or papers presented at a meeting; records is the broadest term. Acta is a formal scholarly or historical term emphasizing documented official acts and proceedings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 先有 act“做事”，再把“做过的事”记下来：acta 就是正式行事记录；-a 提醒你它是复数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'things acted upon, then written down': acta records what was done, and its Latin -a marks a plural.

etymology_story.zh: 该词最终源于希腊语 antiphōnos，意为“以声音回应的”，由 anti-（相对、回应）和 phōnē（声音）构成，经教会拉丁语 antiphona 传入英语。它原本突出声音之间的回应，后来成为特定礼仪圣歌或经文的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word ultimately comes from Greek antiphōnos, meaning 'sounding in response', formed from anti- 'in response to' and phōnē 'voice', through ecclesiastical Latin antiphona. The idea of answering voices developed into the name of a particular liturgical chant or text.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语通常将 antiphon 作为完整借词使用；从历史词素看，可分析为 anti-（回应、相对）+ -phon（声音），这里的 anti- 不表示现代常见的“反对”。主要词族：antiphons（复数）、antiphonal（应答式的；应答圣歌集）、antiphonally（以应答方式）、antiphony（交替应答的演唱或演奏）、antiphonary／antiphoner（应答圣歌集）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats antiphon as a whole borrowed word; historically, it contains anti- 'in response to, opposite' and -phon 'sound', rather than the familiar modern sense 'against'. Its principal family includes antiphons, antiphonal, antiphonally, antiphony, and antiphonary or antiphoner.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chant（圣歌、吟唱）是范围更广的音乐类别；responsory（应答咏）通常有领唱与会众或唱诗班的回应，在礼仪上与 antiphon 有所区别；refrain（叠句、副歌）强调反复出现的文字或旋律，不限于宗教场合。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Chant is the broader musical category; a responsory typically involves a solo passage and a choral or congregational response and is liturgically distinct from an antiphon; a refrain emphasizes repeated words or music and need not be religious.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: anti- 在这里是“回应”，phon 是“声音”：一声唱出，另一声回应。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Here anti- means 'in response' and phon means 'sound': one voice sings, another answers.

senses.meaning_zh: 应答圣歌集；收录对经等礼仪圣歌的书

senses.english_definition: An antiphonal is a book that contains antiphons and other chants used in church worship.

etymology_story.zh: 该词与中世纪拉丁语 antiphonalis（与应答圣歌有关的）相联系，其基础 antiphona 最终来自希腊语表示“声音相互回应”的词。形容词表示应答式的音乐形式，名词则指收录相关礼仪圣歌的书。
etymology_story.en: The word is connected with medieval Latin antiphonalis 'relating to antiphons', based on antiphona, ultimately from Greek words expressing answering voices. The adjective describes the musical practice, while the noun names a book containing the relevant liturgical chants.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词分析：antiphon（应答圣歌）+ -al（与……有关的）→ antiphonal；antiphonal + -ly → antiphonally（以交替应答方式）。名词复数为 antiphonals；相关词族还有 antiphony（交替应答的演唱或演奏）、antiphonary／antiphoner（应答圣歌集）。注意重音由 antiphon 的第一音节移至 antiphonal 的第二音节。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: antiphon + the adjective-forming suffix -al gives antiphonal; adding -ly gives antiphonally. The noun plural is antiphonals, and related words include antiphony, antiphonary, and antiphoner. Stress shifts from the first syllable in antiphon to the second in antiphonal.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 形容词近义表达：responsive（应答的）强调回应；alternating（交替的）只强调轮流，不一定构成回应；responsorial（应答咏式的）通常强调领唱与群体回应的安排。名词义的近义词为 antiphonary、antiphoner，均指应答圣歌集。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the adjective, responsive emphasizes an answering relationship; alternating indicates taking turns without necessarily answering; responsorial typically describes a soloist-and-group response pattern. For the book sense, antiphonary and antiphoner are close equivalents.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: antiphon 是“应答圣歌”，加 -al 就是“应答式的”；两组声音轮流接唱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Add -al to antiphon: the music has an answering pattern, with two groups taking turns.

etymology_story.zh: 人物义来自辛克莱·刘易斯1922年小说《巴比特》的主人公 George F. Babbitt，其姓名后来成为自满、物质至上且墨守成规者的代称。合金义另有来源，得名于1839年研制相关轴承合金的美国发明家 Isaac Babbitt，动词义由合金名称转化而来。
etymology_story.en: The social type is named after George F. Babbitt, the protagonist of Sinclair Lewis's 1922 novel Babbitt, whose name became a label for complacent, materialistic conformity. The alloy has a separate origin in American inventor Isaac Babbitt, who developed the relevant bearing alloy in 1839; the verb derives from the alloy's name.

morphology_enriched.zh: Babbitt 是姓氏转化而来的词，不能按现代英语拆成前缀和词根。人物义词族包括 Babbitt + -ry → Babbittry（巴比特式习气）、Babbitt + -ism → Babbittism（巴比特主义）、Babbitt + -ish → Babbittish（巴比特式的）；技术义由名词 babbitt 零派生为动词，变化形式为 babbitts、babbitted、babbitting，另有 rebabbitt（重新衬巴氏合金）。
morphology_enriched.en: Babbitt is an eponym derived from a surname and has no productive prefix–root division. The social sense forms Babbittry, Babbittism, and Babbittish. In the technical sense, the noun babbitt becomes a verb through conversion, with babbitts, babbitted, and babbitting; rebabbitt means to apply a new babbitt lining.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 人物义：conformist（墨守成规者）强调服从通行规范；philistine（缺乏文化修养者）强调对艺术和思想的漠视；bourgeois（资产阶级人士、小市民）可强调阶层或价值观，贬义程度取决于语境。Babbitt 将商业成功、物质主义、自满和盲从结合在一起；技术义中的 bearing metal（轴承合金）是上位词，并非都指巴氏合金。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the social sense, conformist emphasizes adherence to accepted standards; philistine emphasizes indifference to culture and ideas; bourgeois can identify a social class or its values, with criticism depending on context. Babbitt combines commercial ambition, materialism, complacency, and conformity. In the technical sense, bearing metal is broader and does not always mean babbitt.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 人物义记“小说里的巴比特，把成功等同于金钱和随大流”；合金义另记发明家 Isaac Babbitt，两条来源分开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the fictional Babbitt as money-minded and comfortably conventional; connect the alloy separately with inventor Isaac Babbitt.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由古法语 blason 进入中古英语，早期与盾牌及盾上的纹章有关，更早的来源尚不确定。从展示和描述纹章的用法，又发展出醒目展示、公开宣扬的一般意义。
etymology_story.en: The word entered Middle English from Old French blason, associated with a shield and its heraldic arms; its earlier origin is uncertain. Uses involving the display and description of arms developed into the broader meaning of displaying or proclaiming something conspicuously.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 blazon 是不可再作常规拆分的词基，可同时作名词和动词。主要词族：blazons、blazoned、blazoning、blazoner（纹章描述者；宣扬者）、blazonry（纹章图案或纹章艺术）；相关形式有 emblazon（以纹章装饰；醒目印上）、emblazoned、emblazonment（纹章装饰；醒目展示）。不要把 blazon 当作 blaze + 后缀构成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, blazon is an unanalyzed base used as both noun and verb. Its principal family includes blazons, blazoned, blazoning, blazoner, and blazonry. Related forms include emblazon, emblazoned, and emblazonment. Blazon should not be analyzed as blaze plus a suffix.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 一般动词义：proclaim（公开宣布）强调郑重或公开表达；advertise（宣传）强调吸引注意或促进销售；emblazon（醒目印上、装饰）更突出视觉呈现。纹章名词义中，coat of arms 指纹章本身，而 blazon 还可专指用规范术语写出的描述。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the general verb, proclaim emphasizes public or emphatic announcement; advertise emphasizes attracting attention or promoting something; emblazon emphasizes conspicuous visual display. As a heraldic noun, coat of arms names the design itself, whereas blazon can specifically name its formal verbal description.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从盾牌上醒目的纹章出发：纹章被“展示出来”，消息也能被“醒目宣扬”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture conspicuous arms on a shield: blazon moves from displaying heraldry to displaying or proclaiming anything prominently.

morphology.text: chancre 是独立借词。chancr(e) + -ous → chancrous（下疳的），加后缀时去掉不发音的 e。

etymology.text: 16世纪英语从法语借入 chancre，法语词源再追溯到拉丁语 cancer；现代这个词专指一类疾病病灶。

senses.meaning_zh: 硬下疳；一期梅毒感染部位出现的溃疡，通常无痛
senses.meaning_en: An ulcer at the site of primary syphilis infection, typically painless.
senses.english_definition: A chancre is an ulcer that develops where syphilis first enters the body and is usually painless.
senses.collocation_en: a painless chancre; a syphilitic chancre
senses.collocation_zh: 无痛性硬下疳；梅毒性硬下疳
senses.sentence_en: The textbook describes a chancre as a typically painless ulcer associated with primary syphilis.
senses.sentence_zh: 这本教科书将硬下疳描述为与一期梅毒相关、通常无痛的溃疡。

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 chancre，最终可追溯到拉丁语 cancer（蟹；癌或侵蚀性溃疡）。这个历史上可泛指溃疡性病变的词，在现代医学英语中专指一期梅毒的特征性溃疡。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed chancre from French, ultimately from Latin cancer, meaning 'crab' and also a cancerous or spreading sore. A word historically associated with ulcerative lesions became the modern medical term for the characteristic ulcer of primary syphilis.

morphology_enriched.zh: chancre 是完整借词，现代英语中不拆作常用前缀与词根。主要词族：chancres（复数）；chancr- + -ous → chancrous（硬下疳的、下疳样的），加后缀时去掉词尾不发音的 e；chancr- + -oid → chancroid（软下疳），其形容词为 chancroidal（软下疳的）。注意 chancroid 是另一种疾病名称，并非 chancre 的变体。
morphology_enriched.en: Chancre is a whole borrowed word without a productive modern prefix–root division. Its principal family includes the plural chancres and chancrous, formed from chancr- plus -ous after dropping silent final e. Chancr- plus -oid gives chancroid, with the adjective chancroidal; chancroid names a different disease rather than a variant of chancre.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: syphilitic ulcer（梅毒性溃疡）是解释性表达，但范围可比一期梅毒的 chancre 更广；hard chancre（硬下疳）是强调典型硬结特征的传统名称；ulcer（溃疡）是上位词，不能说明病因。chancroid（软下疳）不是近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Syphilitic ulcer is an explanatory expression but can be broader than the primary lesion called a chancre; hard chancre is a traditional term emphasizing its characteristic firmness; ulcer is the broader category and does not identify a cause. Chancroid is not a synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住“初期感染处的疮”：chancre 是一期梅毒的特征性溃疡，不要与软下疳 chancroid 混淆。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor chancre to the initial syphilis sore at the infection site; keep it distinct from chancroid.

etymology_story.zh: 源自新拉丁语植物名称 Cineraria，来自拉丁语 cinerarius，意为“灰的、与灰有关的”，其词根是 cinis（灰）。名称所指的灰白色外观与这一植物类群中一些植物的叶面茸毛有关，后来英语也用它称瓜叶菊等观赏植物。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from the New Latin plant name Cineraria, based on Latin cinerarius, meaning 'of ashes', from cinis, 'ashes'. The name refers to the ashy appearance of foliage in some plants associated with the group, and English later applied it to ornamentals such as the florist’s cineraria.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中主要作为借入的完整植物名称使用；历史上可分析为 ciner-（灰）+ -aria（拉丁语阴性形式，用于植物属名）。复数为 cinerarias；同源词包括 cinerary（骨灰的、丧葬的）、incinerate（焚化）、incineration（焚化）和 incinerator（焚化炉），它们并非由 cineraria 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cineraria functions mainly as a borrowed plant name; historically, it contains ciner-, 'ashes', and -aria, a Latin feminine ending used in botanical names. Its plural is cinerarias; related words include cinerary, incinerate, incineration, and incinerator, which share its historical root but are not derived directly from cineraria.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: florist’s cineraria（花店栽培的瓜叶菊）更明确地指常见开花盆栽；florist’s ragwort（瓜叶菊）是同一植物的另一俗名。dusty miller（银叶菊等银灰叶观赏植物）与 cineraria 的部分园艺用法有关，但通常不能替换表示开花瓜叶菊的名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Florist’s cineraria specifies the familiar flowering pot plant; florist’s ragwort is another common name for that plant. Dusty miller overlaps with some horticultural uses of cineraria for silvery-leaved plants, but it is generally not interchangeable with the name of the flowering florist’s cineraria.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ciner-＝灰：先记“灰白叶色的命名线索”，再联想到开彩色花的瓜叶菊。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ciner- means 'ashes': remember the ashy foliage behind the name, then connect it to the colourful flowering plant.

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 coagulans，其词干为 coagulant-，是 coagulare（使凝结）的现在分词。更深一层的来源与 coagulum（凝块、凝乳剂）及 cogere（聚拢）有关，核心意象是把分散的东西聚合起来。
etymology_story.en: Coagulant comes from Latin coagulans, with the stem coagulant-, the present participle of coagulare, 'to cause to curdle'. Its deeper history connects coagulum, 'a clot or curdling agent', with cogere, 'to bring together', giving it the underlying idea of gathering dispersed material.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可分析为 coagul-（凝结）+ -ant（表示施事物或具有某种作用的）；与 coagul(ate)（凝结、使凝结）共享词干。主要词族包括 coagulate、coagulated、coagulating、coagulation（凝结）、coagulative（凝结性的）、coagulable（可凝结的）、coagulability（可凝性）和 coagulase（凝固酶）；anti- 构成 anticoagulant（抗凝剂；抗凝的）、anticoagulation（抗凝）及 anticoagulate（使抗凝）。
morphology_enriched.en: The word can be analysed as coagul-, 'coagulate', plus -ant, marking an acting substance or a property; it shares its stem with coagul(ate). The principal family includes coagulate, coagulated, coagulating, coagulation, coagulative, coagulable, coagulability, and coagulase; anti- forms anticoagulant, anticoagulation, and anticoagulate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: clotting agent（促凝剂）多用于血液凝固；flocculant（絮凝剂）强调促使细小颗粒形成较大的絮团，在水处理中与 coagulant 有技术区别；thickener（增稠剂）只强调提高黏度，不一定引起凝结。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Clotting agent usually concerns blood clotting; flocculant emphasizes gathering fine particles into larger flocs and is technically distinct from coagulant in water treatment; thickener increases viscosity without necessarily causing coagulation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把分散的东西“聚成团”：coagulant 是促成凝结的物质，也可形容这种作用。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'bring together into a clot': a coagulant causes the gathering, and coagulant describes that effect.

etymology_story.zh: 这是19世纪科学英语中形成的词，由源于拉丁语 ferrum（铁）的构词成分与材料、矿物名称后缀 -ite 组成。该词用于不同的含铁材料，因此现代英语中的“铁素体”和“铁氧体”必须根据冶金或电子材料语境区分。
etymology_story.en: Ferrite was formed in nineteenth-century scientific English from a combining element based on Latin ferrum, 'iron', and the material or mineral suffix -ite. It came to name different iron-related materials, so its metallurgical and magnetic-ceramic meanings must be distinguished by context.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可写作 ferr-（铁）+ -ite（材料或矿物）；ferr- 与 ferri- 都见于含铁术语。直接词族包括 ferrites（复数）、ferritic（铁素体的；铁氧体的，依语境而定）、ferritize／ferritise（使铁素体化）和 ferritization／ferritisation（铁素体化）；相关含铁词包括 ferrous（二价铁的）、ferric（三价铁的）和 ferromagnetic（铁磁性的）。ferrite core 中的 ferrite 是名词作定语。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern formation is ferr-, 'iron', plus -ite, a material or mineral suffix; both ferr- and ferri- occur in iron-related terminology. Direct family members include ferrites, ferritic, ferritize/ferritise, and ferritization/ferritisation; related iron vocabulary includes ferrous, ferric, and ferromagnetic. In ferrite core, ferrite is an attributive noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: alpha iron（α铁）与常温下的铁素体密切相关，但更侧重铁的晶体形式；magnetic ceramic（磁性陶瓷）是涵盖铁氧体的较宽材料类别；iron oxide（氧化铁）指化学组成类别，不能笼统替换 ferrite。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Alpha iron is closely related to ordinary low-temperature ferrite but emphasizes the crystalline form of iron; magnetic ceramic is a broader material category that includes ferrites; iron oxide names a chemical category and is not a general substitute for ferrite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ferr-＝铁，-ite＝材料：看到 ferrite，先想“铁材料”，再按语境分铁氧体与铁素体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ferr- means 'iron' and -ite signals a material: think 'iron material', then use context to choose the ceramic or steel-phase meaning.

etymology_story.zh: 19世纪英语将印地语、乌尔都语中的 gend-khana（球馆，字面为“球的房屋”）改造为 gymkhana，拼写受到 gymnasium 的影响，其中 khana 源自波斯语，意为“房屋、场所”。该词先与体育活动场所及运动会相联系，后来发展出马术和机动车技巧赛等用法。
etymology_story.en: In the nineteenth century, English reshaped Hindi and Urdu gend-khana, literally 'ball house', under the influence of gymnasium; khana comes from Persian and means 'house' or 'place'. The word became associated with sporting establishments and meetings, and later with equestrian and motoring skill competitions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常作为完整借词使用，不能简单分析为英语 gym 加一个英语后缀。历史结构是 gend（球）+ khana（房屋、场所），首部后来受 gymnasium 影响而改变；复数为 gymkhanas，无常用的直接派生词，gymkhana rider（马术技巧赛骑手）和 gymkhana course（技巧赛赛道）属于名词组合。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English generally treats gymkhana as a whole borrowed word, not as English gym plus an English suffix. Historically, it contains gend, 'ball', and khana, 'house or place', with the first element reshaped under the influence of gymnasium; the plural is gymkhanas, and combinations such as gymkhana rider and gymkhana course are noun compounds rather than direct derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Horse show is broader and need not include riding games; autotest is close to the motoring sense, although competition rules differ; sports club corresponds only to the South Asian establishment sense.

etymology.text: 经中古英语 hauberk、古法语 hauberc 传入，追溯到古低地法兰克语中表示“颈部保护”的名称。想象一件连颈部也能保护的金属环甲衣。

usage_note: 可数历史用语，指衣服形制的锁子甲，不是任何金属胸甲；常见于中世纪展览和历史小说。

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语和古法语 hauberc 传入，通常追溯至法兰克语中意为“颈部保护”的复合词，其两个成分分别表示“颈部”和“保护”。名称后来用于保护躯干的锁子甲长衣，并不表示每件这种甲衣都带有护颈结构。
etymology_story.en: Hauberk entered through Middle English and Old French hauberc and is generally traced to a Frankish compound meaning 'neck protection'. The name came to denote a long coat of mail protecting the body, without implying that every such garment included a neck covering.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 hauberk 是不可再作实用拆分的借词，复数为 hauberks。历史上可联系日耳曼语 hals-（颈部）与表示保护的 berg-；相关词 haubergeon（较短的锁子甲衣）来自古法语中的指小形式，并非现代英语给 hauberk 直接添加后缀形成。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hauberk is a borrowed base with the plural hauberks and no useful productive internal division. Historically, it connects Germanic hals-, 'neck', with berg-, expressing protection; the related word haubergeon, a shorter mail garment, comes from an Old French diminutive rather than a suffix added productively to hauberk in modern English.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mail shirt（锁子甲衣）是较宽泛的名称，不限定长度；coat of mail（锁子甲衣）是接近的描述性说法；haubergeon（短锁子甲衣）通常强调较短的款式，但历史用语并不始终严格区分。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mail shirt is a broader term that does not specify length; coat of mail is a close descriptive equivalent; haubergeon usually denotes a shorter garment, although historical usage does not always maintain a strict distinction.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 历史核心是“颈部＋保护”：想象一件由金属环连成的长甲衣。
mnemonic_anchor.en: The historical image is 'neck + protection': picture a long protective coat made of linked metal rings.

meaning: 肝毒性；对肝脏造成毒性损伤的性质
aliases: 对肝脏造成毒性损伤的性质
forms: 通常作不可数名词；医学中区分类型时可见 hepatotoxicities。
family: hepatotoxic 有肝毒性的；toxicity 毒性。

morphology.text: hepato-（肝）+ toxic（有毒的）+ -ity（性质）→ hepatotoxicity（肝毒性）；toxic 接 -ity 时变为 toxicity。

etymology.text: 现代医学英语用希腊语 hēpar 的词干 hepat-（肝）与 toxic、名词后缀 -ity 组合造词；把它和“肝受到毒性伤害”的画面相连。

usage_note: 用于医学和药物研究；本课取药物等物质损伤肝脏的性质。单凭这个词不能判断具体病因或严重程度。

senses.english_definition: Hepatotoxicity is damage to the liver that occurs when a drug or another substance has a harmful effect on it.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代医学构词：hepato- 源于希腊语 hēpar 的词干 hepat-，意为“肝”，与 toxic 和名词后缀 -ity 组合。词义既指损伤肝脏的毒性性质，也指这种毒性造成的实际肝损伤。[参见 LiverTox 术语表](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK548773/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK548773.pdf)。
etymology_story.en: This modern medical formation combines hepato-, from the stem hepat- of Greek hēpar, meaning 'liver', with toxic and the noun suffix -ity. It denotes both a liver-damaging property and the resulting toxic liver injury; see the [LiverTox glossary](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK548773/pdf/Bookshelf_NBK548773.pdf).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：hepato-（肝）+ toxic（有毒的）+ -ity（性质或状态）→ hepatotoxicity；也可分析为 hepatotoxic + -ity。核心词族：hepatotoxic（有肝毒性的）、hepatotoxicity（肝毒性）、hepatotoxin（肝毒素，复数 hepatotoxins）；相关基础词族有 toxic（有毒的）、toxicity（毒性）、toxin（毒素）。hepatotoxicity 通常不可数。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: hepato- ('liver') + toxic + -ity ('quality or condition'), or hepatotoxic + -ity. The core family comprises hepatotoxic, hepatotoxicity, and hepatotoxin, plural hepatotoxins; the related base family includes toxic, toxicity, and toxin. Hepatotoxicity is normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: liver toxicity（肝毒性）是较通俗的对应表达；toxic liver injury（中毒性肝损伤）强调已经发生的损伤；drug-induced liver injury（药物性肝损伤）限定致伤因素为药物，不能涵盖所有肝毒性来源。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Liver toxicity is a more transparent equivalent; toxic liver injury emphasizes actual damage; drug-induced liver injury specifically identifies medication as the cause and does not cover every source of hepatotoxicity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hepato- 是“肝”，toxicity 是“毒性”：把毒性的靶点锁定在肝脏。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hepato- identifies the liver; toxicity identifies the harm: toxicity with the liver as its target.

meaning: 兰巴达舞（巴西的一种双人舞）

morphology.text: 葡萄牙语来源结构：lamb-（鞭打，来自 lambar）+ -ada（动作名词后缀）→ lambada；英语中作为独立的舞种名称整体记忆。

etymology.text: 20世纪从巴西葡萄牙语借入；原意与鞭子的抽打有关，后来成为这种双人舞的名称，可用快速摆动的舞步帮助记忆。

usage_note: 本课只学舞蹈义；也可指伴奏音乐。舞种名称通常小写。

etymology_story.zh: 英语在20世纪后期从巴西葡萄牙语借入 lambada，葡萄牙语原词还可表示“鞭打、重击”，后来也用来称呼这种音乐和舞蹈。更早的词源不宜武断拆成 lambar + -ada：葡萄牙语词典还将其追溯至 lombo（腰背）加 -ada 的变体。[参见 Michaelis 词典](https://michaelis.uol.com.br/palavra/dNvx4/lambada/)。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed lambada from Brazilian Portuguese in the late twentieth century; the Portuguese word also means a lash or forceful blow and came to name the music and dance. Its deeper history should not be confidently reduced to lambar + -ada: the [Michaelis dictionary](https://michaelis.uol.com.br/palavra/dNvx4/lambada/) traces it to an altered formation from lombo, 'loin or back', plus -ada.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词：lambada，不宜分析为英语词根和后缀。表示一支舞或不同舞蹈实例时，复数为 lambadas；表示音乐时通常不可数。常见组合有 lambada dancer（兰巴达舞者）、lambada dancing（跳兰巴达舞）和 lambada music（兰巴达舞曲），没有常用的英语派生形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, lambada is an unanalyzed loanword rather than an English root-and-suffix formation. Its countable plural is lambadas when individual dances are meant; the music sense is normally uncountable. Common combinations include lambada dancer, lambada dancing, and lambada music; there are no common derived English adjectives or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格同义词。Brazilian partner dance（巴西双人舞）是上位描述；salsa（萨尔萨舞）和 samba（桑巴舞）是相关但不同的舞种，不能替换 lambada。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Brazilian partner dance is a broader description; salsa and samba name related but distinct dances and cannot replace lambada.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把“鞭梢摆动”联想到舞伴同步摆胯；这是记忆画面，不是进一步的词源结论。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture the swinging tip of a whip, then the partners' synchronized hips; this is a memory image, not a further etymological claim.

morphology.text: lev（单数词干）+ -a（原语言复数词尾）→ leva（复数）；这是借入英语的复数形式，不是英语动词变化。

etymology.text: 来自保加利亚语货币名称 lev 的复数；lev 的字面意思是“狮子”。可把钞票上的货币名称与狮子形象联系起来。

usage_note: 主要用于金额、历史价格和货币叙述；如 ten leva。本课解释词义，不说明该货币目前的流通情况。

etymology_story.zh: leva 是从保加利亚语借入的 lev 的复数形式，lev 的字面意思是“狮子”。保加利亚于2026年1月采用欧元，列弗与欧元并行流通一个月，欧元自2月1日起成为唯一法定货币。[词源见 Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/leva)，[货币变更见保加利亚国家银行](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/PressOffice/POPressReleases/POPRDate/PR_20260216_EN)。
etymology_story.en: Leva is the borrowed Bulgarian plural of lev, whose literal meaning is 'lion'. Bulgaria adopted the euro in January 2026, with a month of parallel cash circulation before the euro became its sole legal tender on 1 February; see [Collins for the etymology](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/leva) and the [Bulgarian National Bank for the currency change](https://www.bnb.bg/AboutUs/PressOffice/POPressReleases/POPRDate/PR_20260216_EN).

morphology_enriched.zh: 借入形式可分析为 lev（词干）+ -a（保加利亚语计数形式词尾），英语通常将 leva 作为 lev 的复数使用；它不是英语动词变化，也不再加 -s。词形配对：lev（单数）—leva（复数）；英语也可见规则复数 levs。没有常用的派生形容词或副词。
morphology_enriched.en: The borrowed form can be analyzed as lev plus the Bulgarian count-form ending -a; English conventionally treats leva as the plural of lev. It is not an English verb form and does not take an additional -s. The basic pair is lev–leva; the regular English plural levs also occurs. There are no common derived adjectives or adverbs.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Bulgarian levs（保加利亚列弗）指同样的货币单位，采用英语规则复数；BGN 是该货币的国际代码，属于符号性对应；stotinki（斯托廷基）是其辅币单位，100 stotinki 才等于一列弗。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bulgarian levs denotes the same units using the regular English plural; BGN is the currency's international code rather than an ordinary lexical synonym; stotinki are the smaller units, with one hundred making one lev.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: lev 是一只“狮子”，leva 是数只“狮子”：用狮子形象记住货币名称，用 -a 记住复数。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think of lev as one 'lion' and leva as several: the lion recalls the name, and -a recalls the plural.

etymology_story.zh: 表示“跳”的 loup 属于苏格兰语及相关方言词汇，可追溯至中古英语和古诺尔斯语 hlaupa（跑、跳），与英语 leap 有历史亲缘关系。表示海鲈的 loup 是另一个来源不同的词，来自法语 loup de mer，字面义为“海狼”。[参见苏格兰语词典](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/lowp)及 [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/loup)。
etymology_story.en: The Scots and dialect word meaning 'jump' goes back through Middle English to Old Norse hlaupa, 'run or leap', and is historically related to English leap. The fish name is a separate borrowing from French loup de mer, literally 'sea wolf'; see the [Dictionaries of the Scots Language](https://www.dsl.ac.uk/entry/snd/lowp) and [Collins](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/loup).

morphology_enriched.zh: “跳”义的 loup 是不可再分的词基，兼作动词和名词；规则形式有 loups、louped、louping，名词复数为 loups，另有方言异形 lowp 及地区性不规则变化。louping 既可作现在分词，也可作动名词，不能一概把 -ing 当作派生名词后缀。海鲈义是独立的法语借词，loup de mer 是完整短语；两种读音来自不同词源，并非单纯的词性变音。
morphology_enriched.en: The 'jump' word is an unanalyzed base used as both verb and noun. Regular forms include loups, louped, and louping, with noun plural loups; lowp and regional irregular forms also occur. Louping can be a present participle or a gerund, so -ing is not invariably a noun-forming suffix. The fish sense is a separate French loan, also appearing in loup de mer; the pronunciation difference reflects separate origins rather than a simple change of part of speech.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 跳跃义：jump（跳）最通用；leap（跃）常突出较大的幅度；bound（蹦跃）常突出有力或连续的动作，loup 则带明显地域色彩。鱼类义：European sea bass（欧洲海鲈）是明确名称，sea bass（海鲈）范围可能更广，loup de mer 是相关法语名称。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For movement, jump is the most general term, leap often suggests greater distance, and bound often suggests forceful or repeated movement; loup carries a strong regional association. For the fish, European sea bass is precise, sea bass can be broader, and loup de mer is the associated French name.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “跳”义把 loup 与近义的 leap 连在一起；菜单上的 loup /luː/ 则另记为法语“海狼”所指的海鲈。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the jumping loup with its relative leap; keep menu loup /luː/ separate as the sea bass called a 'sea wolf' in French.

morphology.text: palyn-（与花粉、细粉有关的词干）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -logy（研究）→ palynology（孢粉学）。

etymology.text: 20世纪英语科学造词，取材于希腊语 palynein（撒散）及 palē（细粉）。想象细小花粉像粉末一样撒开，再用显微镜研究。

usage_note: 包括现代或化石花粉、孢子的研究；不仅研究鲜花，也用于重建古环境。

senses.meaning_zh: 孢粉学；研究现代及化石花粉、孢子和相关有机壁微体的学科
senses.meaning_en: The study of living and fossil pollen, spores, and related microscopic organic-walled remains.
senses.english_definition: Palynology is the scientific study of pollen, spores, and similar microscopic remains, often to learn about past environments or identify where material came from.
senses.collocation_en: forensic palynology; Quaternary palynology
senses.collocation_zh: 法医孢粉学；第四纪孢粉学
senses.sentence_en: She used palynology to reconstruct changes in the region's vegetation.
senses.sentence_zh: 她利用孢粉学重建了该地区植被的变化过程。

etymology_story.zh: palynology 由英国学者 H. A. Hyde 和 D. A. Williams 于1944年提出，以希腊语 palynein（撒散）及相关的 palē（细粉、尘土）为词源材料，加上 -logy（研究）。这个名称强调花粉和孢子及其传播，学科后来也涵盖其他有机壁微体。[参见该学科命名史研究](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01916122.2017.1393020)。
etymology_story.en: H. A. Hyde and D. A. Williams proposed palynology in 1944, drawing on Greek palynein, 'scatter', and the related palē, 'fine meal or dust', together with -logy, 'study'. The name emphasized pollen, spores, and their dispersal, while the discipline also came to encompass other organic-walled microscopic remains; see this [study of the discipline's naming](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01916122.2017.1393020).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代分析：palyn-（孢粉相关词干）+ -o-（连接元音）+ -logy（研究、学科）。核心派生词：palynologist（孢粉学家）、palynological / palynologic（孢粉学的）、palynologically（从孢粉学角度）；相关构词有 palynomorph（孢粉型有机壁微体）和 palynofacies（孢粉相）。常见分支名称包括 palaeopalynology / paleopalynology（古孢粉学）、aeropalynology（空气孢粉学）和 archaeopalynology（考古孢粉学）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern analysis: palyn- (the pollen-and-spore stem) + linking -o- + -logy ('study'). Core derivatives are palynologist, palynological or palynologic, and palynologically. Related formations include palynomorph, an organic-walled microscopic body studied in palynology, and palynofacies, an assemblage characterized by its organic microscopic constituents. Branch names include palaeopalynology or paleopalynology, aeropalynology, and archaeopalynology.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: pollen science（花粉科学）是较通俗但通常较窄的表达；pollen analysis（花粉分析）主要指分析方法，而非整个学科；micropalaeontology / micropaleontology（微体古生物学）研究微小化石，与孢粉学部分重叠，但不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Pollen science is a more transparent but usually narrower expression; pollen analysis primarily names an analytical practice rather than the whole discipline; micropalaeontology or micropaleontology studies microscopic fossils and overlaps with palynology without being interchangeable with it.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “撒开的细粉”留下花粉和孢子；-logy 把这些微小线索变成一门学科。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Imagine scattered dust carrying pollen and spores; -logy turns those tiny clues into a field of study.

etymology_story.zh: prograde 是以拉丁语 pro-（向前）和表示“步、行进”的词干成分构成的学术词，构形受到 retrograde（逆行的）的影响。“向前运行”的概念后来也用于地质学中的前积和变质级升高。
etymology_story.en: Prograde is a learned formation combining Latin pro-, meaning “forward,” with a stem associated with stepping or going, influenced by retrograde. The idea of forward movement also developed technical applications in sedimentary advance and increasing metamorphic grade.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词可分析为 pro-（向前）+ -grade（表示行进的黏着成分，并非“等级”这一独立名词的直接用法）。形容词可零派生为副词，动词义则表示向前发展；主要词族包括 progrades、prograded、prograding，以及 progradation（前积作用）、progradational（前积的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern structure is pro- “forward” + -grade, a bound element referring to movement rather than a direct use of the independent noun grade. The adjective also functions as an adverb, while the verb expresses forward development; the principal family includes progrades, prograded, prograding, progradation, and progradational.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: direct 在天文学中可表示“顺行的”；progradational 专指沉积地质中的“前积的”；progressive 泛指逐步发展的，通常不能替代精确的天文学或变质地质学术语 prograde。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Direct can mean prograde in astronomy; progradational specifically concerns sedimentary advance; progressive describes gradual development generally and usually cannot replace prograde in precise astronomical or metamorphic terminology.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: pro- 向前 + -grade 行进：轨道顺着走，沉积向前长，变质向高级发展。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Pro- points forward: an orbit goes forward, sediment builds forward, and metamorphism advances to a higher grade.

senses.meaning_zh: 茅膏菜；一种用叶片上的黏性腺毛捕虫的食虫植物
senses.meaning_en: A carnivorous plant of the genus Drosera that catches insects with sticky hairs on its leaves.

etymology_story.zh: sundew 由 sun（太阳）和 dew（露水）组成，英语中至少在16世纪已有记录。名称指叶片上像阳光下露珠一样闪亮的黏液滴，这些液滴实际上用于捕捉昆虫。
etymology_story.en: Sundew combines sun and dew and is recorded in English from at least the sixteenth century. Its name refers to the glistening droplets on its leaves, which resemble dew in sunlight but actually trap insects.

morphology_enriched.zh: sun（太阳）+ dew（露水）→ sundew，是名词加名词构成的复合词。复数为 sundews；常见复合表达包括 round-leaved sundew（圆叶茅膏菜）和 Cape sundew（好望角茅膏菜）；没有常用的独立动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Sun + dew → sundew is a noun–noun compound. Its plural is sundews; established compounds include round-leaved sundew and Cape sundew, and it has no common independent verb or adjective derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Drosera 是茅膏菜属的学名，强调分类归属；carnivorous plant（食虫植物）是上位概念，还包括捕蝇草等；insectivorous plant（食虫植物）强调以昆虫为捕食对象，也不限于茅膏菜。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Drosera is the scientific genus name and emphasizes classification; carnivorous plant is a broader category that also includes plants such as Venus flytraps; insectivorous plant emphasizes insect prey and likewise includes more than sundews.

etymology.text: 中古英语 teyntour 等形式很可能借自中世纪拉丁语 tentorium（张挂、绷展织物的架子），更早与拉丁语 tendere（伸展）相连。想象布被四边拉平。

senses.meaning_en: A frame or machine that holds cloth stretched to a required width during drying or finishing.

senses.meaning_zh: 【纺织】将织物上架绷展；对织物进行拉幅处理

senses.english_definition: When workers tenter cloth, they hold it stretched on a frame or machine so that it dries or finishes at the required width.

etymology_story.zh: tenter 可追溯至中古英语 tentour 等形式，通常被认为与中世纪拉丁语 tentorium（绷展用架）有关，其更深层来源是拉丁语 tendere（伸展）。绷布架上的钩子称为 tenterhooks，由布被拉紧的形象产生了 on tenterhooks（焦急不安）这一习语。
etymology_story.en: Tenter goes back to Middle English forms such as tentour and is generally connected with Medieval Latin tentorium, a stretching frame, ultimately related to Latin tendere, “to stretch.” The hooks holding the cloth gave rise to on tenterhooks, an expression comparing anxious suspense to being held under tension.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 tenter 是整体词干，其纺织义不宜拆成 tent（帐篷）+ -er。名词零派生为动词；主要形式有 tenters、tentered、tentering（拉幅处理），复合词有 tenterhook（绷布钩）、tenterhooks，以及 tenter frame（拉幅架）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tenter is a whole stem; its textile meaning should not be analysed as tent “shelter” + -er. The noun converts directly into a verb; principal forms include tenters, tentered, and tentering, with compounds such as tenterhook, tenterhooks, and tenter frame.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: stenter 是拉幅设备的另一种常见行业名称，尤其用于现代机器；stretching frame（绷展架）范围更广，不一定用于纺织；作为动词，stretch（拉伸）只说明拉展动作，不必涉及拉幅设备。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Stenter is another established industry term for tenter equipment, especially modern machinery; stretching frame is broader and need not refer to textiles; as a verb, stretch describes pulling something out without necessarily using a tenter.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“绷紧”这一动作：tenter 绷布，tenterhooks 上的布绷紧，焦急的人也紧绷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture cloth held taut on a tenter: the tension also explains the anxiety in on tenterhooks.

forms: 副词，无词形变化；另有形式 thenceforwards。

morphology.text: thence（从那时、从那里）+ forward（向前）→ thenceforward（从那时起向后延续）。

etymology.text: 中古英语时期已将 thence 与 forward 连用成词；两个部分都来自英语本土词汇。可以想成以过去某点为起点向后延伸的时间线。

usage_note: 正式或文学用语，常回指叙事中刚说过的时间；日常可用 from then on。

senses.meaning_zh: 【正式或文学用语】从那时起；此后一直
senses.meaning_en: From that time onward.
senses.english_definition: If something happens thenceforward, it happens from a particular time already mentioned and continues after that time.
senses.collocation_en: was thenceforward known as; thenceforward remained
senses.collocation_zh: 从那时起被称为；此后一直保持
senses.sentence_en: She moved to the coast in 1920 and lived there thenceforward.
senses.sentence_zh: 她于1920年迁居海边，此后一直住在那里。

etymology_story.zh: thenceforward 在中古英语时期由 thence（从那里；从那时）和 forward（向前）组合而成，两个成分都源于英语本族词汇。它把“从某一点向前”的空间意象用于时间，表示从已提到的时刻起持续下去。
etymology_story.en: Thenceforward arose in Middle English from thence, “from there or from that time,” and forward, both native English elements. It applies the spatial image of moving forward from a point to time continuing from a previously mentioned moment.

morphology_enriched.zh: thence（从那时）+ forward（向前）→ thenceforward，是副词复合词，没有常规屈折变化，也没有常用的名词、动词或形容词派生形式。相关平行构词包括 thenceforth（从那时起）和 henceforward（从现在起）。
morphology_enriched.en: Thence “from that time” + forward → thenceforward is an adverbial compound with no regular inflections or common noun, verb, or adjective derivatives. Related parallel formations include thenceforth, “from that time onward,” and henceforward, “from now onward.”

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: thenceforth 与 thenceforward 基本同义，同样偏正式或文学；thereafter 表示“在那之后”，不一定强调一直持续；henceforth 通常以说话时刻为起点，表示“从现在起”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Thenceforth is essentially synonymous and similarly formal or literary; thereafter means “after that” without necessarily emphasizing continuing duration; henceforth normally starts from the present moment and means “from now on.”

mnemonic_anchor.zh: thence 锁定“那时”，forward 把时间线向后延长：从那时起。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Thence marks “that time”; forward extends the timeline: from that time onward.

etymology_story.zh: tup 来自中古英语 tupe，意为“公羊”，更早的来源并不确定。表示公羊交配的动词由名词发展而来；顶撞和机械锤头等用法则与公羊撞击的形象相联系。
etymology_story.en: Tup comes from Middle English tupe, meaning “ram,” but its earlier origin is uncertain. The mating verb developed from the noun, while the butting and mechanical-hammer senses are associated with the image of a ram striking with its head.

morphology_enriched.zh: tup 是不可进一步作可靠现代拆分的简单词，名词与动词之间存在零派生关系。主要形式为 tups、tupped、tupping；加 -ed 或 -ing 时双写 p。tupping 也用作动作名词，常见复合表达有 tupping season（配种季）和 tupping time（配种期）。
morphology_enriched.en: Tup is a simple word with no reliable smaller modern components, and its noun and verb uses are related by conversion. Its principal forms are tups, tupped, and tupping, with p doubled before -ed and -ing. Tupping also functions as an action noun in compounds such as tupping season and tupping time.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: ram 是“公羊”的通用标准词，tup 更具英国地方及养羊行业色彩；serve 在畜牧业中可指雄性给雌性配种，适用动物不限于羊；head-butt 对应 tup 的顶撞义，不包含配种含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Ram is the general standard word for a male sheep, whereas tup has a stronger British regional and sheep-farming association; serve can describe a breeding male mating with a female across several livestock species; head-butt matches the striking sense of tup and carries no mating meaning.

etymology_story.zh: 源自中世纪拉丁语 ultramontanus，字面意为“山脉另一边的”。从阿尔卑斯山以北看，教皇所在的罗马位于山的另一侧，因此该词后来指支持罗马教皇最高权威的立场或人士。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Medieval Latin ultramontanus, meaning 'beyond the mountains.' To people north of the Alps, Rome lay across the mountains, so the word came to describe strong support for papal authority and people holding that position.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可辨识结构为 ultra-（超出、在……之外）+ montane（山地的）；montane 内含源自拉丁语 mons、词干 mont- 的“山”义成分。主要词族：ultramontanism（教皇至上主义）、ultramontanist（教皇至上主义者；教皇至上主义的）、ultramontanes（名词复数）；相关词有 montane（山地的）。
morphology_enriched.en: The recognizable structure is ultra- ('beyond') + montane ('relating to mountains'); montane contains the mountain element from Latin mons, stem mont-. Principal family members are ultramontanism, ultramontanist (noun or adjective), and the plural ultramontanes; montane is a related word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: papalist（拥护教皇权威的；拥护者）与宗教义最接近；papal（教皇的）只表示与教皇有关，不必然表示支持其最高权威；transalpine（阿尔卑斯山另一侧的）对应地理义，本身不带宗教立场。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Papalist is closest to the religious sense and can describe either a position or a supporter. Papal merely means 'relating to the pope' and does not necessarily express support for supreme papal authority. Transalpine matches the geographical sense without implying a religious position.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ultra-＝在另一边，mont-＝山：越过阿尔卑斯山望向罗马，就想到教皇权威。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ultra- means 'beyond' and mont- means 'mountain': look across the Alps toward Rome to connect the geographical meaning with papal authority.

forms: 第三人称单数 adjures；过去式、过去分词 adjured；现在分词 adjuring。
family: adjuration 郑重请求；jury 陪审团（与宣誓有历史联系）。

morphology.text: 历史结构：ad-（向、对）+ jur（宣誓）→ adjure；记成用极郑重的语气要求别人。不是 adjust 的变体。

etymology.text: 经中古英语 adjuren、古法语 ajurer 来自拉丁语 adjurare（以誓言确认）。从宣誓般郑重的要求，发展出恳切劝告的常见用法。

usage_note: 正式、较少见；常用 adjure somebody to do something。本课取恳切劝告义。

senses.meaning_zh: 郑重恳求；严肃敦促
senses.meaning_en: to urge or appeal to someone solemnly and earnestly
senses.english_definition: If you adjure someone to do something, you ask or urge them very seriously and earnestly to do it.
senses.collocation_en: adjure someone to tell the truth; solemnly adjure someone
senses.collocation_zh: 郑重要求某人说实话；郑重恳求某人

senses.sentence_zh: 她郑重劝他在作出无法挽回的决定之前重新考虑。

senses.meaning_zh: 以誓言或神圣权威责令、要求
senses.meaning_en: to charge or command someone under oath or by invoking sacred authority
senses.english_definition: If you adjure someone by something sacred, you invoke its authority to require them to speak or act.
senses.collocation_en: adjure someone by God; adjure someone under oath
senses.collocation_zh: 以上帝之名责令某人；以誓言约束某人并提出要求
senses.sentence_en: The priest adjured the witness by God to speak the truth.
senses.sentence_zh: 神父以上帝之名郑重要求证人说出真相。

etymology_story.zh: 经中古英语和古法语，源自拉丁语 adiurare，由 ad-（向、对）和 iurare（宣誓）组成。其含义从以誓言或神圣权威约束他人，扩展为以极其郑重的口吻恳求或敦促。
etymology_story.en: Through Middle English and Old French, adjure comes from Latin adiurare, formed from ad- ('to') and iurare ('to swear'). Its meaning broadened from placing someone under a solemn or sacred obligation to urging or appealing to them with great seriousness.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 adjure 是整体动词，不能视为由常用独立词自由拼成；历史结构为 ad- + jur-（宣誓）+ 动词词尾。主要词族：adjures（第三人称单数）、adjured（过去式及过去分词）、adjuring（现在分词）、adjuration（郑重恳求；以誓言提出的要求）、adjurer（郑重要求者）、adjuratory（郑重要求的）；与 adjust 无构词关系。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, adjure functions as a whole verb rather than a freely assembled combination of independent words; historically it contains ad- + jur- ('swear') + a verb ending. Principal family members are adjures, adjured, adjuring, adjuration, adjurer, and adjuratory. It is not a derivative or variant of adjust.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: implore（恳求）突出强烈情感和迫切需要；beseech（恳求）语体庄重，常带谦恭意味；enjoin（责令）突出权威性的指示。adjure 则兼有郑重要求的语气及历史上的誓言、神圣权威色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Implore emphasizes emotional urgency, while beseech is formal and often suggests humble pleading. Enjoin emphasizes an authoritative instruction. Adjure combines solemn insistence with a historical association with oaths or sacred authority.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: jur- 联想“宣誓”：像要求对方发誓一样郑重地提出要求。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect jur- with swearing an oath: to adjure is to make a request with oath-like seriousness.

pronunciation.note: 采用词典列出的英语读音。

forms: 此义通常不可数；复数 assiduities 常指殷勤关照。
family: assiduous 勤勉的；assiduously 勤勉地。

morphology.text: assidu-（与 assiduous 共用的词干，勤勉）+ -ity（性质）→ assiduity（勤勉）。

etymology.text: 源于拉丁语 assiduitas（持续在场、勤勉），与 assidere（坐在旁边、守候）相连。想成一直守在工作旁，持续认真投入。

usage_note: 正式名词，强调长期持续的认真努力；本课不教复数的殷勤关照义。

senses.meaning_zh: 勤勉；持续认真投入
senses.meaning_en: persistent care, attention, and effort
senses.english_definition: Assiduity is the quality of working at something with steady care, attention, and effort over a period of time.
senses.collocation_en: with great assiduity; remarkable assiduity
senses.collocation_zh: 极其勤勉地；非凡的勤勉
senses.sentence_en: She checked every reference with the same assiduity she brought to her research.
senses.sentence_zh: 她核查每一条参考文献时，都像做研究一样认真勤勉。

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 assiduitas，表示持续在场、专注或勤勉，与 assiduus（持续在场的）及 assidere（坐在旁边、守候）同源。“一直守在事情旁边”的形象，逐渐发展为持续认真投入的抽象含义。
etymology_story.en: Assiduity comes from Latin assiduitas, expressing constant attendance, attention, or diligence, and is related to assiduus and assidere ('to sit beside' or 'attend'). The image of remaining constantly at hand developed into the abstract meaning of sustained, careful effort.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族关系可表示为 assiduous（勤勉的）去掉 -ous，再接 -ity（性质、状态），形成 assiduity；这是词干变化，不能写成 assiduousity。主要词族：assiduous、assiduously（勤勉地）、assiduousness（勤勉）、assiduity；复数 assiduities 还可在较旧或文学用法中表示殷勤关照。
morphology_enriched.en: The modern family relationship can be represented as assiduous minus -ous plus -ity, producing assiduity through a stem change; the form is not assiduousity. Principal family members are assiduous, assiduously, assiduousness, and assiduity. The plural assiduities can also mean attentive services or courtesies in older or literary usage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: diligence（勤勉）是最通用的近义词，强调认真负责地工作；application（专心用功）突出集中精力；perseverance（坚持不懈）突出遇到困难仍继续。assiduity 尤其强调持续、细致而不间断的用心。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Diligence is the broadest equivalent and emphasizes careful, conscientious work. Application emphasizes concentrated effort, while perseverance emphasizes continuing despite difficulty. Assiduity particularly suggests sustained, close attention.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“坐在旁边守着”记：一直守着任务，认真做到底。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture someone sitting beside a task and staying with it: constant attendance becomes constant care.

morphology.text: candle（蜡烛）+ wick（芯）→ candlewick（烛芯）；两个词直接复合。

etymology.text: 英语本土复合词，12世纪以前已有记录，由 candle 和 wick 合成，直接描述蜡烛中供火焰燃烧的芯。

usage_note: 本课取蜡烛芯义；也可指一种棉绣线和相应刺绣，不在本课考查。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 candle（蜡烛）和 wick（芯）组成的英语复合词，其对应形式在古英语中已有使用。后来，制作烛芯的柔软棉纱也用于装饰性刺绣，词义因而扩展到这种纱线及带有凸起棉纱簇的织物。
etymology_story.en: Candlewick is an English compound of candle and wick, with a corresponding form already used in Old English. Soft cotton yarn used for wicks was later used in decorative embroidery, extending the word to the yarn and to fabric patterned with raised cotton tufts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构：candle（蜡烛）+ wick（芯）→ candlewick，属于名词复合词。主要词族及相关形式：candlewicks（烛芯的复数）、candlewicking（烛芯纱簇绣工艺或绣品）、candlewicked（以烛芯纱簇绣装饰的）；常见复合搭配包括 candlewick yarn（烛芯纱）和 candlewick bedspread（烛芯纱簇绒床罩），其中 candlewick 是作定语的名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: candle + wick → candlewick, a compound noun. Principal family and related forms include candlewicks, candlewicking (the embroidery technique or its work), and candlewicked (decorated with such embroidery). In compounds such as candlewick yarn and candlewick bedspread, candlewick is a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wick（芯）范围更广，也可指油灯等器具的灯芯；wicking（灯芯材料）强调制芯用的材料；chenille（雪尼尔纱或织物）也有柔软绒簇，但结构不同，不能作为烛芯纱簇绒织物的严格同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wick is broader and also applies to lamps and other devices. Wicking emphasizes the material used to make wicks. Chenille is a related textile term for soft, fuzzy yarn or fabric, but its construction differs, so it is not an exact synonym of candlewick fabric.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 蜡烛里的棉芯，变成布面上的棉纱簇：从烛芯记到簇绒织物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Follow the cotton from a candle's wick to raised tufts on cloth: one material links the candle and textile meanings.

family: chain 链条；mail 此处指环扣护甲，不是邮件。

morphology.text: chain（链）+ mail（环扣护甲）→ chainmail（锁子甲）；这里的 mail 与邮政邮件的 mail 是不同词。

etymology.text: 英语由 chain 和表示护甲的 mail 组成。护甲义 mail 经古法语来自拉丁语 macula（网眼），可想象铁环像网眼一样扣在一起。

usage_note: 本课指金属环相扣的护甲；可写 chain mail。本课不把连锁转发信件作为同义用法。

senses.meaning_zh: 锁子甲；由相互扣连的金属环制成的护甲
senses.meaning_en: armour made of interlinked metal rings
senses.english_definition: Chainmail is armour made from many small metal rings linked together to form a flexible protective covering.

etymology_story.zh: 由 chain（链）和表示环甲的 mail 组成；这里的 mail 经古法语来自拉丁语 macula，后者有“网眼”等含义。金属环像网眼一样彼此扣连，因此形成了这种护甲的名称；该 mail 与“邮件”的 mail 来源不同。
etymology_story.en: Chainmail combines chain with mail meaning armour; this mail came through Old French from Latin macula, which could mean a mesh in a net. The linked rings resemble a mesh, and this armour word has a different origin from mail meaning letters or postal deliveries.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代结构：chain（链）+ mail（环甲）→ chainmail，属于复合名词，通常作不可数名词。拼写变体有 chain mail 和 chain-mail；相关形式包括 mail（环甲）、mailed（穿环甲的）及 chainmail-clad（身穿锁子甲的），而 chainmail shirt 中的 chainmail 是作定语的名词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: chain + mail ('armour') → chainmail, a compound noun normally used as an uncountable noun. Spelling variants are chain mail and chain-mail. Related forms include mail ('armour'), mailed ('wearing mail'), and chainmail-clad; in chainmail shirt, chainmail is a noun used attributively.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mail（环甲）在护甲语境中是最接近的同义词；armour（护甲）是上位词，还包括板甲等其他形式；hauberk（长身环甲衣）指一种具体的环甲衣物，不能泛指所有锁子甲。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mail is the closest synonym in an armour context. Armour is the broader category and includes other forms of protection, such as plate armour. A hauberk is a particular long mail garment, rather than a general term for all chainmail.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把小铁环像链条一样扣成衣服，就是 chainmail；这里的 mail 表示护甲。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture small metal rings chained together into a protective shirt: chain + armour-mail gives chainmail.

senses.meaning_zh: 男美发师；男发型师（用语较正式或带法式色彩）
senses.meaning_en: A male hairdresser, especially one described in a formal or French-influenced style.
senses.english_definition: A coiffeur is a man whose job is to cut, arrange, and style people's hair.
senses.chinese_definition: coiffeur 指以剪发、梳理头发和设计发型为职业的男性。
senses.collocation_en: a fashionable coiffeur; a Parisian coiffeur

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语借入 coiffeur；法语中它由 coiffer（梳理头发、做发型）加表示从业者的 -eur 构成。coiffer 与 coiffe（头巾、头饰）同源，词义由头部的覆盖和装饰发展到整理头发。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed coiffeur from French, where coiffer, meaning to arrange or dress the hair, combines with the agent suffix -eur. Coiffer belongs to the family of coiffe, a head covering, connecting the dressing of the head with hairstyling.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中主要作为完整的法语借词使用，不宜把 coiff- 当作能自由构词的英语词根；法语内部结构为 coiff- + -eur（从业者）。主要词族及相关形式：coiffeurs（复数）、coiffeuse（女美发师）、coiffure（发型）、coif（头巾；梳理头发）、coiffed/coifed（梳理过的）、coiffing/coifing（梳理头发）、coiffured（做了发型的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, coiffeur is primarily a whole French loanword; coiff- is not a freely productive English root. Its French structure is coiff- + -eur, an agent suffix. Principal family members and related forms include coiffeurs, coiffeuse, coiffure, coif, coiffed/coifed, coiffing/coifing, and coiffured.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hairdresser（美发师）是最中性的通用词；hairstylist（发型师）突出发型设计；barber（理发师）通常主要为男性剪发和修面。coiffeur 传统上指男性美发师，并带较正式或法式的语感。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hairdresser is the neutral general term; hairstylist emphasizes styling and design; barber usually suggests men's haircuts and shaving. Coiffeur traditionally denotes a male hairdresser and has a more formal or French-associated tone.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: coiffe（头饰）→ coiffer（整理头发）→ coiffeur（给人做发型的人）。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Head covering → dressing the hair → the person who styles it.

senses.meaning_zh: 戏服制作师或供应商；戏服制作、出售或出租公司
senses.meaning_en: A person or business that makes or supplies costumes, especially for performances.
senses.english_definition: A costumier is a person or company that makes or supplies clothes for actors or for people attending events in costume.
senses.chinese_definition: costumier 指为演员或参加化装活动的人制作、供应服装的个人或公司。
